title: Alvin Kamara will soon become the sixth NFL player with 5,000 yards rushing and receiving
summary: Kamara has 7,324 rushing yards and 4,995 receiving yards in his NFL career.
full_text: Few players in NFL history have been a threat to make plays both running and receiving like Saints running back Alvin Kamara. Kamara, who is listed as questionable for Sunday with a back injury, has 7,324 rushing yards and 4,995 receiving yards in his NFL career, which means he's just five receiving yards short of reaching 5,000 yards in both categories. If Kamara does it, he'll be only the sixth player in NFL history with 5,000 yards both rushing and receiving. The previous five are: Marshall Faulk: 12,279 rushing, 6,875 receiving. Marcus Allen: 12,243 rushing; 5,411 receiving. Tiki Barber: 10,449 rushing; 5,183 receiving. Christian McCaffrey: 7,807 rushing; 5,512 receiving. Lenny Moore: 5,174 rushing; 6,039 receiving. The 31-year-old Kamara is not the player he once was. So far this season he has just 25 carries for 74 yards (2.96 yards per carry) and 11 receptions for 47 yards (4.27 yards per catch). Kamara may be nearing the end, but he's poised to end up with an impressive statistical achievement.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Aaron Rodgers set to move ahead of Peyton Manning on the all-time touchdown pass list
summary: With his next touchdown pass, Aaron Rodgers will have more than Peyton Manning, counting the playoffs.
full_text: Aaron Rodgers is poised to take sole possession of third place on the NFL's all-time passing touchdown list. If Rodgers throws a touchdown pass on Sunday against the Colts, it will be the 580th of his NFL career, counting the playoffs. Currently, Rodgers and Peyton Manning are tied for third with 579 career touchdowns. Manning threw 539 touchdowns in the regular season and 40 in the playoffs. Rodgers has thrown 534 in the regular season and 45 in the playoffs. Manning threw 428 touchdown passes with the Colts and 151 with the Broncos. Rodgers threw 520 with the Packers and 28 with the Jets and has now thrown 31 with the Steelers. Rodgers, who has said this is his last NFL season, will probably not catch Drew Brees, who is No. 2 all time with 608 touchdown passes. Rodgers will definitely not catch Tom Brady, who is No. 1 all time with 737 touchdown passes.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Multiple playoff teams have never started 0-5
summary: One of the five 0-4 teams entering Week 5 (the Buccaneers) has finally gotten its first win of 2026.
full_text: One of the five 0-4 teams entering Week 5 (the Buccaneers) has finally gotten its first win of 2026. Four winless teams remain. Two of them — the Chargers and Texans — made the playoffs last year. Via NBC Sports research, the last time two playoff teams started the next year 0-4 happened in 1999. That year, both Super Bowl teams from the prior season (the Broncos and Falcons) got off to an 0-4 start. Also, no pair of playoff teams has started 0-5 in the next season. Ever. No playoff team has started 0-5 the next year since the 2017 Giants. The most teams ever to start the year 0-4 is five. The 2026 quintet matches five 0-4 teams in 2009, 1996, 1991, 1979, and 1962. With the 0-4 Texans playing the 0-4 Titans, the most possible 0-5 teams this year will be three: the Chargers, the Dolphins, and the loser of Texans-Titans.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joey Porter Jr.'s illness invites speculation that it was contract related (even if it wasn't)
summary: Last night's Buccaneers-Cowboys game was preceded by the unexpected news that cornerback Joey Porter Jr. would miss the contest due to a sudden illness.
full_text: '' Last night's Buccaneers-Cowboys game was preceded by the unexpected news that cornerback Joey Porter Jr. would miss the contest due to a sudden illness. In light of a back injury that prompted him to decline to play for the Steelers until he was traded — and given that the back injury instantly disappeared once he was traded to the Cowboys — some connected the dots from the illness to the lack of a long-term deal. As noted by Matt Yoder of Awful Announcing , Prime Video analyst Richard Sherman went there during Thursday night's pregame show. “I think maybe if they would have gave him a new contract, maybe he would have been a little healthier today ,” Sherman said. But there's not much for Porter to gain by declining to play. He already got what he wanted from the Steelers — a trade out of Pittsburgh. If he continues to find phony excuses to not play, he won't help his long-term interests. At this point, his only play seems to be playing as well as he can in the hopes of getting a long-term deal, the franchise tag, or a ticket to the open market. That said, it's clear that the Cowboys are keeping their options open as to the possibility of tagging Porter, the same way they tagged receiver George Pickens after his first year with the team. "We're working under an existing contract with an extended contract," Jones said last Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. "Think about it. Think about it hard. Let's get in here, and let's make each other feel a little better about where we are. Not a little better; in these guys' case, it's a monster amount in their lives, a contract at this level. "But by the same token, there's two to tango here. There's the team and I are being comparable with making that kind of commitment. What you're seeing in both those cases is working through a reasonable way to advance the ball, advance the ball being, 'Get up, be an outstanding player as well as having an outstanding contract.' That's what you're seeing, and I'm satisfied that we were able to do this with George. A lot of credit goes to everybody involved, particularly [coach] Brian Schottenheimer. Brian was very helpful, and they have a great relationship. "And so, that's the way to work through this problem. This thing is not a perfect thing in our agreement, in our overall, if I dare say, labor agreement, and it gives a lot of leverage to both parties. So when you see it work out the way it is with George, you've got to say, 'Look, that's people working together.'" The Cowboys haven't worked out anything with Pickens. Instead, they persuaded him to play under the franchise tag for $27.298 million in 2026, even though the market is now north of $42 million. Jones's explanation suggests that the door is wide open to tag Porter, if a long-term deal can't be negotiated. If Porter's sudden illness was a ruse, it won't be the only time he doesn't play. He'll keep finding plausible ways to refuse to play, with the goal of pressuring the Cowboys into giving him the contract he didn't get from the Steelers. And that he still hasn't gotten from the Cowboys.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chiefs, Vikings are first pair of non-playoff teams since 2013 to start 4-0
summary: The NFL has only three 4-0 teams after four weeks.
full_text: The NFL has only three 4-0 teams after four weeks. Two of them — the Chiefs and Vikings — didn't make it to the playoffs in 2025. Via NBC Sports research, it's the first time since 2013 that multiple teams that failed to make the playoffs in the prior season started with 4-0 records. That year, the Chiefs and Saints started 4-0. (In 2012, the Chiefs were 2-14, and the Saints went 7-9.) The 2025 Chiefs went 6-11 after three straight Super Bowl appearances. The 2025 Vikings finished 9-8, with five straight wins. Minnesota has the current longest active winning streak in the NFL, with nine in a row. They'll go for 10 in a row, tying the second-longest winning streak in franchise history, on Sunday at New Orleans. The 1975 Vikings started 10-0. The 1969 Vikings lost their first and last games of the regular season — and won all 12 in a row in between.
author: Mike Florio

title: Injuries to LT Tyler Guyton, WR CeeDee Lamb are not serious
summary: The X-rays on Cowboys left tackle Tyler Guyton's back were negative, coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday.
full_text: ' The X-rays on Cowboys left tackle Tyler Guyton's back were negative, coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday. Guyton sat out the team's final offensive series with his injury. Broderick Jones replaced him. Wide receiver CeeDee Lamb also received good news as his quad injury is only a bruise. He was in and out of the game on the final drive. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is better after missing the 24-16 loss to the Buccaneers with an illness. He arrived at the game sick, and the Cowboys made him inactive. Safety Alijah Clark is the only concerning injury out of the game, and Schottenheimer called Clark day-to-day. The Cowboys have safeties P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson on injured reserve. The Cowboys don't play again until Oct. 18.
author: Charean Williams

title: Broncos OC Davis Webb: "Not ideal" to lose playcalling role, excited to see how we respond
summary: Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb's job description underwent a dramatic change this week.
full_text: ' Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb's job description underwent a dramatic change this week. Webb took over as the team's offensive playcaller during the offseason, but head coach Sean Payton took that role back after the unit's sluggish play through the first four weeks of the season. During a Friday press conference, Webb was asked if he thinks four games was long enough to make a decision about sticking with the status quo. "Luckily that's not my job , that's [Payton's] job," Webb said, via Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post . "Obviously I think he answered that. I think the world of him and how we've gone about it. Really the ownership to our players. It's not ideal, but in the same breath, it’s exciting because we're 2-2 in the first four games. Our first four opponents were a combined 13-3 to start the season. Welcome to the league.” Webb said that he knows Payton is "itching" to call plays again and said he's "excited to see how our team responds" to the shift even though he's disappointed by how things have played out to this point. "Any time it happens in any aspect of your life job-wise it is a little bit, but, in the same breath, that's the NFL. You get going," Webb said. "Been a backup QB, been up and down before, that's kind of how it goes." Webb noted that he still has a big hand in the weekly operations and in discussions about the game plan, but calling plays was a significant shift in his responsibilities. It's hard to put any positive spin on it from an individual point of view, but improved play for the Broncos is Payton's chief goal.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dolphins claim RB Kaytron Allen off waivers
summary: The Dolphins have added a running back.
full_text: The Dolphins have added a running back. Miami has claimed Kaytron Allen off of waivers after Washington let him go earlier this week, the team announced on Friday. A sixth-round pick in this year’s draft, Allen had appeared in all four games for Washington, taking 12 carries for 41 yards. He also appeared on special teams, taking 29 snaps on the unit. The Dolphins had a need for more depth at running back, particularly after De’Von Achane suffered a torn ACL. Jaylen Wright started for the Dolphins at running back last week, though Ollie Gordon was the leading rusher with 100 yards on nine carries.

title: 49ers release DL Ogbo Okoronkwo
summary: The 49ers released defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo on Friday, the team announced.
full_text: ' The 49ers released defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo on Friday, the team announced. Okoronkwo played four games this season, with one start, and has two tackles and a sack. He entered the NFL as a fifth-round pick of the Rams in 2018. Okoronkwo spent four seasons with the Rams (2018-21), one with the Texans (2022), two with the Browns (2023-24) and one with the Eagles (2025). Okoronkwo, 31, has registered 134 tackles, 18 sacks, 41 quarterback hits, four passes defensed and four forced fumbles in his career.

title: Report: Broncos to put Pat Bryant on injured reserve
summary: Broncos head coach Sean Payton said on Wednesday that he didn't think wide receiver Pat Bryant would be placed on injured reserve, but it appears something has changed about Denver's view of the wideout's ankle injury.
full_text: ' Broncos head coach Sean Payton said on Wednesday that he didn’t think wide receiver Pat Bryant would be placed on injured reserve, but it appears something has changed about Denver's view of the wideout's ankle injury. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports on Friday that the team will place Bryant on injured reserve. He was injured in last Sunday's loss to the 49ers. Bryant will miss at least the next four games. The Broncos will visit the Chargers on Sunday and then host the Seahawks on Thursday night in Week 6. A trip to Arizona and a visit from the Chiefs make up the rest of that quartet. Bryant has nine catches for 133 yards and a touchdown so far this season.

title: Falcons-Saints on Monday night draws 11.9 million viewers
summary: The Week 3 Monday night game between the Eagles and Bears racked up 22.6 million viewers on the Disney family of networks.
full_text: The Week 3 Monday night game between the Eagles and Bears racked up 22.6 million viewers on the Disney family of networks. The Week 4 Monday night game between the Falcons and Saints did almost half that number. Via ESPN, the latest Monday night game on ESPN, ESPN2, and ESPN Deportes attracted a total average audience of 11.9 million. It's a surprising drop in audience, especially in light of the significance of the game. It happened 20 years after the return of the Saints to the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina, with a 23-3 win over Atlanta sparked by a blocked punt by Steve Gleason that is immortalized in a statue outside the stadium. There was extensive focus, and rightfully so, on the relevance of the 2026 rematch. Ultimately, the game has to hold the audience. The Falcons led 24-7 at the half, en route to a 45-24 win. By then, it was easy for many to check out. Also, the fact that (unlock most Monday night games) the game wasn't simulcast on ABC ate into the audience. Through the first three weeks, Monday Night Football had averaged 21.8 million viewers. The Week 4 game pulls the average down to 19.325 million. This week's game should make up for it — the Bills visit the Rams in what could be a shootout that goes down to the wire.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones "Extraordinarily, extraordinarily disappointed" by Cowboys' loss to Buccaneers
summary: Cowboys owner and General Manager Jerry Jones was stunned to see his team get upset by the previously winless Buccaneers on Thursday night.
full_text: ' Cowboys owner and General Manager Jerry Jones was stunned to see his team get upset by the previously winless Buccaneers on Thursday night. Jones said he thought his lines would be more physical on both sides of the ball, and that his defense would play better against Buccaneers undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who was making his second start in place of the injured Baker Mayfield. "Extraordinarily, extraordinarily disappointed," Jones said, via the team's website. "You really do need to get it done when it's there to take. They basically were very physical. I thought both their fronts, was really surprised at how well they ran the ball, how they ran it between the tackles. That was surprising . We thought if they were going to run it, they'd do it outside, and thought we'd put it on the quarterback's shoulders. Their staff, their quarterback, all their players got a great victory here tonight, and it was a tough loss for us." Jones said it was frustrating because he thought his team had a chance to take a step forward, and instead it took a step backward. "Boy, I've been so disappointed before with losses, but this was disappointing," Jones said. "And I'm disappointed because I see potential growth here. And we need to have good experiences on an individual basis as well as a team. And this was not a good experience out here." Up next for the 2-3 Cowboys are back-to-back road games at Green Bay and Philadelphia, in which Jones hopes not to witness any more extraordinary disappointments.
author: Michael David Smith

title: J.K. Dobbins is in a "dark spot" after rough start to 2026
summary: Broncos running back J.K.
full_text: ' Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins had high hopes for his second season with the Broncos. Through four games, he has yet to perform at the level he'd anticipated. “Right now, it’s a dark spot ,” Dobbins said Thursday, via Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post . “That’s part of being in the NFL, though. I’m going to find a way to play to the standard that I play at.” Dobbins has only 161 rushing yards through four games, on 46 attempts. He's averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per carry. (His career average remains 5.1 yards per attempt.) He suffered a soft-tissue injury during training camp, but he won't blame his production to date on that or any other injury. “I’m healthy,” Dobbins said. “I’m out there playing. Any time — whether it’s fully healthy, not healthy, 75 percent, 60, 80, 90, 100, if I’m out there, I’ve got to play good, you know what I mean? No matter what’s going on, if I’m going out there, that means I think I can make plays. . . . It don’t matter. . . . I’ve got to make my plays and I’ve got to be me.” Against the 49ers on Sunday, Dobbins was on the field for only 21 snaps; RJ Harvey took 29 reps. He was asked whether he was frustrated early in the game; he didn't get a carry until the second quarter. “I just love the game," Dobbins said. "I’m a passionate guy. Whatever you saw, it was just me wanting to win the game. I just want to win no matter what, you know? It could be me getting two carries in two minutes of playing time. As long as we win the game, I’m fine. It has nothing to do with me being a passionate guy and wanting to win the game.” The Broncos haven't won as many as they'd hoped in the early going; after a 14-3 season in 2025, they're 2-2. The shift back to Sean Payton as the play-caller could unlock the offense against the Chargers on Sunday — and it possibly will better unleash Dobbins.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chargers placing Rashawn Slater on IR after ankle procedure
summary: One of the Chargers' offensive tackles is now on the mend.
full_text: One of the Chargers' offensive tackles is now on the mend. Los Angeles announced on Friday that left tackle Rashawn Slater underwent successful ankle surgery on Friday and will be placed on injured reserve. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network notes it was a tightrope procedure, which should accelerate Slater's return from a high-ankle sprain. Slater, the No. 13 overall pick of the 2021 draft, missed all of last season due to a torn patellar tendon suffered in training camp. This is now the third season significantly impacted by injury for Slater, who also missed much of the 2022 season with a torn biceps.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Eagles to release Andy Dalton
summary: There have been some major changes to the Eagles roster this week and another tweak is reportedly coming.
full_text: ''' There have been some major changes to the Eagles roster this week and another tweak is reportedly coming. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that the Eagles will release quarterback Andy Dalton. Right tackle Lane Johnson retired earlier this week and the Eagles traded guard/center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens on Wednesday. Tanner McKee supplanted Dalton as the Eagles' No. 2 quarterback last weekend and the Eagles also have rookie Cole Payton on the 53-man roster. With a slew of injuries to go with the other changes, the Eagles needed to free up a roster spot ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London. Dalton was traded to the Eagles by the Panthers in March. His only pass attempt as an Eagle came in Week 3 and he threw an interception in the end zone on that throw.

title: Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison questionable for Sunday vs. Saints
summary: The Vikings may or may not have their top two receivers when they play the Saints on Sunday.

title: Falcons vs. Ravens: How to watch Bijan Robinson vs. Derrick Henry on 'SNF'
summary: Tyler Huntley steps in for an injured Lamar Jackson as Baltimore faces a surging Atlanta offense led by Bijan Robinson
full_text:
Two teams, both on two-game winning streaks, meet in prime time this Sunday night, as the Atlanta Falcons host the Baltimore Ravens . The Falcons went from laughing stock to potential NFC South favorite over two weeks, as Michael Penix Jr . has brought some stability to Kevin Stefanski's offense. As for the Ravens, they are tied with the Cleveland Browns for the AFC North lead at 3-1, but won't have their two-time NFL MVP under center this week.
Baltimore ruled star quarterback Lamar Jackson out for this matchup due to the ankle injury suffered during last Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans . He's not the only notable Raven ruled out, as Baltimore also announced pass rusher Trey Hendrickson and new center Cam Jurgens would not be suiting up as well. It will be Tyler Huntley at quarterback for the Ravens, who won both of his starts for Baltimore last year.
As for the Falcons, this is a fun homecoming of sorts. They left Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sept. 20 as a team with little hope, having just lost by 31 points to the Carolina Panthers . Now, they return as arguably the hottest team in the NFL with a new quarterback and an Offensive Player of the Year favorite at running back.
Let's break down this exciting, primetime interconference matchup, but first, here's how you can watch:
Historical data courtesy of CBS Sports Research
Date: Sunday, Oct. 11 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Mercedes-Benz Stadium (Atlanta, Georgia) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Falcons -3.5, O/U 43.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook)
Who is "Snoop" Huntley?: Huntley is getting the start on Sunday night, and he's in his sixth season with the Ravens. "Snoop" famously made the Pro Bowl as an alternate in 2022 after helping the Ravens finish with a 10-7 record and a wild-card berth. Huntley is 7-9 in his career as a starter, and has scored 14 total touchdowns compared to 12 turnovers in those games.
Baltimore's bad omen: Lamar Jackson's durability has been a talking point, because the Ravens aren't the Ravens without their best player. Here's a stat fans won't want to hear: The Ravens have won a total of zero playoff games in seasons where Jackson misses games due to injury. That's not a good sign for 2026.
The Robinson Bros: The Falcons certainly made a statement on "Monday Night Football" last week. It was an evening meant to mark the 20th anniversary of the "Rebirth" of New Orleans. Instead, Atlanta had a "rebirth" of its own.
The Falcons dominated the New Orleans Saints , 45-24. Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns, while the other Robinson, Brian Robinson Jr. , rushed 14 times for 62 yards and THREE touchdowns. They became the second duo in franchise history to score at least two rushing touchdowns apiece in the same game, joining Dave Hampton and Eddie Ray in 1973. Bijan has been a beast, and enters this week ranked second in rushing yards per game (123.5) and scrimmage yards per game (153.5). Usually, those numbers are good enough to lead the league, but Kenneth Walker III is having an MVP-like season of his own out in Kansas City.
Derrick Henry vs. Falcons run defense: Derrick Henry is still one of the best running backs in the game, and ranks fourth in rushing yards (374) and is tied for first in rushing touchdowns (seven) entering Week 5. He has his work cut out for him against this Atlanta run defense, though. The Falcons held the Saints to 50 rushing yards on 19 carries (2.6 yards per carry), and lead the league with just 48.3 rushing yards allowed per game. With Jackson out of the lineup, the Ravens are going to rely even more on Henry. Will he be able to break loose against Jeff Ulbrich's unit?
I don't want to declare the Falcons the greatest show on turf just because they destroyed the Green Bay Packers and the Saints, but there's no denying Penix has looked comfortable in his return to the field. The Falcons are averaging 40.0 points per game with him under center, and Drake London is averaging 145.0 receiving yards. "Snoop" is not the worst backup quarterback in the world, but it's worth mentioning that he couldn't get the Ravens to score a single point in the second half vs. the Titans last week. The city of Atlanta is juiced for this matchup. Falcons win.
Pick: Falcons 27, Ravens 21
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Jaguars vs. Eagles: Where to watch NFL London matchup, plus pick, odds, kickoff time and latest updates
summary: Here's how to follow Sunday's action from London
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are returning to London, their second home, to host the Philadelphia Eagles in the first game of Sunday's NFL slate.
Jacksonville (3-1) just registered statement wins over the Patriots and Bengals . The steady play of quarterback Trevor Lawrence leads the way, supplemented by a defense that has allowed the second-fewest points in the NFL so far.
Philadelphia (2-2) experienced a tumultuous week that included a second-straight loss, the sudden retirement of perennial Pro Bowl lineman Lane Johnson and the trade of fellow Pro Bowl lineman Cam Jurgens . The trade of Jurgens raised questions about the Eagles' motives during the season's final 13 games.
Philadelphia's offensive line will look vastly different. Rookie Markel Bell will replace Johnson at right tackle, and Drew Kendall -- if healthy -- will replace Jurgens at center.
A third-round pick in April's draft, Bell made his first career start during last week's loss to the Rams . Given the circumstances, Bell's overall performance was solid. He allowed six pressures and an 18.8% pressure rate per drop-back. He was better in run blocking while helping the Eagles run for 104 yards despite Saquon Barkley missing most of the game with an injury.
Kendall, a 2025 fifth-round pick, has logged four career starts, including three this season. Kendell's play was one of the reasons why the Eagles felt comfortable trading Jurgens.
Philadelphia has a whopping 12 players on this week's injury report. Among them were Kendall (knee), Barkley (hamstring), and wideouts DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Marquise Brown (ankle) and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring).
These injuries (among others) surely contributed to the Eagles being a sizable underdog in London.
The two teams are in entirely different situations entering Sunday's game. The Eagles have lost two straight and appear to be in jeopardy of waiving the white flag on the season. Philadelphia's struggles have been on both sides of the ball. They're 26th in the NFL in scoring, and their defense is a mediocre 17th in points allowed.
One of the biggest issues so far has been Jalen Hurts ' struggles, which can be attributed in part to instability on the offensive line, injuries to Barkley, a new offensive coordinator for a second straight year, and AJ Brown's absence after he was traded to New England. Makai Lemon , a rookie first-round pick, has caught just 10 passes for 65 yards.
Jacksonville shook off a Week 3 loss in Denver with a blowout win over the Patriots and a five-point win in Cincinnati. The Jaguars have been money so far on third down and in the red zone. Their offense is third in both third-down and red-zone efficiency. The defense is ranked fifth on third down and second in the red zone. Linebacker Foyesade Oluokun has been a force this season with 24 tackles, two interceptions and a forced fumble.
It's hard to fathom the Eagles falling to 2-3 given the talent on their roster. It's even harder, however, to envision them beating the Jaguars unless Jacksonville beats itself with turnovers and other poor play.
Rest assured that Eagles veteran defensive coordinator Vic Fangio will try to make life difficult for Lawrence by taking away the running game and bottling up his receivers. If Lawrence can handle the pressure, the Jaguars should fly back to the States with a 4-1 record.
Score: Jaguars 16, Eagles 13
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Colts vs. Steelers: AFC matchup should have the feel of a playoff game in Pittsburgh
summary: Plus, how to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
full_text:
While it is certainly not a playoff game, Sunday's showdown between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Indianapolis Colts will probably feel like one.
Both teams are 2-2 and could use a win to strengthen their position in their respective divisions. Indianapolis entered Sunday a game behind the Jaguars in the AFC South. Pittsburgh is trailing both Baltimore and Cleveland by a game in the AFC North.
Standings aside, this is an important game for both clubs. The Steelers need to stack wins during the season's first eight weeks as their schedule becomes much tougher after their Week 9 bye. A loss on Sunday would do considerable damage to their playoff chances. The Colts, after starting the season 0-2, can get over .500 for the first time if they can win in a city that has historically been a house of horrors for the franchise.
The two teams last played each other less than a year ago. In Pittsburgh in Week 9, the Steelers recorded a 27-20 win on the strength of six forced turnovers. Pittsburgh led 27-7 with 6:51 left before the Colts scored two late touchdowns.
The Steelers' defense recorded three interceptions of Daniel Jones , who was also sacked five times. Two of those sacks were courtesy of Alex Highsmith , who also had a forced fumble. Another standout on the Steelers' defense that day was Joey Porter Jr. , who had an interception, a sack, eight tackles and four pass breakups. Porter is now a Cowboy after he and the Steelers were unable to reach a contract extension.
Neither team was able to establish the run. Jonathan Taylor gained just 45 yards on 15 carries. Jaylen Warren was held to 31 yards on 16 carries, although he was able to find the end zone twice.
The Steelers have owned the Colts over the last 50-plus years. They are 28-8 against the Colts since 1974, which includes postseason wins in 1976, 1995, 1996, and 2005. Indianapolis hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2008, when Peyton Manning tamed a Steelers defense that won a Super Bowl later that year.
Two of those playoff losses were especially painful for Colts fans. The Colts were Super Bowl favorites entering the 2005 postseason, but their season ended early after Mike Vanderjagt (who at the time was the most accurate kicker in NFL history) missed a game-tying, 46-yard field goal attempt with 21 seconds left. The Steelers went on to become the first sixth seed to win it all.
A decade earlier, the Steelers won the AFC after Aaron Bailey was unable to wrap his arms around Jim Harbaugh's Hail Mary.
The Jim Harbaugh Hail Mary that ALMOST sent the #Colts to the @SuperBowl . #NFLPlayoffs (1995 AFC Championship) pic.twitter.com/iyen1sxN5W
Steelers wideout Michael Pittman , a former Colt who caught nine passes for 115 yards last year against Pittsburgh, is expected to miss several weeks after reinjuring his foot. In Pittman's absence, the Steelers will have to lean more on Roman Wilson and rookie Germie Bernard . Expect Aaron Rodgers to also get tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth involved in the passing game.
Few teams have been better than the Colts' offense inside the 20-yard line. Indianapolis has come away with touchdowns on nine of its 12 trips inside the red zone, which is the sixth-highest rate in the NFL.
The Colts' defense has been even better on third down. Opponents have converted on just 14 of their 48 (29.2%) third-down attempts, which is the fourth-lowest success rate in the NFL. Conversely, the Steelers' offense is just 28th in the NFL on third down, and their defense is 17th in the league in red zone efficiency.
Pittsburgh has a clear advantage in this game. The Steelers are 30th in the NFL in rushing but are eighth in average yards per carry. On Sunday, they'll face a Colts defense that is 28th in the league in average yards-per-carry allowed (4.8). That could mean a big game for Warren, who ran for a combined 220 yards in Pittsburgh's last two games. Warren should be fresh as it will be 10 days since the Steelers' last game.
Score: Steelers 24, Colts 20

title: NFL Week 5 injury report: Eagles' Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith out, Bears' Caleb Williams questionable
summary: Here's a look at the game designations for Week 5 in the NFL
full_text:
Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season is almost here and teams are sending out their final injury reports for the week in preparation for the upcoming matchups. Injuries have plagued this season already and each week it seems we are seeing a top player go down.
Teams have needed to restructure and make new plans as key players are unavailable, with numerous quarterbacks out. This week, Bears QB Caleb Williams is questionable and could make his return, while QB Jayden Daniels is good to go.
This week, the Chiefs and Panthers are on a bye, so they have some time to get healthy for Week 6.
Here's a look at the final injury reports for Sunday:
The already struggling Eagles will be without star running back Saquon Barkley, who suffered a hamstring injury during last week's loss to the Rams . The offense will also be without WR DeVonta Smith.
The Jags are relatively healthy heading into their annual London game, with just two players with designations this week. CB Jaylon Jones was ruled out with a hamstring injury, despite being limited in practice all week, and Eric Murray is doubtful after being limited for the last two days of practice.
The Bears have a chance to get their starting quarterback back on the field this week, after missing Caleb Williams for two weeks with a hamstring injury. Williams was limited in practice on Friday after not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday. Last week, the Bears turned to backup Tyson Bagent in his absence. The Bears' offense will also be without running back Kyle Monangai.
The Packers are also without a running back, as Chris Brooks is dealing with an ankle injury. Running back Pierre Strong will play his first game since 2024 with Brooks out. Green Bay's defensive tackle Javon Hargrave is questionable with a toe injury after he was limited in Friday's practice.
The Texans' offense will be without WR Tank Dell, who is their only player ruled out ahead of Sunday's game as he continues to recover from a knee injury. The Texans activated his 21-day window to return from IR this week, and he was limited in two practices this week, while being a non-participant on Friday. It seems like Houston is closer to having their wideout back. The good news for the Texans is Azeez Al-Shaair is not on the injury report.
The Titans also only have one player out ahead of the divisional matchup. S Amani Hooker is out with a concussion. WR Carnell Tate is questionable with a back injury and head coach Robert Saleh said he would be "good to go" for Sunday.
The Bengals only have one player out this week, S Kyle Duggar, who is out with a quad injury. The big news is WRs Tee Higgins (groin/neck) and Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) are questionable. Chase did not practice on Wednesday, was limited on Thursday and was a full participant on Friday. Higgins did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday and was a full participant on Friday.
The Dolphins have numerous players out this week. Of their questionable players, LB Jackson Woodard was limited on Friday after not practicing the other two days of the week, DT Kenneth Grant was limited on Wednesday and Thursday and was a full participant on Friday. RB Jaylen Wright was limited on Thursday and Friday, while CB Storm Duck was a full participant all week.
The Raiders have a relatively short injury report this week. RB Ashton Jeanty is their only questionable player and he is dealing with a hamstring injury. He was downgraded from a full participant on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday, and he did not practice on Friday. TE Brock Bowers (knee) was not given a game designation after being a full participant on Thursday and Friday.
The Patriots will once again be without their top defender, Christian Gonzalez, who is dealing with a shoulder injury. The defense will also be without cornerback Carlton Davis, who didn't practice last week. The good news for the defense is that they may get Christian Barmore back after missing him last week. They will also be without wide receiver Mack Hollins, who suffered a calf injury last week. They are already without WR A.J. Brown , so losing any more pass catchers is a major hit to Drake Maye's offense.
The biggest question mark for the Vikings surrounds WR Justin Jefferson, who is questionable with an ankle injury. He was limited in practice all week. Another WR with a questionable status is Jordan Addison, who was upgraded to limited on Thursday and Friday after not practicing on Wednesday.
The Saints had a long injury report on their short week and have six players with injury designations, including three ruled out. QB Tyler Shough was on the injury report with a left hand injury, but was not given a game designation.
All Cleveland players with game designations this week are out. The Browns will be without G Teven Jenkins (back) and DT Mason Graham (knee/ankle). They don't have any questionable players this week.
The Jets offense will be without running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell. Edges Kingsley Enagbare and Will McDonald are both among those questionable. Enagbare was a full participant on Friday, while McDonald was added to the injury report on Friday as a limited participant.
Colts WR Keenan Allen is questionable with a groin injury and was a full participant on Friday after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. Another wideout that is questionable for Indy is Darius Slayton, who popped up on the injury report Friday as a limited participant.
Over on the Steelers side, WR Michael Pittman is out with a foot injury, CB Jamel Dean is out with an ankle injury and S DeShon Elliott is out with a knee injury. RB Rico Dowdle was limited all week with a toe injury and CB Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday and Friday after being sidelined in Wednesday's practice with a wrist injury.
The Giants are healthy heading into their divisional matchup. They have two players with game designations and both are out.
The good news for Washington is QB Jayden Daniels will play. The Commanders' injury report is a bit longer, with six players out ahead of Sunday, including WR Stefon Diggs and DE Charles Dmenihu. Coach Dan Quinn said WR Terry McLaurin "looked really good," but didn't confirm whether he will play or not. McLaurin did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday and was limited on Friday.
The Broncos are healthy this week, with two players out, including CB Patrick Surtain II, out with an ankle injury.
The Chargers, on the other hand, have a lengthy injury report this week. The offense will be without WR Quentin Johnston, WR Brenen Thompson, OT Joe Alt and G Kayode Awosika. The defense will be without S Derwin James. The offense could be without Ladd McConkey, who is dealing with a foot injury and did not practice all week.
The Lions have four players ruled out this week, including S Brian Branch, who is dealing with an Achilles injury. DL Tyleik Williams is questionable with a foot injury and was limited on Wednesday and Thursday and was a full participant on Friday.
The Cardinals have two players out and two players questionable this week. DL Walter Nolen and ILB Karson Sharar were full participants on Thursday and Friday but are listed as questionable.
The 49ers are dealing with numerous injuries this season and the hits seem to keep coming. The Niners are once again without DE Nick Bosa, who isn't on IR because of limited space. Another hit to the team is FB Kyle Juszczyk, who is dealing with a knee injury. The two questionable players are CB Upton Stout, who didn't practice on two of the three days, and DE Mykel Williams, who made progress as a full participant over the last two days of practice.
The biggest news out of Baltimore is that Lamar Jackson will miss this week with an ankle injury. The defense also took a hit this week, with linebacker Trey Hendrickson out due to a finger injury.
The Falcons may be without defensive end Za'Darius Smith, who did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday and was upgraded to limited on Friday.…
