title: More alarming injury news for Eagles as they prepare to face Jaguars in London
summary: Philadelphia's offense could be stuck in the mud once again on Sunday
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles ' (2-2) offense is officially in free fall.
Philadelphia is coming off an epic meltdown home defeat against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 in which they blew a double-digit lead and went 0-12 in third-down conversion attempts. In the wake of that loss, Eagles six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired on Tuesday , and the team then traded two-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens .
That's on top of their CVS receipt-length injury list, which includes 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), both being ruled out ahead of Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) in London.
Friday’s Injury Report #PHIvsJAX pic.twitter.com/DY2iRiLFmu
That means Week 5 could look a lot like Week 4. Quarterback Jalen Hurts completed just 12 of his 27 throws for 93 yards while taking four sacks. That all added up to a career-low 3.0 yards per dropback. Since Week 3, Hurts is averaging an NFL-worst 4.7 yards per pass attempt after ranking 11th best in the league in that same metric with a 7.5 yards per pass average through the first two weeks of the season.
The good news for the Eagles is that even with a loss in Week 5, the NFC East will likely remain up for grabs. The New York Giants are 3-1, but their ceiling is capped by the season-ending knee injury to quarterback Jaxson Dart . Fill-in Jameis Winston ranks dead last in the NFL in completion percentage at 55.1% this season. The Giants are also without three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Brian Burns , their best pass rusher, whose 16.5 sacks ranked second in the league in 2025, for the rest of the year after he tore his ACL and meniscus. The Washington Commanders are 1-3, and quarterback Jayden Daniels is once again dealing with an elbow injury.
It will be interesting to see how head coach Nick Sirianni and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion adjust to the absences of both their star playmakers, with the team facing a schematic clash early in the season .
author: Garrett Podell

title: Eagles releasing QB Andy Dalton: Possible landing spots for the signal caller include Vikings, Titans
summary: Dalton will begin the process of finding a new team
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles have made a surprise personnel move as they prepare for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London. The team has released veteran quarterback Andy Dalton , according to multiple reports.
Dalton, who will turn 39 later this month, was intercepted in his only pass attempt this season. It occurred in the end zone during the first half of Philadelphia's eventual Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears when Jalen Hurts temporarily left the game after getting hit by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson .
Dillon Thieneman. First career INT 🚨 @PHIvsCHI on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GQhn7Oz1ZK
Dalton's spot on the Eagles' depth chart will be replaced by Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton . McKee, a 2023 sixth-round pick, has made one start in the last two years. He has five career touchdown passes and one interception and has completed 61.4% of his passes. Payton, a fifth-round pick in this year's draft, has yet to play in a regular-season game.
While the Eagles adjust their quarterback room, Dalton will begin his search for a new team. A three-time Pro Bowler, Dalton spent his first nine NFL seasons with the Bengals , with whom he helped lead to the playoffs five straight seasons from 2011-16. He has also spent time with the Saints , Bears and Panthers .
In his career, Dalton has thrown for 39,793 yards, 254 touchdowns, and 152 interceptions. He has completed 62.6% of his passes.
Where will Dalton end up next? Here are a few possible landing spots.
Minnesota could use another backup quarterback after it traded JJ McCarthy to the Giants . In Dalton, the Vikings would have two veteran quarterbacks behind Kyler Murray , alongside Carson Wentz . Wentz played well earlier this season after Murray sustained an injury.
Speaking of the Giants, they could also use a veteran quarterback after losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending injury. Jameis Winston is coming off his best game as a Giant, but it's safe to say that the Giants would still benefit from having another quarterback in the room. However, after acquiring JJ McCarthy, it's unlikely they're willing to make another move.
This is a situation where Dalton could serve as a mentor for Tyler Shough , whose season so far has had its share of ups and downs. At this point, Shough does not have a mentor in the quarterback room. His current backup is Spencer Rattler , who is a year younger than he is. Dalton could be a valuable sounding board for a young room looking for some guidance.
Like New Orleans, Dalton could serve as a mentor in Miami for Malik Willis , who is currently entrenched in his first season as a full-time starter. Willis' current backup, Kyle McCord , is also in his first year with the Dolphins and has yet to play in an NFL regular-season game. But the question remains whether the tanking Dolphins would go after a quarterback now or get their pick during the 2027 NFL Draft.
Another team where Dalton could help a young quarterback find his footing. Cam Ward , the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft , is still growing as a starting quarterback. It's safe to assume that a player with Dalton's experience would help him with his continued development.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Arvell Reese, Sonny Styles to meet in Week 5: Did Giants make right choice between first-round linebackers?
summary: There might not have been a wrong answer for the Giants at pick No. 5 in the 2026 NFL Draft
full_text:
When the Washington Commanders host the New York Giants on Sunday, keep an eye on No. 52. Both of them.
There is a striking parallel between the two teams: Both have a first-round rookie linebacker from Ohio State who wears the same number as the other. Giants standout Arvell Reese and burgeoning Commanders star Sonny Styles became the first college linebacker teammates to be selected in the top 10 of the same NFL Draft when they flew off the board in April. In Week 5, they go head-to-head.
At the draft, the Giants were in the enviable position of having both Reese and Styles available to them at pick No. 5. There was immense debate prior to draft night about which player New York should select if both were up for grabs. After the event, a major question was whether they took the right one.
In the end, there might not have been a wrong answer.
That the Giants are off to a 3-1 start despite being without quarterback Jaxson Dart for nearly three full games is largely a credit to Reese and the defense. New York is a top-10 team in yards and points allowed through Week 4, and Reese is the engine that powers the unit. Not only does he pace the team with 33 tackles, but he also leads the entire league in solo stops with 26.
Reese is also fresh off the best game of his young career: a nine-tackle effort with one tackle for loss in a 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals . The NFL recognized him as the Week 4 Rookie of the Week after he became the fifth Giants rookie with three passes defended and an interception in one game.
. @Giants LB Arvell Reese is the Week 4 @Pepsi Rookie of the Week! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/rPL7zPszYQ
The production is already game-changing. It is everything the Giants could have asked for when they used their first of two first-round picks on a linebacker. Reese's utility goes well beyond the numbers, though. His versatility proved to be a major asset across four games for a Giants defense that lost its top edge rusher, Brian Burns , for the season with a torn ACL . Reese's pass-rushing ability from the off-ball linebacker spot will be crucial the rest of the year as the Giants work to overcome the absence of Burns, who last year amassed 16.5 sacks in an All-Pro campaign.
Reese is a more natural pass-rusher than Styles, which is an obvious asset, but at the draft, there was hesitation over whether he was the better pick. The Giants were already stocked at the edge rusher position with Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux providing both top-flight play in the starting lineup and enviable depth. With one of them out for the year, though, Reese is even more important to the unit than he already was. He is a linebacker first and likely always will be, but Reese can also play in the trenches. In his debut, even with Burns healthy, he aligned on the line of scrimmage on 11 of 52 snaps.
Reese is exactly what the Giants hoped they were getting when they picked him. But who's to say Sonny Styles would not have been the same? He could have been just as impactful, had he been the No. 5 pick instead.
When the Commanders upset the Seahawks in Week 3, Styles looked the part of a star in the making. He earned the NFC Defensive Player of the Week award for his efforts, which also made him the first rookie linebacker in franchise history with an interception, a forced fumble and multiple passes defended in one game.
Styles' ability to wreak havoc in the backfield with inside pressure is also tremendous. He boasts the highest pressure rate among rookie defenders with at least 25 pass-rush snaps at 17.9%. The Commanders are about as aggressive as they come in pass defense with the second-highest blitz rate in the league, per Next Gen Stats, and Styles is a key figure in that scheme as they regularly rush him toward the quarterback.
And then there was this play, where Styles demolished Saquon Barkley en route to a sack.
Oh my Sonny Styles 😳 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/c77koTv4jd
While they attack the pocket from different angles, Styles and Reese are both impact pass-rushers. Perhaps the Giants would have been better off with Styles, given their depth on the edge.
Styles has stepped up in the face of injuries just like Reese. Leo Chenal and Jordan Magee are both on injured reserve, leaving Styles, Frankie Luvu and Kain Medrano as the only three available inside linebackers. Not only that, but Styles routinely handles the defense's green-dot duties, relaying play calls to the rest of the unit as just a rookie. There is a chance he could have secured that job with the Giants, too, considering New York relies on 2026 newcomer Tremaine Edmunds to orchestrate the defense. Styles has a whole lot on his plate for someone with only four games of experience, and is not just getting by. He is thriving.
In hindsight, the Giants found themselves in a win-win position at the draft. With Reese and Styles as their targets, they could not have gone wrong. What both players displayed over the first four games of their professional careers proved that New York could have gone in either direction and come away with the same result, at least for the first month of the year. The final analysis will not be complete for years, when their career arcs take full shape, but as of now, the Ohio State products are on level footing.
If the argument for Reese was that he is the better pass rusher, then Styles bridged the gap with his effective blitzes. If the argument for Styles was that he is the better defender in coverage, then Reese closed that discrepancy. According to Pro Football Focus, Reese graded out over four games as the ninth-best linebacker in coverage, while Styles is a mere six spots ahead of him at No. 3. In a sample size of 74 qualified linebackers, both are excellent.
Both are top-five rookie linebackers in overall PFF defensive grade.
Harold Perkins Jr. , Falcons
Josiah Trotter , Buccaneers
Reese has the second-best odds to win Defensive Rookie of the Year at +275, and Styles is directly behind him with the third-shortest odds at +750, per DraftKings . The margin between their first-year production is extremely thin, and both carry long-term stardom potential. The Giants ought to feel elated about their choice in the draft, and the Commanders should, too.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Former NFL star calls out Cowboys for controversial two-point decision in fourth quarter: "Wasn't smart'
summary: Dez Bryant didn't like Dallas' call to go for two, and he may have been right
full_text:
Former Cowboys star Dez Bryant isn't a fan of analytics, at least not when it pertains to one specific scenario, and that exact situation came up during Dallas' stunning 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night.
With the Cowboys trailing 24-10 in the fourth quarter, Dak Prescott engineered a 99-yard drive that culminated with an 18-yard touchdown pass to George Pickens . After the score, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer decided to go for two, but the Cowboys came up short.
Why would you go for two down by eight? Cowboys fans were booing before they even lined up. pic.twitter.com/AG0K3Re0lH
Bryant shared his thoughts about the decision on social media, and he definitely didn't agree with Schottenheimer's choice to bypass an easy extra point.
Dez better get used to the idea of the Cowboys doing this, because if this same situation comes up in the future, Dallas will definitely be going for two, and Schottenheimer made that clear after the game.
"That's our philosophy," Schottenheimer said via Patrik Walker of the team's official website . "When you're down 14, especially with our offense, because when you get it, you have a chance to go and win the game, and you make it a six-point game."
Bryant was clearly frustrated with the call, but Schottenheimer's decision came down to numbers, so let's break down both sides of the coin.
This all comes down to analytics. The math says it makes more sense to go for two when you score a touchdown while trailing by 14. The main reason teams do this is so they know what they need to get sooner rather than later.
A two-point conversion has about a 50% chance of success if you look at the historical rate, while an extra point has about a 97% success rate. Since the Cowboys needed two scores to tie or take the lead, Schottenheimer had to plan ahead and decide what the team would do after each touchdown.
With that in mind, he essentially had two options (this all assumes the game played out similarly to Thursday, with the Cowboys defense not giving up any more points):
1. Kick the extra point after each touchdown 2. Go for two after the first touchdown, and the result of that attempt would determine what the team would do on the second touchdown. If you convert the two-pointer, you kick the extra point on the second attempt. If you fail on the two-pointer, then you have to attempt a two-point conversion on your second attempt.
If you go with option 1, that guarantees overtime. If you go with option 2, you have a chance to win in regulation. For the Cowboys specifically, option 2 likely had some appeal because the Bucs had been steamrolling their defense all night. If the Cowboys had converted the two-pointer, then Dallas' defense would have only had to make one more stop to give the Cowboys a chance to win the game.
Now, let's run through all the numbers on the two-point decision:
If you kick two extra points, there's no scenario where you win in regulation, and that's part of the allure of the two-pointer. If you make the first one, you put your team in an advantageous situation, and that's what Schottenheimer was trying to do.
After the game was over, Bryant offered a longer explanation for why he didn't like the two-point decision, and considering this take is coming from a former player, it's certainly worth listening to.
"I don't care if we got the 2, I still think that wasn't a smart decision," Bryant wrote . "Knowing you're down 7 vs. down 8 makes a difference."
Basically, there's a psychological aspect of the decision that the math doesn't account for. A player's mentality changes based on the score, especially late in the game. If you watch a highlight of the Cowboys' two-point attempt, Dak Prescott and several other players walked off the field with a dejected look after the conversion failed. This team just drove 99 yards for a huge touchdown, but it felt like they lost momentum after the failed two-point conversion.
Not only is there a psychological aspect to consider, but there's also the overtime aspect. In general, teams want to win in regulation because, in the past, overtime would essentially come down to a coin flip. If you won the coin toss, you got the ball, and you could go down and win the game with a touchdown. However, with the new overtime rules, both teams are guaranteed a possession, so if you force overtime, you know your best unit — in Dallas' case, that would be the offense — will get to see the field at least once.
The time left in the game should also play into a coach's consideration. If the Cowboys had scored with 2:30 left, it probably wouldn't make sense to go for two, because if you fail, you're now in a situation where you might need TWO more possessions to win, which is what would happen if you also failed on the second two-pointer. In that situation, your opponent would get two possessions, and they would be able to burn off a minimum of two minutes without getting a single first down.
Also, if you miss the first two-point conversion, you're down eight, which means you have to score quickly, because you have to leave yourself some time in case you miss the second two-point conversion. And if you do miss, then your defense has to make ANOTHER stop.
I get the math of going for two in the Cowboys' situation, but this shouldn't be an automatic play. As Bryant pointed out, there are other factors at play besides the raw numbers, so teams should probably make case-by-case decisions rather than make it their "philosophy."
author: John Breech

title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson for Week 5 matchup vs. Falcons due to ankle injury
summary: Tyler Huntley will make his first start of the year in Atlanta
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson when the team travels to Atlanta to take on the red-hot Falcons , as he has been ruled out with an ankle injury. Tyler Huntley will start under center as Baltimore looks to improve on its 3-1 record.
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters they knew Jackson being ruled out for Week 5 was always a possibility, but that the quarterback worked "his tail off" in recovery, and is "doing everything in his power to get back." He did not practice at all this week.
The two-time NFL MVP injured his ankle at the end of the second quarter in the Ravens' eventual 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans last Sunday. On the second-to-last play of the first half, Jermaine Johnson II tackled Jackson, who appeared to twist his ankle. Jackson was having an impressive game up to that point, completing 15-of-20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns.
Huntley replaced Jackson in the third quarter and completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards and rushed four times for 16 yards. The Ravens did not score a single point in the final two quarters. "Snoop" has a 7-9 record as a starter and has scored 14 total touchdowns compared to 12 turnovers.
The Ravens are 6-11 in the regular season without Jackson since he became the full-time starter. His durability has become a talking point, as Baltimore has won zero playoff games in seasons where Jackson missed time due to injuries.
Jackson's injury comes at a bad time, as the Ravens have to travel to take on one of the hottest teams in the NFL in prime time. Since Michael Penix Jr . returned to the field, the Falcons are averaging 40.0 points per game after averaging just 8.0 points per game in Weeks 1-2. Penix has brought some stability to the passing attack, as Drake London is averaging 145.0 receiving yards per game over the past two contests, but the real headliner for Atlanta's offense is running back Bijan Robinson .
Robinson ranks second in rushing yards per game (123.5) and scrimmage yards per game (153.5) entering Week 5. In the Falcons' 45-24 shellacking of the New Orleans Saints on Monday night, he rushed for 145 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries. Brian Robinson Jr . also played a part in the beatdown, rushing for 62 yards and three touchdowns. The Falcons ran 35 times and passed the ball just 20 times. The Falcons also boast the No. 1 rushing defense in the league, allowing 48.3 rushing yards per game.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Mike Ditka's five greatest moments as a player and coach: Super Bowl XX takes top spot
summary: Ditka's football journey was one of a kind
full_text:
The NFL lost a giant on Friday with the passing of Mike Ditka. A Chicago icon, Ditka led the Bears to championships as both a player and a coach. He is just one of two men in history to win Super Bowls as a player, an assistant coach and as a head coach.
Ditka wasn't just a great player and coach. He was a legendary character who epitomized Chicago's tough, blue-collar spirit. He had a unique look, a fiery temper, and a humorous side that occasionally surfaced at press conferences. That side of him famously came out in 1999, when he shared a magazine cover with Ricky Williams depicting a wedding.
Ditka and the Saints ' decision to trade a bounty of picks for Williams didn't work out, but most of Ditka's other football ventures did. Here's a look at his five greatest NFL moments.
Thanks for da memories, Coach 💙 pic.twitter.com/VITX0Dffzq
After a meteoric rise in Chicago, Ditka's NFL career seemed to be coming to a close in 1969 following three disappointing seasons in Philadelphia. But Cowboys coach Tom Landry thought that Ditka still had some gas left in the tank. "You think you can still play football?" Ditka recalled Landry asking him over the phone. "I think I can," Ditka said, to which Landry replied, "I hope you can, because I just traded for you."
In hindsight, Landry did more than add years onto Ditka's playing career. Ditka ended his playing career on a high note, catching a touchdown pass in Super Bowl VI, the Cowboys' first Super Bowl win. He retired the following season and immediately joined Landry's staff as special teams and receivers coach.
Mike Ditka, Super Bowl VI The legendary tight end hauled in a 7-yard touchdown from Roger Staubach to salt away the Dallas Cowboys' first Super Bowl championship. Iron Mike later made a nice 21-yard leaping snag on a crosser, and nearly scored again on a 17-yard end around. pic.twitter.com/ZPIezlZxvr
Ditka won a second Super Bowl with the Cowboys in 1977, and in 1982, then-Bears owner George Halas felt that Ditka was ready to return to Chicago as the Bears' new head coach.
Ditka's role on the Bears' 1963 championship team undoubtedly paved the way for his future success as both a player and a coach. That was the Bears' eighth and final NFL title under Halas, who passed away in 1983, a year after he hired Ditka as coach.
The 1963 Bears were formidable, to say the least. They posted an 11-1-2 record that included season sweeps over Vince Lombardi's Packers and Johnny Unitas' Colts .
In the NFL Championship game, the Bears recorded a 17-14 win over the New York Giants and Y.A. Tittle, who was named the league's MVP that season. The Bears' win was the byproduct of six forced turnovers that included five interceptions of Tittle. Ditka, who was named to his third of five consecutive Pro Bowls that season, contributed to the cause with 38 yards on three catches.
Ironically, the Bears would not win another playoff game until 1984 (Ditka's third season as Chicago's coach) despite Halas drafting future Hall of Famers Gale Sayers and Dick Butkus in 1965. Butkus and Sayers never played in a postseason game.
One of the stars of the '85 Bears was then-rookie William "Refrigerator" Perry, a 6-foot-2, 335-pound defensive lineman who bowled over defenders while lining up at running back.
The origin of Perry, the running back, dates back to the 1984 NFC Championship game. With the game out of hand, then-49ers coach Bill Walsh put offensive lineman Guy McIntyre into the game as a fullback. Walsh's usage of McIntyre in that situation drew Chicago's ire, Ditka's especially.
In October of that year, the Bears returned to San Francisco, but this time, they were the better team. Chicago's 26-10 win included Perry's offensive debut. Perry carried the ball twice through the teeth of the 49ers ' defense during the game's final moments.
"It was calculated," Ditka said in 2015 . "Believe me, it was payback time, and I don't apologize for it. I never would. What goes around comes around."
That day spawned the birth of the phenomenon that was Refrigerator Perry, the running back. The following week on Monday night, Perry ran for his first career touchdown.
"He would just grab [the football] like it was a cheesburger," quarterback Jim McMahon recalled years later. "He wanted it so bad. He would rip my arms off."
Perry's stardom reached its zenith in the Super Bowl, when he scored Chicago's fourth and final touchdown on a one-yard run.
A Super Bowl record: The first Refrigerator to score 😏 There's nothing like a lineman TD and this one from William "Refrigerator" Perry will never get old. 👊 #SuperBowlNBCSN | @ChicagoBears pic.twitter.com/WlQoqJurJ9
Unfortunately, Perry's score came at the expense of Walter Payton, the Bears' iconic running back who was hoping to score on football's biggest stage. At the time, Ditka didn't know that scoring a touchdown meant that much to Payton, who was almost inconsolable afterward.
Bears players from that team have mixed emotions on the situation. While some feel that Ditka should have known better, others don't fault him for not thinking about an individual player during a game of that magnitude.
"It never, ever, crossed my mind," Ditka said decades later. "Now was that wrong of me? Yes, probably, but it didn't. I didn't think it would mean anything to, I think, the greatest Bear ever, but it did. So, I was wrong. That I regret a lot. I really do regret it a lot, because I didn't realize that it was important to him, and it was very important to him."
Ditka's Hall of Fame career as a player started with arguably the greatest rookie season in NFL history. In a 14-game regular season, Ditka caught 56 passes for 1,076 yards and 12 touchdowns and averaged a whopping 19.2 yards per catch en route to winning the NFL Rookie of the Year.
Ditka's record for most receiving yards by a rookie tight end lasted for 63 years until it was broken by the Raiders' tight end Brock Bowers in 2024. His receptions record for a rookie tight end stood for 27 years until it was broken by then-Eagles tight end Keith Jackson. Ditka's 12 touchdown receptions that season remain the single-season tight end rookie record.
That season served as a springboard for the next 50-plus years of Ditka's life. It contributed to him becoming the first tight end to earn Hall of Fame induction in 1988.
Mike Ditka was the NFL's modern right end when he entered the league in 1961, he is the first tight end into the hall of fame. His signature play as a TE was against the Steelers, two days after the JFK Assassination with this catch and run to set a GT FG (I believe) pic.twitter.com/glSZrNHQjD
As great a player as Ditka was, he is largely remembered for being the coach of the Bears' only Super Bowl-winning team.
Ditka first planted the seeds to becoming the Bears' coach when he was still working for Dallas. He wrote a note to Halas, who had traded Ditka away as a player over a contract dispute.
"It said, 'Coach, I know I left the Bears on bad terms, but I've always had a great love for the Chicago Bears. I would love the opportunity to come back and coach the Bears someday,' " Ditka recalled.
Halas ultimately did hire Ditka, and in a twist of irony, made him the NFL's lowest-paid head coach. Ditka no longer cared about money, though. He just wanted to win, and he quickly made that clear to his new players.
"The first practice, he gets us all together, and he said, 'Boys, I've got some good news, and I've got some bad news,'" recalled Hall of Fame defensive lineman Steve McMichael. "The good news is, you give me three years, we're going to the Super Bowl. The bad news is half of you aren't gonna be here to see it."
Super Bowl XX #Bears pic.twitter.com/LVaGM6sksD
Ditka's words proved to be prophetic. The Bears won it all three years later, and when it was over, he was carried off the field by his players and into NFL immortality.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL Week 5 picks: Experts face off on 49ers at Seahawks, Falcons vs. Ravens and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
We are already five weeks into the 2026 NFL regular season. Can you believe it? This week, the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars face off in London, the San Francisco 49ers will play the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Seattle, and Josh Allen takes on Matthew Stafford on "Monday Night Football."
There were 23 games decided by one score over the past two weeks, which is tied for the most in a two-week span in NFL history. A total of 18 games this season were decided by a game-winning score in the final four minutes or in overtime, which is tied for the second-most through Week 4. The NFL always delivers, and we are expecting more fireworks in Week 5.
Which teams should you pick, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 6 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Credit to CBS Sports Research
Dajani (Jaguars -7): Our London Jaguars fans must feel proud. The team they've supported for years returns to the United Kingdom as arguably the best team in the AFC, and they will take on a squad that looks like it's flailing. The Eagles blew a 10-point lead to the Los Angeles Rams in the final four minutes of the fourth quarter last Sunday, and went an incredible 0-12 on third downs. If that wasn't bad enough, franchise legend right tackle Lane Johnson decided to retire on Tuesday to focus on his mental health, and the team traded left guard Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens on Wednesday. I know Jurgens wasn't exactly Larry Allen, but that's just another starter gone on Jalen Hurts ' offensive line.
Then, there are the injuries for the Eagles. Running back Saquon Barkley left last week's game with a hamstring injury, and his replacement, Tank Bigsby, was also injured and placed on injured reserve. Star wideout DeVonta Smith missed last week with a hamstring issue as well. The vibes are not great in Philly right now. Even if Barkley plays, this Jaguars run defense has been fantastic. They allowed a grand total of 17 rushing yards to the Cincinnati Bengals ' running backs last week and are tied for second in takeaways with eight.  … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Eagles 18
Dubin (Eagles +7): I don't exactly feel great about this prediction given the way the Eagles have looked so far this season, but I'm betting that they can at least keep the game relatively close against a Jaguars team that looks like one of the best in football. They did the same thing against the Rams last week, despite all the injury and availability issues Dajani described above. Jacksonville should be able to win, but I like the Eagles to cover.  … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Eagles 17
Dajani (Packers +3): I can't believe I'm backing a team that I think has looked like one of the worst in the NFL up to this point. They couldn't even cover the spread against an undrafted backup quarterback making his first start. But sometimes that's the NFL! The Packers return home to host the rival Chicago Bears , who are trotting out Tyson Bagent at quarterback. I'm not sure Bagent can run this Bears offense as effectively as Case Keenum can. Plus, running backs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai are banged up and missed practice on Wednesday. I'm going to kick myself if the Bears cover, but Green Bay is 6-1 SU and ATS in its last seven home games vs. Chicago. Something weird is going to happen!   … Prediction: Packers 21, Bears 20
Dubin (Push): The Packers barely squeaked by a Buccaneers team playing its backup quarterback last week, and now get to go up against another backup quarterback here in Tyson Bagent. I think Bagent can lead a more competent offense than Jalon Daniels did, though, and the Bears should be able to run the ball against this Green Bay defense. Chicago's defense has played surprisingly well this year, but it's basically been all about success on third down. If the Packers can actually sustain some drives, they should be able to keep things relatively close.  … Prediction: Bears 23, Packers 20
Dajani ( Steelers -2.5): The Indianapolis Colts just got back from London, while the Steelers had extended rest following their Thursday night loss to the Cleveland Browns . I think that could play a legitimate factor in this game. One thing that stood out to me from Indy's win over Washington was how questionable the defense looked. Athan Kaliakmanis came off the bench and threw for 186 yards, one touchdown and an interception in his first NFL action, while Treylon Burks burned Sauce Gardner for a 47-yard touchdown. The Colts rank second-worst in the NFL in total defense and eighth-worst in total offense. I don't have much faith in the Steelers as legitimate contenders, but they've owned the Colts in Pittsburgh. They are 17-2 all-time when Indy comes to visit. I expect a competitive game, but I understand why the Steelers are 2.5-point favorites.  … Prediction: Steelers 24, Colts 17
Dubin (Colts +2.5): The Steelers have looked good for exactly one of their three games so far this year, and that was in a game against a Bengals defense that now looks a lot friendlier than it did through the first two weeks of the season. The Colts also have a fairly friendly defense, but I frankly don't trust the Steelers as far as Aaron Rodgers or I can throw them, so I'm taking the Colts to win a low-ish scoring game on the back of Jonathan Taylor .  … Prediction: Colts 20, Steelers 16
Dajani (49ers +2.5): This could be the game of the week. Two NFC West rivals that fought for the No. 1 seed in the conference last year and ended up battling in the playoffs as well. The Seahawks defeated the lowly Los Angeles Chargers last week, 30-23, although they led 27-6 at one point. The 49ers, on the other hand, won a tough battle vs. the Denver Broncos , 24-14. I think Brock Purdy has been an underrated storyline this year, and should be the frontrunner for MVP. Sure, he's benefitted from playing teams like the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals , but the 49ers quarterback is the only player to ever start a season 4-0 with one or fewer sacks/fumbles/interceptions combined. He also has the highest EPA per dropback (0.53) through four games since Tom Brady in 2007! The 49ers are 4-0 SU and ATS in their last four road games vs. the Seahawks, and 12-2 SU and 11-2-1 ATS in their last 14 road divisional games. Give me the upset.   … Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 23
Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): I think these look like the two best teams in the league so far this season, despite Seattle's weird loss to Washington and the let-up the defense showed in the second half against L.A. last week. The 49ers have been electric offensively despite hemorrhaging skill-position players, but running into this Seattle defense could change that — especially if Mike Evans is still not 100% healthy. The 49ers' defense is also dealing with some injury issues and could have some trouble covering Jaxon Smith-Njigba , as everyone in the league does.  … Prediction: Seahawks 24, 49ers 21
Dajani ( Falcons -3.5): I don't want to declare the Atlanta Falcons the greatest show on turf just because they destroyed the Packers and New Orleans Saints , but Michael Penix Jr . has looked comfortable in his return to the field. That's probably because he's got an MVP candidate next to him in Bijan Robinson , who is off to a historic start, averaging 153.5 total yards per game. I would like to see Lamar Jackson take the field on "Sunday Night Football," but it looks like it will be Tyler Huntley instead. "Snoop" is not the worst backup quarterback in the world, but he couldn't get the Ravens to score a single point in the second half vs. the Tennessee Titans . I wish I had gotten this line at -2.5, but I'll have to settle for -3.5.   … Prediction: Falcons 27, Ravens 21
Dubin (Falcons -3.5): This line seems to be assuming that Lamar Jackson will not play for the Ravens, which would obviously be a huge bummer. (If he does…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Tributes pour in as NFL world mourns, remembers football giant and HOFer Mike Ditka
summary: A Hall of Fame coach who guided the iconic 1985 Bears to a Super Bowl XX title, Ditka won 106 games in Chicago, second in franchise history
full_text:
Legendary head coach Mike Ditka died at the age of 86 on Friday . A football giant, Ditka is a member of both the College Football Hall of Fame and Pro Football Hall of Fame. The former tight end won Offensive Rookie of the Year in 1961 with the Chicago Bears after racking up 1,076 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns in his first NFL season — the perfect way to start a 12-year career that saw him win Super Bowl VI with the Dallas Cowboys .
Ditka retired following the 1972 season and began his coaching career as an assistant under Tom Landry in Dallas. The Cowboys made three Super Bowls during his tenure, winning one (XII). In 1982, the Bears, who drafted Ditka No. 5 overall out of Pittsburgh, hired him to be their new head coach.
Chicago made the NFC Championship game in 1984, and then went 15-1 in 1985 on the way to a Super Bowl XX win over the New England Patriots . It remains the Bears' lone Super Bowl title.
Ditka registered seven double-digit win seasons in his 11 years with the Bears, won NFL Coach of the Year in 1985 and 1988, and made seven playoff appearances with three NFC Championship appearances. His 106 wins rank second in franchise history behind George Halas, who coached Chicago for four decades. No Bears head coach has held their post for more than nine years other than Ditka and Halas. He wrapped up his coaching career with the New Orleans Saints , going 15-33 over three seasons.
"Mike Ditka epitomized football over so many years," NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. "He brought intensity, authenticity, and an unmistakable personality to everything he did. As a Hall of Fame player, Super Bowl-winning coach with his beloved and iconic Bears, and as a broadcaster, Mike served as an ambassador for the game and inspired generations of fans. Through his work with the Gridiron Greats Assistance Fund, Mike was a champion for taking care of those who helped build our game. We extend our deepest condolences to Diana and the Ditka family."
Ditka is one of two men to win a Super Bowl as a player, assistant coach and head coach in NFL history, joining fellow Hall of Famer Tom Flores. Reactions around the football world poured in to mourn the loss of a legendary leader. That includes Walter Payton's son, Jarrett, who shared a statement from the Ditka family.
"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka. While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever. With love and gratitude, The Ditka Family."

title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones expresses interest in making trades despite embarrassing loss to Buccaneers
summary: Despite a stunning home loss to Tampa Bay, Dallas sits at 2-3 in a wide-open NFC East with enough draft capital to make another splash before the deadline
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (2-3) couldn't have done much more to embarrass themselves than what they did in their 24-16 head-scratcher of a loss against the previously-winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) on "Thursday Night Football" to kick off Week 5.
The Cowboys trudged off their home field at AT&T Stadium on Thursday while being serenaded by a chorus of boos, and they earned every bit of it. Tampa Bay entered the game with undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and when the clock hit zero, he was walking off the field with the third-largest upset win, as a 9.5-point underdog, by an undrafted rookie quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger, per CBS Sports Research. Daniels was an efficient 19 for 25 passing with 189 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 23 yards on 7 carries. Even more damning was allowing Buccaneers running back Bucky Irvin to explode for a career-high 165 yards rushing and a touchdown on 21 carries for a 7.9 yards per carry average. Entering Thursday, he had averaged just 59.2 rushing yards per game across the last two seasons.
Dallas' loss was so disheartening that someone yelled "embarrassing" at Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott as he walked through the bowels of the stadium to the locker room by himself after the game.
"It's a loss we're supposed to have, definitely supposed to have. To use the word embarrassing — it's tough," Prescott said. "I feel like I'm discrediting the NFL if I use that [the word embarrassing] and particularly the Tampa Bay Bucs, the great Todd Bowles. … [But] when a winless team comes into your home stadium on a Thursday night primetime game, yeah, we're supposed to win that."
Was the loss embarrassing enough to dissuade Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones from no longer pursuing additional win-now trades? He already traded a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for 26-year-old cornerback Joey Porter Jr . Porter Jr. didn't make his home debut Thursday night because of "flu-like" symptoms. Jones' answer to that question is simple: Nope, I'm still open for business. The man is set to turn 84 years old on Oct. 13, so he's open to doing what he can to win a fourth Super Bowl right now.
"The future capital, I wouldn't give it up for a player who didn't have some future or the potential of future that you could add years to. The future capital that you have are draft picks. Those guys have question marks with them too. So if we do see an opportunity, and it fits for us, we'll take a good look at it," Jones said postgame. "This isn't fold the tents here. We are 2-3, didn't expect to be 2-3. Didn't expect this Tampa team to come here 0-4 either. They got a lot of good players. Unquestionably, they were the better team tonight."
Jones does say a lot of eyebrow-raising things, but it is fair for him to envision the NFC East division to still be up for grabs for his Cowboys, as surreal as that sentiment feels in this moment. The New York Giants are 3-1, but their ceiling is limited by the season-ending knee injury to quarterback Jaxson Dart . Fill-in Jameis Winston ranks dead last in the NFL in completion percentage at 55.1% this season. The Giants are also without three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Brian Burns , their best pass rusher, whose 16.5 sacks ranked second in the league in 2025, for the rest of the year after he tore his ACL and meniscus. The Philadelphia Eagles (2-2) are fresh off an epic meltdown home loss of their own against the Los Angeles Rams in which they blew a double-digit lead and went 0-12 in third-down conversion attempts.
In the aftermath of that loss, Eagles six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired on Tuesday , and Philadelphia then traded two-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens . That's on top of their CVS receipt-length injury list. The Washington Commanders are 1-3, and quarterback Jayden Daniels is once again dealing with an elbow injury.
As a refresher before we dive into the trade candidates, here is a look at the draft picks the Cowboys still own the rights to in the event Jones wants to continue doubling down on the 2026 season.
Here is a look at three players Jones could trade for and "add years to" to win now and over the next season or two.
This is the big fish right here. The Cowboys currently rank eighth-worst in the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (32.7%) and fifth-worst in sack rate (3.4%). Their pass rush is one of their most glaring remaining needs on defense. Two of their veteran, Pro Bowl edge rushers they acquired this offseason, Rashan Gary and Von Miller , look to be past their expiration date, and the Cowboys have yet to be able to replace All-Pro Micah Parsons ' production after trading him to the Green Bay Packers just before the start of the 2025 season.
Should Jones be comfortable parting with high-round draft capital, Los Angeles Chargers 24-year-old Pro Bowl edge rusher Tuli Tuipulotu makes a lot of sense. The age is right, and like Porter Jr., he is a former second-round pick in the final year of his rookie deal, looking to cash in on a large, new deal. Tulipulotu's contract situation could make him available in a trade should the 0-4 Chargers decide to have a fire sale ahead of a highly anticipated 2027 NFL Draft class.
He erupted for 13.0 sacks, the sixth most in the NFL, and 70 quarterback pressures, the 11th most in the league, in 2025 en route to earning his first Pro Bowl selection in 2025, and he's on pace for another strong season through the first quarter of 2026. He's up to 2.0 and 14 quarterback pressures already this season, despite Los Angeles having spent the sixth-most time in the NFL trailing their opponents at 2:13:59.
This is the splash move if Jerry truly wants to be "all in" again.
The Dallas Cowboys reportedly tried to trade for Miami Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks in the offseason, when he had just one year left on his contract, before Miami extended Brooks on a three-year, $48 million contract with $35 million guaranteed in the summer.
However, the Dolphins are in the middle of a tear-it-down-to-the-studs rebuild in Year 1, with new head coach Jeff Hafley and new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, both of whom come from the Green Bay Packers' draft-and-develop franchise model. Miami is 0-4 and has the NFL's worst scoring offense (11.5 points per game), and is the only team that has not led at any point in 2026. The Dolphins are also paying more for players not on their roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than the players on their roster ($156 million).
Brooks is 29 years old and under contract through the 2029 season, his age-32 season. That's basically the rest of his prime. Jones not having to worry about Brooks' contract situation is likely a relief, and on a hopeless 2026 Dolphins team, he is still a bright spot. Pro Football Focus grades Brooks as the NFL's No. 12 overall linebacker with a defensive grade of 82.7. He would also be an immediate help to the Cowboys' league-worst run defense, which is allowing an average of 168.4 yards per game. Brooks ranks as PFF's No. 4 linebacker against the run with an 82.7 run defense grade.
One might look at this trade candidate and think, "Wait, a minute. Dallas is loaded at wide receiver with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens !" Yes, that is true, but this trade is more about special teams with a little bit of potential WR3 or WR4 upside. Denver Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. is still a developing wide receiver at 24 years old, but he is already one of the NFL's best return men. Mims Jr. is a two-time Pro Bowl returner and earned first-team All-Pro returner accolades in 2024 when he led the NFL with a 15.7 yards per punt return average. He has both a kick and a punt return touchdown in his career, and he led the NFL with 452 punt return yards in 2025.
Dallas does have a three-time Pro…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Are the Texans cooked after their 0-4 start? Why a sliver of hope still remains for Houston
summary: The Texans are winless and on the brink of losing their season, but there are at least a few reasons to wait it out a little longer
full_text:
Going into the 2026 season, the Houston Texans were a trendy dark horse pick to come out of the AFC and make the Super Bowl . On the backs of one of the best defenses in the NFL and a retooled offensive line in front of QB CJ Stroud , the Texans were expected to wreck shop through the AFC.
Four games into the season, and we still haven't seen the Texans pick up their first win.
The offense has been inconsistent, battling through Nico Collins injuries and an offensive line that hasn't truly gelled together yet. Defensively, a unit that was supposed to be elite has looked the opposite during the early quarter of the season. Their 2.42 points allowed per drive is the highest through four games since Demeco Ryans took over as head coach and is a far cry from last season's 1.21 points allowed per drive.
The spin zone for Texans fans is that this organization came back from being 0-3 to making the playoffs in 2025, but 0-4 feels like a deep hole to climb out of, with the 1992 Chargers as the only team to make the playoffs after starting 0-4. The Texans go into their game against Tennessee (who is also winless) desperately needing a win to keep their season alive, but how and why did we get to this point?
Let's start with the bad for the Texans right now, which focuses on the defensive side of the ball. Yes, they've faced a lot of the NFL's best offenses in Buffalo, Cincinnati and Dallas to start the season, but something about the group has felt…off. It's why head coach Demeco Ryans took back playcalling duties from defensive coordinator Matt Burke and why the team overall has looked the way it has.
For the 2026 Texans to work, this defense would have to be an elite group as the offense found its way and gelled together, and the defense hasn't been that. Again, they've faced some tough offenses and were without starting LB Azeez Al-Shaair in their loss to the Cowboys , but the underlying metrics this season have revealed a much larger problem.
Through four games, the Texans are allowing the most explosive passes since Demeco Ryans took over. Despite still being a top ten defense based on success rate (how often teams move the ball against them), they're 25th in defensive EPA per play (geared more toward explosiveness) and 28th in explosive play rate allowed this season. They've given up far too many big passes, and it's taken a major hit to their entire defense.
Now, the first issue seems to be communication, which is why Ryans is taking over. There have been far too many coverage busts in the secondary for a unit as talented as the Texans. This play against the Cowboys is a good example. The Cowboys are running a deep crosser for WR Ceedee Lamb , with WR George Pickens running a clear-out route. The Texans are running Cover 3, but CB Derek Stingley Jr is trying to pass off the crossing route of Lamb to S Calen Bullock , because he has a better angle on it. Bullock, however, sticks with Pickens' deep clear-out route, and Lamb runs wide open.
A good example of how the Cowboys' receiver duo complements each other so well. Lamb running a deep crosser, and the Texans want to try and pass the routes off and cut off the crosser, but Pickens' vertical route occupies both defenders leaving the route open pic.twitter.com/BzXE8WoMNi
On the play that would set up the eventual game-winning touchdown for the Cowboys, CB Kamari Lassiter bites on a sluggo from Pickens, and S Reed Blankenship gets too sucked into the middle of the field. That leaves a void for QB Dak Prescott to find Pickens for a big play. Lassiter and Blankenship (both good players) have had rough starts to the season. Lassiter has especially been picked on in the passing game, giving up a 110.4 passer rating when in coverage.
#DoubleDakDime , with some Pickens coolness added too pic.twitter.com/cWwHLaymiW
While it hasn't been great for the secondary, I definitely think that's fixable. What might not be fixable is their run game, which looks awful once again. After investing a lot in the offseason in revamping the offensive line and running back room, the Texans' run game is…worse than it was last year through four games.
The unit is averaging -0.15 EPA/rush, a 32.9% rushing success rate (excluding scrambles) and a paltry 3.5 yards per carry. The entire goal of this offense was for the run game to help grind teams down so Stroud doesn't have to carry the entire offense, and so far, the Texans' run game hasn't held up its part of the bargain. The idea of condensing formations and being a ground-and-pound team is great in theory, but the Texans find themselves running into a wall — literally — and asking CJ Stroud to save them from themselves.
Now, if there's a silver lining to the season so far, it's been that Stroud has been HOOPIN to start the season. Stroud is 11th in EPA per dropback and 13th in dropback success rate, looking more like the player we saw in 2023 than the guy we saw in 2024 and 2025. His pocket movement has improved significantly, and his elite ball placement has remained. This touchdown to Nico Collins was just exquisite QB play.
Good player pic.twitter.com/bsFealZUno
Do I think the Texans are cooked for this season? I'm choosing to hold on a little bit longer. All of their losses have been one-score losses, and the QB is playing at a high level right now. Once the secondary resolves its communication issues, the defense should pick up again. A 0-4 start is a steep hill to climb out of, but I think the Texans can get out of it.
author: JP Acosta

title: Mike Ditka, Hall of Fame tight end and Bears' Super Bowl-winning coach, dies at age 86
summary: Ditka was a fixture in the NFL for more than 50 years
full_text:
Mike Ditka, a Hall of Fame tight end and the coach of the Chicago Bears ' only Super Bowl championship team, has died at the age of 86, his family announced on Friday.
Ditka's long list of accomplishments includes being a member of both the College and Pro Football Hall of Fame, the 1961 NFL Rookie of the Year and a two-time NFL Coach of the Year. The first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, Ditka's No. 89 has been retired by the Bears.
"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka," his family said in a statement . "While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family.
"Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever."
Ditka was raised in Aliquippa, Pennsylvania, the same area that produced fellow Hall of Famers Tony Dorsett, Ty Law and Darrelle Revis . He went to the University of Pittsburgh, aspiring to be a dentist. It quickly became clear, however, that football would become Ditka's chosen profession.
Mike Ditka - Pittsburgh Panthers RIP 💔 1939-2026 pic.twitter.com/hq7L3GJ4sY
Following a decorated college career (he averaged a whopping 24.3 yards per catch at Pitt), Ditka was taken with the fifth overall pick in the 1961 NFL Draft. That season, he became the first tight end in NFL history to go over 1,000 yards receiving.
Ditka led the Bears to the 1963 NFL title and later helped the Cowboys capture their first title at the end of the 1971 season. He caught a touchdown pass from Roger Staubach during Dallas' 24-3 win over Miami in Super Bowl VI.
Happy 86th Birthday, "Iron Mike"! Mike Ditka Highlights from the #Bears ' 1963 NFL Championship season — the legendary tight end's first as an AP First-Team All-Pro #DaBears pic.twitter.com/H38CRVDDwz
After retiring as a player, Ditka joined Tom Landry's staff as the Cowboys' special teams and receivers coach. He won a second Super Bowl in that role at the end of the 1977 season.
In 1982, Ditka returned to Chicago to become the Bears' coach. Just three years after landing the job, Ditka helped lead the Bears to an 18-1 record that concluded with a 46-10 win over the Patriots in Super Bowl XX.
In Chicago, Ditka enjoyed a successful (albeit at times volatile) working relationship with legendary defensive coordinator Buddy Ryan, who was the architect of the Bears' vaunted 46 defense. Fittingly, both men were carried off the field following Chicago's victory over New England.
"The '85 beers would not have been the '85 beers without Buddy Bryan," Ditka said in 2018 shortly after Ryan's passing. "We won the Super Bowl because of our defense. I mean, you'd have to be a fool to say otherwise. We had great players on offense, and Walter Payton and Willie Gault and some of the other guys we had, and we had a wonderful offensive line. But our defense is why we won."
Ditka's success as the Bears' coach made him an icon in the Windy City. He was imitated often on Saturday Night Live, where he was affectionately referred to as "Da Coach." Bears fans embraced his tough, rugged demeanor that fit Chicago's blue-collar spirit like a glove.
Happy 85th, Mike Ditka! Classic "Iron Mike" from his coaching days with the #Bears and #Saints pic.twitter.com/cO0PDhQt1P
Ditka coached the Bears for 11 years before getting into broadcasting in 1993. He briefly returned to the sidelines with the Saints in 1997. His tenure in New Orleans is largely remembered for trading each of the team's 1999 NFL Draft picks to Washington in exchange for the No. 1 overall pick. The Saints used that pick to draft Ricky Williams, the reigning Heisman Trophy Winner.
Ditka returned to broadcasting following his run in New Orleans (and in 2005, starred alongside Will Ferrell in the movie "Kicking and Screaming") but had kept a low profile in recent years. In 2020, he was at the Super Bowl as part of the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Misunderstood Shedeur Sanders opens up on public perception as Browns QB: 'Why would people think this?'
summary: What the second-year quarterback told Cosmopolitan this week about how he's viewed nationally
full_text:
Shedeur Sanders hasn't been in the spotlight this season due to the Browns ' 3-1 start with Deshaun Watson as Cleveland's starter , and it sounds like he's fine with taking a backseat to media scrutiny for the first time in his career.
In a wide-ranging interview this week with Cosmopolitan that was conducted earlier this summer, Sanders said he's still coming to grips with being routinely misjudged by the public.
"I wish people understood me more as a human being," Sanders said. "I don't think a lot of people really know me. I'm just now starting to understand that. You hear a lot of things online, but every encounter I have in person, people end up saying, 'Oh, wow, he's actually a great guy.' Why would you think I'm a bad guy?
"So I've been looking at things a lot more lately, like, 'Why would people think this?' It's not something I'm going to put (solely) on myself, but I do want to fix that. I want to connect with more people, so they can meet me and see the truth."
Sanders told the magazine he "lives" in his own world and can't remember the last time he has looked at social media banter surrounding his play, Cleveland's quarterback situation or anything relating to football.
The pre-draft experience for Sanders and his rollercoaster first 1.5 seasons in the NFL is well-documented. His brother streamed much of his NFL Draft party in April 2025, which included the raw emotion and initial shock of being skipped over for Louisville's Tyler Shough at No. 40 overall in the second round, along with a prank call impersonating New Orleans Saints general manager Mickey Loomis .
Later came the reports of Sanders sandbagging certain interviews , deciding not to throw at the combine and how he handled the process, all directly affecting his draft slide.
Sanders has tried to explain the misinterpretations surrounding him before. Prior to his rookie season last fall in the NFL, Sanders attributed "99% of hatred" directed at him toward his father, Colorado coach and Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders.
"I'm just his son, but (the kids) didn't grow up in an era to where they watched him play," Shedeur Sanders said during a 2025 interview with Cleveland.com after he was picked in the fifth round. "It's just the older generation that does it to me rather than the younger people. Because when I come in person, there's no negativity I see. But it's all over online."
While the Browns would reportedly "welcome a deal" for the right price involving Sanders or Dillon Gabriel since they have four quarterbacks on the roster, nothing appears imminent ahead of next month's NFL trade deadline.
Browns insider Mary Kay Cabot said Thursday, " anything can happen over the next three weeks " before stressing the franchise would be okay with keeping its deep quarterback room as is.
Sanders battled with Watson throughout camp and the preseason before first-year coach Todd Monken ultimately went with the former first-rounder.
Sanders has made appearances in two games this season, including one pass thrown against the Carolina Panthers in Week 3. In eight games last fall as a first-year player, Sanders completed 120-of-212 pass attempts for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
Monken said Wednesday he was "looking forward" to seeing Gabriel back on the field following his return from injured reserve. He's expected to push Sanders for the No. 2 spot behind Watson moving forward.
The Browns, who are in a first-place tie in the AFC North with Baltimore, play the Jets in New York on Sunday, hoping to move out front.
author: Brad Crawford

title: Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels orchestrates wild upset of Cowboys in second career start
summary: The undrafted Kansas product is making history in place of the injured Baker Mayfield
full_text:
Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels has quickly become one of the most fun stories of the 2026 NFL season. When Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield was sidelined by a dislocated thumb, Todd Bowles called upon the first-year player out of Kansas to lead his winless team.
Daniels made his first career start against the Green Bay Packers in Week 4, and hung around in a 17-14 loss. However, he became a national storyline by upsetting Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5 , 24-16.
It was the largest upset of the NFL season thus far, as the Bucs were 9.5-point underdogs. Daniels, on the other hand, became the third undrafted rookie quarterback since 1970 to win a primetime road game, and the first undrafted rookie quarterback to beat the Cowboys since Jake Delhomme did so in 1999, per CBS Sports Research.
Who is this fun quarterback that already looks so comfortable as an NFL starter? Let's take a look at who Jalon Daniels is.
Daniels was born in Lawndale, California, and attended Lawndale High School. As a recruit, 247Sports ranked him as a three-star prospect, the No. 61 dual-threat athlete in the country, and No. 298 overall player from the state of California. Daniels initially committed to Middle Tennessee State, but later decommitted and pledged allegiance to the Jayhawks.
Daniels was one of three Kansas quarterbacks who appeared during the season opener in 2020, which was played in an empty stadium due to the coronavirus pandemic. He got the start for his second collegiate game, and completed 19 of 33 passes for 159 yards while also rushing for 23 yards in a 47-14 loss to Baylor. Daniels was just 17 years old at the time.
It was a tough season for Daniels and the Jayhawks, as Kansas finished with a 0-9 record. The true freshman completed 50% of his passes for 718 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions in seven games played with six starts.
Kansas named Jason Bean its new starting quarterback for the 2021 season, but an injury forced Daniels back into the lineup. That first start came against the hated Texas Longhorns -- who were around 30-point favorites against Kansas. Daniels led the Jayhawks to a thrilling 57-56 upset victory in overtime, in which he threw for 202 yards, three touchdowns, and rushed for 45 yards and another touchdown.
Daniels showed off his ability as a magician on the game-winning two-point conversion.
Kansas beats Texas 57-56 on a crazy 2-point conversion in overtime! 🏈 pic.twitter.com/IJy6KZWjqL
Daniels was named the starter for the 2022 season, which was his junior year. Kansas started hot, winning its first five games before eventually falling to a ranked TCU team. Overall, the Jayhawks tallied their most victories in a single season (6) since 2008, while Daniels threw for 2,014 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions.
Entering 2023, Daniels was named the Big 12 Preseason Offensive Player of the Year. The college football world was prepared to embrace him as the lovable legend of Lawrence, but a nagging back injury suffered prior to the start of the campaign held Daniels to just three games. Even without Daniels, Kansas went 9-4 and won its first bowl game in 15 years. Running back Devin Neal emerged as a star, rushing for 1,280 yards and 16 touchdowns that year.
Daniels announced on Nov. 16, 2023 , that he would be returning to Kansas for what would be his redshirt junior season in 2024.
"I'm going to be blunt. This season didn't go as planned," Daniels said. "But life comes at you fast, and sometimes your story's out of your control. But I guess that just means I have unfinished business. My dreams haven't changed, my goals are still there, and my vision for my future is clear. So you want something to talk about? Talk about this: I'm not done yet, and I'm not going anywhere. Rock Chalk."
Kansas had a rough start to the year, losing six of its first eight games. However, the Jayhawks rebounded to beat three ranked teams in a row in Iowa State, BYU and Colorado. Daniels threw for 2,454 yards, 14 touchdowns and a career-high 12 interceptions, but also recorded a career-high 439 yards rushing and six touchdowns.
Daniels then returned for his sixth year at Kansas thanks to COVID-19 and injury waivers.
"It's all about finishing where you started," Daniels told CBS Sports prior to the 2025 season. "I went to multiple high schools. I went to multiple middle schools. Kansas gave me a chance when no other Power Five school in the nation gave me a chance, and I feel like that has a big part to do with it."
Daniels registered his second-straight 5-7 season, and threw for a career-high 2,531 yards, a career-high 22 touchdowns and seven interceptions.
"My Kansas journey has kind of been just like my life; it's come with a lot of ups and downs, and it hasn't been easy at all," Daniels said. "When I felt like I've been performing at my greatest, trials and tribulations such as injuries have come about. It's always just been about being able to bounce back from it."
Daniels' Kansas story didn't go or end how everyone wanted it to. While he flashed star potential, he left Lawrence with a 19-26 record and questions about his future as a football player.
Daniels finished his collegiate career ranked second in program history in passing yards (9,282) and passing touchdowns (67), and was one of two Jayhawks to ever accumulate 10,000 yards of total offense , joining Todd Reesing. Draft pundits criticized his throwing mechanics, accuracy, and ability to diagnose coverages, but what he could do as a scrambler was enticing. It all led to Daniels going undrafted, but he found an opportunity with the Buccaneers.
In Tampa, Mayfield was established as the starter, and he had Jake Browning as a new No. 2. Browning was once viewed as a top backup in the NFL , as he won four of seven starts with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023. However, Daniels found a way to unseat him. The rookie completed 61.4% of his passes for 239 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in three preseason games played and also rushed for 37 yards and another touchdown to earn a spot on the final 53-man roster.
Then, in Week 4, Daniels was presented with a massive opportunity.
From being an underrated recruit out of California, to the ups and downs at Kansas and his victorious fight to earn a roster spot on an NFL team , Daniels was about to start multiple games for the Buccaneers.
"I think that one thing I learned in college was, you can't be the thermometer, you have to be the thermostat," Daniels said ahead of his first NFL start. "You have to be someone who comes in and is able to set the temperature of the room, not test the room and try to be able to blend in with it. If a team is low, I have to be able to pick it up to be able to make sure that they're even. If we're high, then I have to be able to be low to be able to make sure that we're even. I try to be as even-keel as possible. I think that being able to go out there and have that even-keeled feel, the team around you feels that."
In Week 4, Daniels became the first Kansas quarterback to start a game since Frank Seurer in 1987, and the first undrafted rookie quarterback to start a game in Buccaneers history. title: NFL Week 5 schedule: A look at three underrated games you should watch, including a rare matchup
summary: A look at some of the less talked-about games of the week
full_text:
It's Week 5 of the 2026 NFL regular season, and we have another exciting slate of games, plus some under-the-radar matchups I think everyone should be paying more attention to. Last week, all three of my underrated games turned out to be worth a watch.
First, in one of my highlighted games of the week, we saw one of the few remaining undefeated teams get handed their first L, when the Las Vegas Raiders lost to the Kansas City Chiefs in a close divisional battle.
Another of my underrated games was the battle between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Rams , which turned out to be a close game, with the Rams pulling off a near-impossible comeback to win 24-20.
The third and final of my spotlighted games last week was the game that put the New York Giants in first place in the NFC East for the first time since 2015.
So now it's once again that time to dive into why some of the less talked-about contests should be on your radar.
Sunday, Oct. 11 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox, stream on fubo
The Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers are two of the oldest franchises with one of the most storied rivalries in NFL history, which always makes this one a good watch. The rivalry has certainly changed over the years, and I'm intrigued by how it will continue to evolve in this era of the teams.
Both teams have their long-term answer at QB in Jordan Love for the Packers and Caleb Williams for the Bears, so this new-look rivalry should only get more interesting as these two continue to see each other more.
This week, however, the Bears' side will have a different player at the helm, with Williams still out due to a hamstring injury. Chicago has been a fascinating team to watch this season. With their win against the New York Jets last week, they became the first NFL team in 30 years to win three games in the first four weeks of the season with three different quarterbacks.
If you told me the Bears would start Caleb Williams, Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent and only one of those QBs would record a loss through the first four weeks, I would be shocked to find out Williams was the one with an L. Head coach Ben Johnson has shown he can operate his offense regardless of who is throwing passes and I'm curious whether that will be kept up against the 2-2 Packers, who have home field advantage.
Sunday, Oct. 11 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox, stream on fubo
The Minnesota Vikings are one of three undefeated teams remaining in the league, but you wouldn't necessarily know it from their numbers. Their offense needs work, having scored only one touchdown in the last three games and ranking last in passing yards (709).
The 1-3 New Orleans Saints are coming off an ugly loss to the resurgent Atlanta Falcons and will be looking to erase the memory of that 45-24 defeat. The Saints don't have much longer to get things together and turn their season around, so they could have an extra boost against a Vikings team that isn't without cracks.
These teams are very different in their strengths and weaknesses, which I expect will make for an interesting matchup. Both have major things to work on, and while it may seem like the Vikings can give up a loss with less of a hit than the Saints could, their divisions make that conversation a bit more nuanced. The Vikings are just ahead of the 3-1 Bears, and the 2-2 Packers and Detroit Lions are capable teams as of late, while the AFC South tends to be a division with more struggle. The Panthers and Falcons have the best record at 2-2 each, and while they're playing well, they haven't proven consistency in the past. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 1-4 after Thursday's win over the Cowboys.
New Orleans could see itself tied for the best record in their division with a win this week, which seems surprising, considering it is going into the game with just one win.
Sunday, Oct. 11 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
OK, you may think you're reading a misprint here, or that I've completely lost the plot putting two winless teams in my underrated games of the week, but hear me out. It's not that often you get the chance five weeks into the season to see a matchup, and a divisional matchup at that, with two 0-4 teams going against each other. This is only the seventh 0-4 matchup in the Super Bowl era, and who doesn't love watching history?
Of the five teams without a check in the win column, these two just happen to both be in the AFC South and happen to be facing each other this weekend, what luck! Both teams are in desperation mode, and one of these teams has to win. Right? Right ...
The Texans record isn't a reflection of how their games have gone. They came within five points of the Buffalo Bills in Week 2, lost by two to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 3 and lost by four to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4. They are a few bounces of the football away from a 3-1 record.
The Titans also had close games in three of their losses. They fell 24-20 to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2, 12-7 to the New York Giants in Week 3 and 24-18 to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4.
I am curious to see which team will finally close out the game and whether it becomes a turning point.
