title: Just how embarrassing was Dallas' loss to the Bucs? What went wrong and where Cowboys go from here
summary: Dallas blew a golden chance to position themselves to capitalize on a weakened NFC East vs. the winless Bucs
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys (2-3) blew a golden opportunity to position themselves as the team to beat in the NFC East after gifting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) their first win of the season in a 24-16 "Thursday Night Football" defeat. This defeat takes the cake as the most head-scratching loss of the short Brian Schottenheimer era, losing at home as a 9.5-point favorite against a winless squad with a backup quarterback. As Dallas trudged off their home field, a chorus of boos rang throughout the 100,000-seat AT&T Stadium like it was the Haunted Mansion.
It was so baffling that someone yelled "embarrassing" at Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott as he walked through the bowels of the stadium to the locker room by himself postgame.
"It's a loss we're supposed to have, definitely supposed to have. To use the word embarrassing — it's tough," Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott said. "I feel like I'm discrediting the NFL if I use that [the word embarrassing] and particularly the Tampa Bay Bucs, the great Todd Bowles. … [But] when a winless team comes into your home stadium on a Thursday night primetime game, yeah, we're supposed to win that."
All the Cowboys had to do to get a winning streak going after a road win at the Houston Texans in Week 4 was take care of business at home against a previously 0-4 Buccaneers team. The Bucs entered Week 5 with 16 sacks allowed (the most in the league and the team's most through four games since 1991), nine turnovers (the third-most in the NFL) and a negative-5 turnover differential (tied for the second-worst in the NFL).
Dallas only had to play a clean game at home, and it would be 3-2 with a 10-day layoff until its next game at the Green Bay Packers on "Sunday Night Football" on Oct. 18. Instead, the Cowboys are 2-3 and looked like a team that was playing their third game in 12 days, with the sloppiness and lack of execution in all three phases of the game, particularly on defense.
The 2026 Cowboys are now the third team since 1940 to allow 375-plus total yards (419 on Thursday) without an interception in five straight games within a season. Since Dallas did so in five consecutive games to begin a season, it's the longest such streak to begin a year, per CBS Sports Research. When asked by CBS Sports how Jones would evaluate new defensive coordinator Christian Parker's work through the first five games, Jones said he didn't even want to discuss the topic.
"Well, I don't want to go there at all," Jones said. "We did all the [wrong] things to get that score to end up like it was, and I thought we had the team that could get out of here with a win. So it's very disappointing. … I feel that he's competent."
The miscues were most glaring on defense, where the Cowboys were facing undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels , making his second career start. On the Buccaneers' opening drive, the Cowboys committed three defensive penalties that helped Tampa Bay go on a 15-play, 73-yard scoring drive that tied the game at 7-7 early.
Tampa Bay's drive lasted 10:58, the longest drive the franchise has had since 2007, and it also ranked as the second-longest drive by any team in "Thursday Night Football" history, per CBS Sports Research. Daniels completed all eight of his throws for 49 yards, including a five-yard touchdown pass. That tied the most pass attempts without an incompletion on any drive by a Buccaneers quarterback in the last 35 seasons.
Following that drive, Dallas' offense lost the rhythm it had on its touchdown drive to begin the game, punting on its next three possessions while its defense struggled to get off the field.
"Yeah, it's no fun, but it's the NFL. It's not an excuse," Prescott said. "There was so much simple in that first drive, and I think after [the Buccaneers] said, 'OK, we're going to throw the kitchen sink at these guys.' And it worked."
After the Cowboys entered the locker room with a 10-7 lead, the wheels came off the Dallas defense's collective wagon. Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving juked seemingly the entire Cowboys' front seven at the line of scrimmage before taking his first carry of the second half 72 yards. Tampa wide receiver Emeka Egbuka scored on a 14-yard end-around on the very next play for a touchdown. Forget needing 11 minutes, the Cowboys allowed Tampa Bay to score their second touchdown in just two plays.
Irving finished with a career-high 165 yards rushing and a touchdown on 21 carries for a 7.9 yards per carry average. Entering Thursday, he had averaged just 59.2 rushing yards per game across the last two seasons.
"The thing that probably bothers me the most was how they ran between the tackles so to speak and were able to have that running game up in there where we have a lot of strength [ Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark ]," said owner and general manager Jerry Jones . "That's something that we have to look at and will."
Bucky Irving out and running! @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tLym5RtEYd
Another play just as embarrassing as giving up Irving's 72-yard run: A coverage bust allowed Buccaneers wide receiver Tez Johnson to spring free deep down the sideline for a 64-yard completion to the Dallas 15. Cornerback DaRon Bland, who was pressed back into the boundary corner spot because new corner Joey Porter Jr . fell ill with flu-like symptoms, slipped on Johnson's double move on the play. Three plays later, Irving was in the end zone again.
By the end of the night, Daniels finished with 189 yards and a touchdown on 19-of-25 passing for a 110.2 passer rating to cap off the third-largest upset win by an undrafted rookie quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger, per CBS Sports Research.
Tez Johnson is WIDE open for another Bucs big gain! @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yilGqjeFzj
Don't get us wrong: It wasn't just the defense that fell short for the Cowboys. The offense and special teams units had their own contribution to the Cowboys' misery. After the kickoff following Irving's third-quarter touchdown, Pro Bowl return man KaVontae Turpin fumbled the football right back to the Buccaneers, which allowed Tampa Bay to begin its next drive at the Cowboys' 37.
Young edge rushers Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence combined to sack Jalon Daniels for a loss of 11 on the first play from scrimmage. However, on third-and-21, Dallas surrendered a 21-yard pass from Daniels to Emeka Egbuka to move the chains. The Cowboys' defense then locked in, allowing just three points on the drive, a 41-yard field goal that put them down 24-10 in the third quarter.
Soon after, facing a fourth-and-3 at Dallas' 43, Prescott missed an open George Pickens along the sideline on a fourth-and-3 incompletion to Jake Ferguson . It looked like Prescott was predetermined to throw the second he snapped the ball because of Todd Bowles' pressure package. Prescott chalked up his misfire in that moment — and on the throws that led to two tipped-ball interceptions — as decision-making, not fatigue.
Surprisingly, Dallas defense stuffed Buccaneers running back Sean Tucker 's fourth-and-goal run from the one to get the Cowboys the ball back down two scores with 8:32 left — plenty of time to come back at home. Prescott delivered with an 18-yard precision strike to Pickens, who broke out with a season-high 130 yards receiving and a touchdown on nine catches, to trim the lead to eight. A failed two-point conversion play kept the margin there.
Prescott got the ball back one more time, but tight end Jake Ferguson tipped the ball into the air on a tight window throw, allowing Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone to intercept the pass. That sealed the upset victory for Tampa Bay's first win of the year. Prescott finished with 316 yards passing, a touchdown and two interceptions while completing 24 of 42 throws.
After three straight 12-win seasons from 2021 to 2023, the Cowboys have been mired in mediocrity. In 2024, Dallas went 7-10 with Prescott sidelined…

There are a few showers early with overcast skies later in the day. High 72F. Winds W at 10 to 15 mph. Chance of rain 30%. At -7.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook , there is split ATS action. That the rebuilding Titans are winless is not a surprise, but that the Texans are is a shocker. Believe it or not, this marks the NFL's first matchup of 0-4 or worse clubs since 2019 when 0-4 Miami lost 17-16 at home to 0-5 Washington. It's the first divisional game between 0-4 or worse teams since 2004 between Miami and Buffalo.
Many expected the Titans to take a jump this season with a new coaching staff led by head coach Robert Saleh and offensive coordinator Brian Daboll. Tennessee had won just three games in each of the past two years and had a preseason 2026 win total of 6.5 with the Over a slight favorite. That's pretty clearly landing Under now, and the updated win total is 4.5 with the Under at -145.
To be the NFL's last winless team, the Titans are +370 third-favorites behind the Dolphins (+150) and Chargers (+300). If Tennessee doesn't win Sunday, it likely won't until at least Week 7 at home against Cleveland. What I'd be fascinated to see is if the Titans get the No. 1 overall pick in a supposedly quarterback-loaded 2027 NFL Draft . Would they give up on 2025 No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward already or take someone like Ohio State wideout Jeremiah Smith to help?
Ward is now 3-18 as an NFL starter, the third QB ever to start 3-18 or worse through 21 games behind Steve DeBerg (2-19) and Troy Aikman (3-18). It obviously all worked out for Aikman in Dallas. Should the Titans get Smith in the next draft, they might all of a sudden have a scary wide receivers room with rookie Carnell Tate already shining.
Tate, the No. 4 overall pick this year out of Ohio State, has 22 catches for 268 yards, with the yardage total the fourth-most in Titans/Oilers history in a player's first four games. That total is 37% of all Titans receiving yardage this season, the fifth-highest such total in the league. Tate has yet to score his first NFL TD and is +425 to get one Sunday.

Houston won double-digit games and reached at least the Divisional Round of the playoffs each of the past three seasons but on Sunday, it could become the first team in league history to follow a 10-game winning streak with a six-game skid – including the playoffs. You may remember the 2025 Texans started 0-3 and 3-5 before winning out in the regular season and then won their playoff opener in Pittsburgh before falling in New England.
The Texans are only the seventh team all-time and first since the 2012 Saints to start 0-4 after at least a 12-win season and the second team to start 0-4 after winning a playoff game in three straight seasons after the 1987 Giants . The 1992 Chargers are the lone team to reach the playoffs following a 0-4 start. In the preseason, Houston was -190 for the playoffs and is now +240, a probability change of minus-40.5%. To be the last winless team, it is the +1500 longshot.
The thing is, DeMeco Ryans ' team isn't far from being 3-1 as it led in the final five minutes in three of its games. Houston is the fourth club in the past 35 years to blow a lead in the final five minutes of three of its first four games. The last to do so was the 2018 Falcons , who finished 7-9. Overall, the Texans have been within one score (eight points or fewer) of their opponent 85% of the time this season. Only the Chiefs have a higher rate.
C.J. Stroud was not signed to a long-term extension before the season and he's playing great, averaging 285.3 passing yards with five pass TDs and zero picks. Those are the fifth-most yards and second-best TD-INT ratio in the league entering Week 5. Stroud's 1,141 passing yards are the seventh-most by a QB on a team to start 0-4. Houston is the first club to start 0-4 without throwing an interception.
The issue has been what was the NFL's No. 1 total and scoring defense last year as the Texans are 0-2 when scoring at least 30 points compared to 10-0 when doing so in Ryans' first three seasons. Houston is tied for 26th in scoring defense at 27.3 PPG after allowing an average of only 20.0 PPG in the first three seasons under Ryans – he announced Wednesday that he would take over defensive play-calling from coordinator Matt Burke.
That unit has already allowed more games with 30+ points this season (two) than last (one). Tennessee hasn't scored 20 points in a game yet and the team total is set at a comically low Over/Under of 14.5 points.
Houston's Pro Bowl cornerback combination of Derek Stingley Jr . and Kamari Lassiter is allowing 9.5 yards per attempt in coverage this year compared to 6.6 in 2025. Tate might have a big day as the Texans have allowed 830 yards to receivers this season, which is second-most in the NFL.
The Texans have won five straight road games in this series, the third-longest active head-to-head divisional road winning streak in the league. Week 5 is usually when the club gets going as it is 18-8 SU and 15-10-1 ATS in Weeks 5-18 over the past three seasons compared to 4-8 SU and 1-11 ATS in Weeks 1-4. Tennessee is on a 10-game divisional losing streak overall, losing by an average of 15.8 points and covering the spread just once.

title: Brian Schottenheimer considers staff changes after Cowboys' loss, Jerry Jones responds to embarrassing loss
summary: What the Dallas coach and owner both said after Thursday night's humiliating home loss to a previously winless team
full_text:
Running out of answers early this season, there was no direct way to explain what happened during the Cowboys' deflating 24-16 home loss to the previously-winless Buccaneers on Thursday night for coach Brian Schottenheimer.
Tampa Bay's decisive 17-point third quarter behind undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and Bucky Irving's first 100-yard outing on the ground in two years put the spotlight on the Cowboys' second-year coach and his 2-3 start this fall.
Schottenheimer hinted at potential coaching staff changes after Dallas collapsed in all three phases of the game following two turnovers from Dak Prescott , struggles defensively and a lost fumble from KaVontae Turpin on a kickoff return.
"I'm going to look at everything," Schottenheimer said. "I'll spend countless hours trying to figure it out and getting a chance to step back, look at these five games, and see what we need to improve. ... Yeah, I think we evaluate everything, but at the end of the day, we're five games in. I am disappointed in the way we performed this evening as a football team, and that's just going to be one part of the process."
The Cowboys trailed 24-10 after the third quarter before a 10-play, 99-yard touchdown drive ending with a Prescott scoring toss to George Pickens , which brought Dallas within a possession with 5:26 left.
After forcing a three-and-out, the Cowboys moved to Tampa Bay's 22-yard line before Prescott's throw over the middle was picked off with 1:22 remaining, ending the threat. The Bucs doubled up the Cowboys in time of possession and rushed for 241 yards — 191 more than the opposition.
"Again, it comes down to this being the National Football League, and it's going to come down to the fourth quarter," Schottenheimer said. "And even with as poorly as we performed, we had a chance to still get back in and try to win the game, and we came up short."
Schottenheimer called the loss a "missed opportunity" after his 12th setback in his first 22 games with the franchise after replacing Mike McCarthy ahead of the 2025 season.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said his team was noticeably dominated at the line of scrimmage, pointing to Irving's production and a weak effort from his offense. Javonte Williams finished with 12 carries for 45 yards and a touchdown as the Cowboys only attempted 13 rushes out of 55 offensive plays.
"Extraordinarily, extraordinarily disappointed," Jones said, via the team's official website . "You really do need to get it done when it's there to take. They basically were very physical. I thought both their fronts, was really surprised at how well they ran the ball, how they ran it between the tackles. That was surprising.
"We thought if they were going to run it, they'd do it outside, and thought we'd put it on the quarterback's shoulders. Their staff, their quarterback, all their players got a great victory here tonight, and it was a tough loss for us."
With no Baker Mayfield , who's out with a hand injury, the Bucs entered the matchup 0-4 and last in the NFC South with one of the league's most anemic offenses.
"Boy, I've been so disappointed before with losses, but this was disappointing," Jones said. "And I'm disappointed because I see potential growth here. And we need to have good experiences on an individual basis as well as a team. And this was not a good experience out here."
Through five games, Dallas is two games back of the Eagles in the NFC East and plays Green Bay next week, a team that has alternated wins and losses this season just like the Cowboys.
author: Brad Crawford

title: Dak Prescott takes issue with 'embarrassing' comment by heckler after Cowboys' loss to Bucs
summary: A detractor prompted a sharp response from Prescott both in the hallway and at the podium
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers earned their first win of the season on Thursday night, as they defeated the Dallas Cowboys , 24-16. It's also fair to say that the Cowboys earned an embarrassing loss.
An undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels , making his second career start, came into AT&T Stadium and helped drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in front of the sports world in primetime. The Cowboys' offense wasn't much better, as Brian Schottenheimer's unit turned the ball over three times in the second half.
After the game, a viral exchange took place between a service driver and quarterback Dak Prescott . As the Cowboys' signal-caller made the quiet walk to the locker room in the bowels of "Jerry World," someone was heard saying, "embarrassing." Prescott then shot a look in that person's direction.
"He heard me," the man said.
"You say that once I look off, huh?" Prescott responded.
Check out what happened, courtesy of Spectrum News 1:
Here’s our angle of a worker — either stadium employee or valet car driver — calling out Dak Prescott and the Cowboys performance, with Dak’s reaction which he said was prompted by the man looking away after saying the criticisms. #dallascowboys #nfl pic.twitter.com/ffznCyahvv
The interaction quickly went viral, forcing Prescott to address it in his postgame press conference.
"Yeah. I mean, not that they're not wrong," Prescott said. "But the thing was I just ... yeah. I don't know if it was an employee, it was a driver, whoever it was, he's free to speak his mind."
Did Prescott feel disrespected by the comment? Did he agree with it?
"When he said it, I just happened to look at him," Prescott said. "And at that point, he looked away, didn't look, and then when I turned my head back, he said something else, and so that's the part that just as a man or as just a person — feel free to speak your mind, just speak it. Don't coward away from the reaction that you're going to get. If you're saying it's embarrassing, say it's embarrassing; if you're saying it to me, then say it to me, you know what I mean? Go back on it. So that's all that was, and hate it that it's even being talked about to be honest with you."
A post shared by NFL on CBS (@nfloncbs)
KDFW Fox 4 reports that the man who made the "embarrassing" comment was a car service driver, and not a stadium employee.
The Cowboys' performance on Thursday night was embarrassing, marking the largest upset of the 2026 NFL season thus far. Dallas was favored by 9.5 points over a previously winless team starting a backup quarterback, yet was outplayed in virtually every facet of the game.
The Buccaneers outrushed the Cowboys 241 yards to 50 yards; outgained the Cowboys 419 yards to 366; did better on third downs (7-of-13 compared to 4-of-10); won the turnover battle, 3-0; and dominated time of possession 39:21 to 20:39. The Cowboys don't look like a team capable of making the playoffs, and the defense is still one of the worst in the NFL .

title: Week 5 NFL bold predictions: Bijan Robinson makes NFL primetime history, struggling Packers upset Bears
summary: Plus, the Dolphins finally get more points on the board and other bold predictions for Week 5
full_text:
Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 5 of the 2026 season certainly reminded us all of that.
The Dallas Cowboys (2-3) entered their "Thursday Night Football" home game against the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) as 9.5-point home favorites. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was making his second career NFL start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and the Buccaneers pulled off the third-largest upset win by an undrafted rookie quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger in a 24-16 victory .
What other craziness could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 5 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions.
For the first time since their 2006 NFC title season, the Chicago Bears (3-1) are favored at Lambeau Field over the Green Bay Packers (2-2). This snaps a 19-game streak of visits to Lambeau in which the Bears were the underdog.
It makes sense why this has finally shifted. Chicago won two of its three matchups in the 2024 season, including the last two on miraculous comebacks that required rallies from double-digit deficits in both Week 16 and the opening round of the postseason.
This season, the Bears lead the NFL in total offense (429.0 total yards per game), rushing offense (196.3), and first down offense (25.3 first downs per game) despite quarterback Caleb Williams going down midway through Week 2. Even the defense has picked up the slack, allowing the fewest points per game (9.3) in the entire league since Week 2.
On the flip side, the Packers' offense is struggling. They're dead last in rushing yards per game (58.0), nearly 20 yards fewer than the Bengals ' 74.3 rushing yards per game. Because of that inability to run the ball with the litany of offensive line injuries they've had, Green Bay's unbalanced offense ranks 28th in scoring (18.3 points per game) and dead last in third down efficiency (26.1% conversion rate.
However, the Packers will upset the Bears behind a masterful performance from Jordan Love . Here's how it will happen. Week 5 is shaping up to be the Green Bay debut of Pro Bowl right guard Kevin Zeitler , whom the Packers signed last week. With Zeitler and new left guard Laken Tomlinson looking down the interior of the pocket, Love will have time to shred the Bears' secondary. The last time he faced them in the wild card round loss in January, he threw for 323 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Love will put together another line like that in Week 5 and lead the Packers to victory over their hated rivals.
Only two players in NFL history have run for 140-plus rushing yards in three consecutive primetime games: the league's all-time leading rusher, Emmitt Smith (1993-1994 and in 1995), and Atlanta Falcons All-Pro Bijan Robinson .
His streak began in Week 17 last season when he erupted for 195 yards and a touchdown (93 yards) on 22 carries in a 27-24 victory over the Los Angeles Rams on "Monday Night Football." Fast forward to Week 3 this season, and he decimated the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field with 194 yards rushing and two rushing touchdowns on 29 carries on "Thursday Night Football." In Week 4, he bullied the New Orleans Saints in their 20th anniversary of the reopening of the Superdome on "Monday Night Football" with 145 yards rushing and two rushing touchdowns on 19 carries, including a 59-yard scoring sprint on his first run of the night.
Now, Robinson is looking to go for 140 yards rushing for a fourth primetime game in a row, something no one has yet accomplished in the league. He'll face a stout Baltimore Ravens run defense that is allowing the 10th-fewest rushing yards per game (100.0) in the league this season. They certainly get plenty of reps in practice against an elite running back in Derrick Henry , but he's much more of a bruiser at his size (6-foot-3, 252 pounds) and age (32 years old) than the more elusive Robinson (5-foot-11, 215 pounds at 24 years old).
The difference in style between the two will be too much for Baltimore to handle, and Robinson will rush for over 140 yards once again.
Pittsburgh Steelers four-time All-Pro edge rusher T.J. Watt is set to celebrate his 32nd birthday on Sunday in Week 5. Watt's 4.5 sacks this season are tied for the third most in the league with Will Anderson Jr. , and his 119.5 career sacks are tied for the fourth most by a player prior to turning 32 in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research.
Watt won't secure that record, but he will break the record for the most sacks on a player's birthday in NFL history against Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones . The record is 2.0, which has been done many times, but no one has done three. The last time Watt registered at least three sacks in a game was back in 2023 against the San Francisco 49ers , when he sacked Brock Purdy three times in Week 1.
He'll accomplish that feat against a struggling Jones, who has four total touchdowns to seven turnovers this season. He hasn't been the easiest to sack this season: Jones' eight sacks taken are tied for the 12th-fewest in the league entering Week 5. However, Watt will find some extra juice on his birthday to set the league's all-time birthday sack record with three.
Despite the New York Giants being 3-1 after quarterback Jaxson Dart went down, that doesn't mean fill-in Jameis Winston is lighting the world on fire. In fact, it's kind of the opposite with Winston ranking dead last in the league in completion percentage (55.1%).
However, Winston will register his first game with a completion percentage of 70% or higher since the 2021 season on Sunday against the Washington Commanders . Washington is allowing the third-most points per game (30.5), the eighth-most passing yards per game, and the fifth-highest passer rating (106.8) in the NFL this season. They also blitz a lot. New Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones worked under Brian Flores with the Minnesota Vikings , and like Flores, he is aggressive. Minnesota leads the league in blitz rate at 71.2%, and Jones' Washington defense ranks second at 46.4%.
Winston is just 11-for-22 when blitzed this season for 83 yards and an interception, but he'll get the ball out quickly to produce his most efficient game he's had since his 2021 season with the New Orleans Saints.
The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly how one would expect for a squad paying more for players not on their roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than the players on their roster ($156 million). They're 0-4 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 11.5 points per game.
Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis has a hard knock life trying to quarterback a Miami Dolphins team that entered the year with Jalen Tolbert as the roster's career receiving yards leader. With a supporting cast like that, it's no wonder the 2026 Dolphins are the first team since the 2019 "Tank for Tua" Dolphins to score fewer than 14 points in each of the first four games of the season.
That puts Miami in a position to avoid becoming the fifth team since 1950 to have fewer than 14 points in each of its first five games. But the Dolphins are going to score at least 14 points against Cincinnati on Sunday. How? Well, the Bengals are the NFL's second-worst rushing offense, averaging 74.3 rushing yards per game. Defending the Bengals simply involves defending their passing game, and both Ja'Mar Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) aren't healthy. The Dolphins will be able to wear out the Bengals defense because Cincinnati's offense won't be able to sustain drives with Higgins and Chase hurt.
Then, Willis will strike for a couple of touchdowns, and Miami will break 14 points for the first time in 2026.

summary: Plus ranking every NBA team's offense for the 2026-27 season
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .

As shot selection and shot-making continue to steadily improve, there is a strong chance the 2026-27 season will deliver even more growth on that end of the floor. If that comes to fruition, which team will best exemplify offensive expertise? There are a number of capable squads.
Our Sam Quinn ranked all 30 offenses ahead of the season , and there are a few teams in the top 10 that stand out considering where they finished last year. These lineups could be in for a huge step forward:
7. 76ers (2025-26 offensive ranking: No. 16) 9. Pacers (25-26: No. 28) 10. Jazz (25-26: No. 22)
On the other hand, not all of last year's elite shooting teams will replicate their success. We're not predicting huge declines for the Nuggets , Celtics and the like, but after it led the league in offensive rating a season ago, we think Denver could be in for a hint of regression.
Still, Quinn is not buying a complete downfall for the Nuggets. Nikola Jokić alone is enough to keep them at No. 5 in the preseason rankings.
Week 5 is already off to a topsy-turvy start. The Cowboys were more than a touchdown favorite against the Buccaneers and lost on "Thursday Night Football." Who's the next team to fall victim to an upset? Our Tyler Sullivan named a few candidates , and the most striking are the Lions , who hold a 5.5-point edge over the Cardinals .
Sullivan says it would not shock him if Jacoby Brissett throws for 350 yards against the hapless Detroit defense. It also would not surprise him if the 49ers pull off a modest upset of the Seahawks to establish themselves as the clear Super Bowl favorites. And he's not alone. Our Jordan Dajani is also taking San Francisco straight up as a road underdog .
One favorite that should feel confident, though, is Jacksonville. The Jaguars are touchdown favorites over the Eagles in London, and nobody foresees any funny business in the international contest. These teams are trending in opposite directions , and our Jared Dubin says they are two full tiers apart on the NFL ladder .
First-year coach Bob Chesney brought more than wins to UCLA . And if you don't already know Wayne Knight , get ready to meet him when the No. 21 Bruins battle No. 13 Oregon tomorrow at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. The top-25 Big Ten showdown is among the most impactful matchups in the College Football Playoff picture in Week 6 because, believe it or not, UCLA actually has a more compelling CFP résumé than Oregon .
Still, the Ducks are 11.5-point favorites. Our experts are torn on how this one will play out. David Cobb likes the Ducks to cover the double-digit spread . Brad Crawford put Oregon on upset alert . So maybe you should stay away from predicting which team will win and simply bank on this being a low-scoring game. That's how Tom Fornelli is approaching it in his weekly Six Pack of picks .
In the SEC, there is an even more highly ranked game this weekend. No. 2 Georgia travels to No. 6 Alabama in a game that could decide who becomes the top-ranked team in the land. We took a position-by-position look at the matchup , and you might be surprised to learn who has the quarterback edge. The Bulldogs are in better shape than you may realize .

title: NFL Week 5 best bets: Backing the Bears, Texans and a touchdown prop for Davante Adams
summary: The Texans are due, the Bears have a favorable matchup, and a handful of player props stand out as value plays heading into Week 5
full_text:
It was a good Week 4. Not a great Week 4, but a good one.
We went 3-2 on best bets, nailing both game picks. The Cowboys beat the Texans as slight road underdogs, and the Jaguars , also slight road underdogs, beat the Bengals . Those were two bold calls, and both games came down to the final possession, but I was glad to be on the right side. Sometimes you gotta be bold. We also cashed in on Kirk Cousins 1+ interception, and that one also came down to, quite literally, the Raiders ' final offensive play. Better late than never!
My two misses were frustrating ones. I pegged Josh Downs to record 5+ receptions and 50+ yards against the struggling Commanders secondary. Neither happened as Daniel Jones continued his season-long turnover woes with a fumble and an interception. When Washington had to turn to third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis , the Colts took control and barely had to throw the ball. Furthermore, we missed on Aaron Jones Sr. 50+ rushing yards and anytime touchdown scorer. He ran for 94 yards but didn't find the end zone. In fact, the Vikings ' offense has only had one touchdown over the past three weeks. I'm thinking we've gotta stay away from any positive Minnesota offensive production, at least for another week or two.
I'll keep saying it: The more we learn, the better we should do. That played out with our best week yet. Let's keep that trajectory.
As always, all betting odds are courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
You might think that the Titans held up OK against the Ravens last week, only losing 24-18. That wouldn't be the case. It was 24-7 at halftime, and only a Lamar Jackson injury prevented this one from being a complete laugher. The Titans haven't lost by multiple possessions once -- back in Week 1 -- so that's another reason this line is where it is.
But I very much believe we're going to see a Texans blowout here. The Texans are 0-4. DeMeco Ryans took defensive play-calling duties back from Matt Burke this week, citing the need for better communication; the Texans are 28th in explosive play rate allowed. Even if the move doesn't improve things immediately, the Titans (26th in explosive play rate) aren't equipped to exploit that weakness.
Moreover, C.J. Stroud is playing really well, even if it's being overshadowed by the winless record. He's ninth in yards per attempt and 11th in success rate plus explosive play rate. If you only took his numbers when Nico Collins is on the field, those ranks would be second and third, respectively. He hasn't thrown an interception this season either.
All of this is to say I expect a big Texans win.
The Packers cannot stop the run. The Bears lead the NFL in rushing yards. Is that a good place to start for why I'm rolling with the Bears? I'd say yes.
There are other things working in the Bears' favor. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen is getting the most out of his group; the Bears lead the NFL in sack rate, and the Bears have the second-lowest missed tackle rate in the league. (The Packers have the fourth- highest rate, for what it's worth.) The Chicago defense's biggest weakness is its run defense, but the Packers have not been able to run the ball consistently whatsoever.
Jordan Love could hit some big plays over the top to ruin this pick. The Bears are giving up a lot of big plays. But I also think they can get a turnover or two -- something they did well last year -- and the offense can control this game on the ground. No Edgerrin Cooper for the Packers will loom large, too.
Only Lamar Jackson (144) has more rushing yards than Drake Maye (136) this season among quarterbacks, and the Patriots signal caller is coming off a 54-yard day on the ground against the Bills. He's surpassed 30+ yards in two of four games this year, and this should be an enticing matchup to make it three out of five.
The Raiders have allowed 77 rushing yards to opposing quarterbacks this season, the ninth-most in the NFL, and that's on 6.4 yards per carry, the sixth-highest. They allowed Malik Willis to run for 39 yards in Week 1 and a 36-yard scramble by Tyler Shough in Week 3. Maye is averaging nearly six carries per game. The Raiders should be able to score enough against a banged-up New England defense to force the Patriots' offense to keep its foot on the gas pedal. That means Maye dropbacks, which means more opportunities to run.
Only the Cardinals have given up more touchdown passes to wide receivers than the Bills through four weeks. After dominating with Puka Nacua out in Weeks 2 and 3, Adams had a tough Week 4 against the Eagles in the rain. But Adams and the Rams are back in sunny Los Angeles this weekend; Adams has scored eight touchdowns in eight career home games with the Rams, and the Bills' secondary is not exactly in great shape, especially with Christian Benford dealing with a toe injury.
These parlays -- I include at least one every week -- haven't been hitting yet, but I really like this one and the potential payout, too. Jacoby Brissett threw two touchdowns and three interceptions last week. But it gets even better.
Jacoby Brissett has thrown multiple touchdowns and at least one interception in six of his last 10 starts!
This is who he is as a player. He's probably going to give you some good counting numbers. The Cardinals are constantly playing catch-up, and Brissett will do his darndest to keep up: He's thrown multiple touchdowns in eight of his last 10 starts.
But he'll also put the ball in harm's way. A lot. Like, "nine interceptions in his last 10 starts" a lot. The Lions haven't had an interception since Week 1. I know the defense is in really rough shape -- and it might struggle overall Sunday -- but one pick shouldn't be too much to ask for ... right?

title: Is Brock Purdy the 'best QB in NFL?' His case is real entering a MVP statement game in Seattle
summary: Purdy enters Week 5 as one of the NFL's hottest MVP candidates, but will that remain the case after he faces the Seahawks?
full_text:
Brock Purdy ranks second in NFL MVP odds behind Josh Allen entering his 50th career start and a showdown in Week 5 at the defending Super Bowl champions. He's been more embraced as an MVP contender in 2026 while elevating an aging and injury-prone supporting cast to a 4-0 record. It was a different story during his surprise MVP campaign in 2023, where some weaponized the term "game manager" against him.
His style of play in Kyle Shanahan's system also continues to win over critics. But Sunday's game in Seattle represents a big litmus test for Purdy's MVP and superstar quarterback credentials.
Purdy has been at the controls of the most efficient offense in the league this year, and he's been phenomenal himself, with a completion rate of 70%, an average of 8.9 yards per attempt, 12 total touchdowns, one turnover, and no sacks. It's about the best combination of clean football and playmaking you could dream up.
It all adds up to the highest EPA per dropback (0.53) by any quarterback through four games since Tom Brady's historic 2007 season. Purdy is also the first quarterback all-time with one or fewer combined sacks, fumbles and interceptions during a 4-0 start. He sports the lowest negative play rate (0.8%) among quarterbacks through four games on record.
The best part, the 49ers have been the most injured team in football this season, racking up the most games missed and IR stints in the NFL up to this point. Most of those have been on defense, but this offense could be humming even more if they had a healthy WR room, which currently has Ricky Pearsall , De'Zhaun Stribling , Demarcus Robinson and Christian Kirk on injured reserve.
This sets the stage for an early MVP statement game vs. the defending champions.
A win and the discourse will anoint Purdy the early-season MVP, carrying a beat-up team to a 5-0 start with wins over the Rams , Broncos, and Seahawks , three conference finalists from a year ago.
A loss means the detractors will crawl out from underneath their rocks and be quick to point out that Purdy's early-season success came vs. the jetlagged Rams, Dolphins , Cardinals , and a Broncos team without its top two cornerbacks. They'll also sprinkle in the term "YAC merchant" referring to the house calls Deebo Samuel and George Kittle have made off short passes in the past two weeks.
Purdy doesn't have to deal with that fake noise but there is the reality that he and the 49ers have struggled mightily with high stakes against Mike Macdonald's defense. Purdy is 2-4 in his career vs. Macdonald as the Seahawks head coach and Ravens defensive coordinator. The 49ers average just 16.3 points per game in those contests and Purdy had six touchdown passes and nine interceptions.
The three worst games of Purdy's career (in terms of EPA per dropback) have come vs. Macdonald, including a Christmas nightmare in 2023 where he threw four interceptions in a blowout loss to the Ravens and eventual MVP winner Lamar Jackson .
The other two games came in Week 18 last year, with home-field advantage throughout the NFC playoffs on the line, including the divisional round in Seattle. The 49ers combined to score nine points and Purdy had just one 20-yard completion in those games. They are two of the four games with fewer than seven points in Kyle Shanahan's head coaching career.
Turning the tide in this rivalry won't be easy without 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk , who is out for a few weeks with a knee injury. He is an important chess piece in the 49ers' motion offense, especially opening up running lanes. If Purdy and co. can overcome that underrated absence and exorcise the demons against a vicious "Dark Side" defense backed by "the 12" it'll go a long way in further legitimizing Purdy's MVP campaign and status as a superstar quarterback. The latter has been cemented enough to the point where one bad game wouldn't change that in my opinion.
Purdy's MVP-caliber play dates back to Week 11 last season when he returned from a nagging turf toe injury that cost him almost half the season. He racked up 10 touchdowns across two games as the 49ers offense shredded the Colts and Bears for 90 points in primetime, including a thrilling win vs. Chicago to set up that winner-take-all Week 18 game vs. Seattle for the top seed.
It's remarkable that Purdy leads the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.22) and is among the league leaders in touchdowns (33) and yards per dropback (7.5) since returning from injury despite the two duds against the Seahawks.
His production also wasn't due to an all-world supporting cast. He averaged 4.3 yards after catch per completion last season, tied for the fewest in the NFL. You could see why Purdy has started to turn critics into supporters, as he helped lead San Francisco to the playoffs last year, even though Nick Bosa and Fred Warner were lost for the year before the midway point.
Purdy's consistent excellence doesn't hurt, either. He enters the 50th start of his career on Sunday with a 34-15 record, and top-two totals all-time through 50 starts in completion rate (68.1), yards per attempt (8.9) and passer rating (105.7). Only Norm Van Brocklin (hall of famer who last played in the 1960) averages more yards per attempt and only Patrick Mahomes has a higher passer rating through 50 starts.
Purdy is also 34 passes away from officially qualifying on the all-time passing leaderboard, where he would rank first in passer rating.
#49ers Brock Purdy has a 105.7 career passer rating on 1,466 attempts. He qualifies for all-time leaderboard with 34 more attempts. He could go 0 for 34 with 2 INTs this week and would still rank ahead of 2nd place Lamar Jackson's current 102.7 rating.
The numbers have always been there for Purdy, but the support has never been this loud. It's been fascinating to watch the evolution of the narratives around him in just five seasons:
Now, he's gaining MVP support from all over as he's built up an incredible five-season sample of excellence.
CBS Sports senior NFL writer Pete Prisco gave Purdy his endorsement this week . "He hasn't been sacked yet, and a lot of that is on him. He knows how to get the ball out, get it to the right guy, gets the ball out of his hands, he's not standing back there holding the football. I am so impressed with him. He would be the MVP right now, I don't think there's any question about that."
The best way to describe the narrative shift around Purdy is to look at his supporting cast. In his first two years he put up amazing numbers but he averaged the most yards after catch per completion in the NFL. The 49ers had the best supporting cast in the NFL coupled with Kyle Shanahan's QB-friendly system that helped Jimmy Garoppolo thrive, so it was easy to doubt Purdy's greatness.
The script has flipped as his supporting cast has been a revolving door. In the last two years he's 19th in YAC per completion as the 49ers have among the most games missed due to injury. His play over five seasons has also proved he's so much better than Garoppolo ever was.
Brock Purdy Career Evolution - NFL Ranks
If the above Purdy numbers through 50 starts don't speak for themselves, consider that he leads the NFL in pretty much every advanced metric since he was the last pick of the 2022 NFL Draft .
The chart below sums up his excellence. He's first in EPA per dropback. The most all-encompassing advanced metric, which focuses on how each QB impacts his team's scoring chances, by avoiding negative plays and making big ones, for example.
He leads in success rate. This looks at how a QB keeps his offense on schedule by moving the chains.
This is his fourth straight qualified season in which Purdy ranks top five in the NFL in EPA per dropback. Only six others have done that this century. Peyton Manning , Aaron Rodgers , Drew Brees, Patrick Mahomes, Tom Brady and Philip Rivers . That's Purdy with five surefire Hall of Famers and Rivers, who has a chance to be one. Does that pass the smell test?

title: Super Bowl champion Seahawks defense vs. Brock Purdy's 49ers will be one of Week 5's top battles. Here's why
summary: Purdy is playing the best of any QB in the league this season, but now he'll face the NFL's No. 1 defense
full_text:
How well is San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy playing right now in his team's 4-0 start to the 2026 season?
He's on such a tear that he created his own statistical club. Purdy is the only quarterback in NFL history to start 4-0 with one or fewer sacks, fumbles or interceptions combined, according to CBS Sports Research. Purdy leads the NFL in passer rating (126.2), passing success rate (61.9%) and expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.53) while co-leading the league in passing touchdowns (11). Purdy's EPA per dropback of 0.53 is the second-highest through four games in the 21st century, behind only Tom Brady's 0.59 EPA per dropback in New England's 16-0 2007 regular season. He's also been accurate, ranking fifth in the NFL in completion percentage (69.9%).
However, he'll now be tested by the best of the best in Week 5 when playing at Lumen Field against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks . San Francisco leads the NFL in yards per play this season (6.8), but Seattle leads the NFL in yards per play allowed (4.0).
In each of the last two showdowns, the Seahawks' defense had the edge over the 49ers' offense. In Week 18 of the 2025 season, with the NFC West title and the conference's No. 1 seed on the line, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald and his "Dark Side" defense threw 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan, Purdy, and their offense in a body bag in a 13-3 win. That marked San Francisco's fewest points scored in a game since Week 1 of the 2017 season, Shanahan's first game as the 49ers' head coach.
The last meeting occurred in January in the NFC divisional round at Lumen Field. Seattle dropped the hammer on San Francisco in a 41-6 victory that began with Rashid Shaheed taking the opening kickoff back for a touchdown. That 35-point margin of victory tied the record for the most lopsided Seahawks playoff win in team history.
Sunday is another battle — likely one of the best of the weekend.
Seattle's current "Dark Side" defense under Macdonald is on pace to have a profile similar to their "Legion of Boom" predecessors from the 2010's if they remain on this pace. The Seahawks defense has surrendered the fifth-fewest points per game (18.3), the fewest total yards per game (246.8), the fewest yards per play (4.0) and the fewest passing yards per game (144.8) while tied for the most interceptions (6) in 2026. At the moment, they are on pace to become the first team since the 2013-2014 Seahawks to lead the NFL in total defense in consecutive seasons.
So, where will the matchup of Purdy and Co. vs. the "Dark Side" Seahawks be won? When Purdy drops back to pass on early downs. He leads the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.50) when passing on early downs, while being tied for the most touchdown passes in the NFL (7) on early downs.
A big factor in that success is that Purdy typically doesn't face pressure on those early down drop-backs, as he has an NFL-low 24.7% pressure rate in those situations, per TruMedia. He also averages 2.88 seconds before pressure comes on early down dropbacks, the fourth-longest average in the league, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. When he has a clean pocket on early downs, Purdy is averaging 9.6 yards per attempt, the third-most in the league per Next Gen Stats.
Purdy's early down success will be thoroughly tested by the Seattle defense. The Seahawks have created the second-highest pressure rate (44.2%) on early downs even though they blitz at the second-lowest rate (17.9%) in those situations, per TruMedia. The only defense in the league with a higher early down pressure rate is the Vikings (48%), who have blitzed 60.5% more often (78.4%). That means Seattle is winning with their front four at an incredibly high rate on early downs.
Seahawks edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu (22.2% early down pressure rate), edge rusher DeMarcus Lawrence (15.5% early down pressure rate) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (14.8% early down pressure rate) all rank inside the top 25 in early down pressure rate individually entering Week 5, per TruMedia.
That means a lot will be asked of 38-year-old, 12-time Pro Bowl 49ers left tackle Trent Williams and the rest of Purdy's offensive line. The Seahawks have been able to fluster the three-time first-team All-Pro left tackle at a slightly higher rate than normal since Macdonald became Seattle's head coach in 2024. Williams has allowed 12 pressures without a sack on 143 pass-blocking snaps in four combined matchups with the Seahawks' defense since, including the playoffs, for an 8.4% pressure rate, compared to an 8.1% rate allowed against all other opponents over the last three seasons, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats.
However, half of the 12 pressures Williams allowed in this span happened during his 35 matchups with edge rusher Boye Mafe (17.1% pressure rate), who joined the Cincinnati Bengals in free agency this past offseason. Lawrence, with two, is the only other Seahawks defender to have multiple pressures when matched up with Williams in the Macdonald era (since 2024).
Simply staying ahead of the chains on a down-to-down basis and not having negative plays is an antidote against any intimidating defense. That is something Purdy and the 49ers' offense as a whole have specialized in through the first quarter of the 2026 season.
As an offense, San Francisco possesses the lowest rate of plays losing yards (2.2%) by any team through the first four games of a season in the 21st century (excluding kneel downs), per CBS Sports Research. Purdy himself has produced the lowest negative play rate (0.8%) by any quarterback through four games this century as well.
The battle of wits of Shanahan and Purdy versus Macdonald and his "Dark Side" is shaping up to be THE head-to-head battle of the entire Week 5 slate.

full_text:
What a wild week in the NFL . I did not expect Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns to be leading the AFC North after four weeks, or the Houston Texans to be 0-4. How about the Minnesota Vikings ? They lead the NFC North with a perfect 4-0 record despite having what is statistically the second-worst offense in the NFL!
Our picks didn't do so hot last week. We went 2-3 on best bets, as the Vikings, Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions let us down. I knew the Lions' defense was bad, but they made Bryce Young look better than Tom Brady . What an embarrassment. I'm going to start calling them the Etroit Lions, because they have no "D."
Here's a look at what I'm thinking this week. As always, credit to the CBS Sports research team for making me sound smart.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Top five picks ATS record: 10-10 Overall ATS record: 28-35-1 Straight-up record: 35-29
Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET (NFL Network, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
The Jacksonville Jaguars look like one of the best teams in the AFC, while the Philadelphia Eagles are potentially spiraling. It was remarkable how they allowed 14 unanswered points to the Los Angeles Rams in the final four minutes of the fourth quarter last week, and didn't convert a single third down. Seriously, Philly went 0-12 on third downs. Then, this week has been tough for the franchise.
Saquon Barkley has an injured hamstring, his backup in Tank Bigsby was just placed on injured reserve, and the Eagles lost two starters on the offensive line. Right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement on Tuesday to focus on his mental health, and Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens on Wednesday. I know Jurgens wasn't exactly impressive at left guard, but that's still two starters down on Jalen Hurts ' offensive line as the team prepares to cross the pond. By the way, the Eagles are leaving a bit late for this trip, traveling on Friday.
As for the Jaguars, Trevor Lawrence is throwing the ball with confidence, while the defense ranks second in takeaways and rushing, allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per game. This is a large spread, but Hurts hasn't looked very good at all in this Sean Mannion offense.
The pick: Jaguars -7.5 Projected score: Jaguars 27-18
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
I'm pretty sure I mentioned this a couple of weeks ago, but the Pittsburgh Steelers are very much Jekyll and Hyde. They drop 30 points on the Cincinnati Bengals and then get run over by Deshaun Watson and the Browns. What the Steelers have working for them this week are two things: They are at home, where they are 2-0, and they have a rest advantage.
The Indianapolis Colts just got back from London, while the Steelers had an extended break following their Thursday night loss to Cleveland. Even in their win over the Washington Commanders , I didn't think this Colts defense looked very good. We had Athan Kaliakmanis coming off the bench and throwing for 186 yards, one touchdown and an interception in his first NFL action, as the Commanders' offense put up 317 yards of total offense.
The Colts rank second-worst in the NFL in total defense and eighth-worst in total offense. Laquon Treadwell of all people was their leading receiver last Sunday! Additionally, the Steelers have owned the Colts in Pittsburgh, and are 17-2 all-time when Indy comes to visit. The Steelers are 5-0 SU and ATS in their last five games following an ATS loss, so I'll back them in this spot.
The pick: Steelers -2.5 Projected score: Steelers 24-17
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
Fading the Miami Dolphins was lucrative until last week. They covered against the second-worst offense in the NFL -- who didn't score at the end of the fourth quarter in the name of sportsmanship. Yuck!
It's not fun to pile on Miami. We knew this was going to be a rebuilding year. The Dolphins are the only team in the NFL that has not held a lead this season, and they are averaging just 11.5 points per game. This is an opportunity for the Bengals to get off a two-game skid. It's true that Ja'Marr Chase is in concussion protocol and Tee Higgins missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday with groin and neck injuries, but Dohnte Meyers and Mitchell Tinsley really stepped up for Joe Burrow's dynamic duo on Sunday. Meyers caught seven passes for 82 yards! Also, it does appear Chase is making some progress, as he was a limited participant in practice on Thursday.
Betting the Bengals on the road is usually lucrative, as Cincinnati is 11-4 ATS in road games started by Burrow since 2024.
The pick: Bengals -6.5 Projected score: Bengals 24-16
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
The Browns are rested following their massive win over the Steelers last week in prime time, while the New York Jets just lost to Tyson Bagent . I didn't think Bagent looked especially great in his first "start" of the season, but he relied on his powerful rushing attack, which generated 232 yards and two touchdowns. The Jets' offense was atrocious, recording just 157 total yards while going 0-7 on third downs. That forced New York's defense to be on the field for 89 plays. EIGHTY-NINE PLAYS. Chicago racked up 34 first downs compared to New York's seven. It was bad.
As for the Browns, Deshaun Watson is playing the best ball of his Cleveland career. He's led game-winning drives in three straight games, and is finding success with his young playmakers. The Browns are actually the first team to have four players under 23-years-old that have racked up 150 scrimmage yards through four games in Denzel Boston (283 yards), Quinshon Judkins (273), Harold Fannin Jr (153) and KC Concepcion (153).
It's wild to say, but the Browns are the better team right now.
The pick: Browns +2.5 Projected score: Browns 17-13
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
Jayden Daniels is back for Washington, which is maybe a controversial decision? General manager Adam Peters told fans his star quarterback doesn't need surgery right now after dislocating his left elbow again in Week 2, but ESPN reported that he is probably going to need surgery at some point .
Daniels is wearing a brace to protect himself, but he literally re-injured that elbow while wearing a brace when he tried to return to the field last year in his very first game back against the Vikings. If he re-injures it again, you have to wonder if he could further mess up that elbow.
The weather in this NFC East matchup may be wet and windy, meaning the ground game will be important. Commanders running backs Jacory Croskey-Merritt , Rachaad White and Jeremy McNichols are nursing injuries, while wide receivers Stefon Diggs and Terry McLaurin missed practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. I'm leaning towards the underdog here -- who have reeled off two straight victories now.
The pick: Giants +3.5 Projected score: Commanders 20-17

title: Can the Cardinals beat the Lions? Here’s how
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are at a crossroads. Their 1-3-0 record will either become an even bigger hole to dig out of, or the team will begin to rebound. It all starts with this weekend’s game against the Detroit Lions. Two seasons ago, Detroit finished 15-2-0 and looked like the favorite to reach the Super Bowl. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - OCTOBER 04: Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals during the game against the New York Giants on October 3, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are at a crossroads. Their 1-3-0 record will either become an even bigger hole to dig out of, or the team will begin to rebound. It all starts with this weekend’s game against the Detroit Lions. Two seasons ago, Detroit finished 15-2-0 and looked like the favorite to reach the Super Bowl. Then the parity bug struck, and the Lions finished dead last in their division in 2025. RELATED: MEET NEW CARDINALS OT JAYDEN WILLIAMS The Lions are in a similar boat. At 2-2-0, a loss against Arizona will push them deep into the lower third of teams this year. A Cardinals loss will send them straight into the abyss. Yes, it’s still a young season, but when a team loses early and often, that trend continues, and before anyone realizes it, the conversations become more focused on the top of next year’s draft order. What can the Cardinals do in order to secure a win against Detroit? Feed McBride and Higgins The Lions, through four games, are horrible against tight-end coverage. That falls right into what the Cardinals’ offense does best. McBride is third in the league in receptions with 33, so this offense is feeding him a steady diet already. But he is converting only 36.4 of receptions into first downs, while the league leaders have this stat at 70%, which is concerning. McBride is also tied for second in the number of targets with 46. The Lions’ linebackers are very poor with regard to adequate pass coverage on the tight ends. Detroit will counter by attempting to make the tackle as soon as McBride catches it, then force Arizona to run another play. Their defenders don’t have to erase every completion. And use Elijah Higgins a lot more in this contest. If the defense is laser-focused on limiting McBride’s production, throw Higgins into the mix. He has great hands and will gain good yardage after the catch. Be pass happy all day Detroit has a very good defensive front, but their defensive backfield is in trouble. This group ranks dead last in the league in pass coverage, so QB Jacoby Brissett should have a field day. Throw the damn ball, and then keep throwing it. The Cardinals have plenty of pass catchers, so throw short to intermediate, and then a couple of long passes to keep the linebackers and safeties active. Detroit has given up the league’s most passing yards (1,308), the second most pass attempts (165), the most pass completions (115), is ranked #29 in completion percentage (69.7%), has allowed the third most passing touchdowns (11), and the fourth most first-down conversions via the pass (40). The goal for Brissett is a 400-plus yard day. Yes, this Lions pass defense is that bad, allowing a league-high 304.0 yards per game. Cardinals offensive line must hold up It is going to be very tough when their top pass protector, OT Paris Johnson, is now gone for the year. But if the Cardinals offense is going to go all Air Jordan, they must protect Brissett all game long. In addition, RG Isaiah Adams has been ruled out for the game. In their stead is Jon Gaines for Adams, and rookie Jayden Williams is now in at left tackle. The team did pick up veteran and first-round draft pick Jedrick Wills, who is very good in the run game, but he is not a good pass protector. Gaines will be fine. He subbed in for Adams earlier in the season and gathered a 60.8 grade from Pro Football Focus for the one contest. His pass blocking graded out at 64.9. Williams was selected in Round 7 of this year’s NFL Draft out of Ole Miss. The pick was heralded as a “steal” by several media outlets right after the draft. He has had all of training camp, preseason games, and now four weeks of development. He could become the weakest link, and then again, he could surprise a lot of folks. In his final year at Ole Miss, he only allowed two sacks in a tough conference. The kid is a good athlete, so we will see. He will be going up against RDE D.J. Wonnum.

title: NFL predictions: Can Falcons overcome Ravens on Sunday Night Football?
summary: The Falcons emerge from Week 4’s Monday Night Football matchup with the hated Saints as glorious victors, dominating on a level I previously assumed was impossible. Atlanta’s 45-24 humiliation of New Orleans on such a historic night is nothing short of astonishing, and requires a re-evaluation of what we all believed this Falcons team could […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 17: Jase McClellan #30 of the Atlanta Falcons runs with the ball during a NFL preseason football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M & T Bank on August 17, 2024 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons emerge from Week 4’s Monday Night Football matchup with the hated Saints as glorious victors, dominating on a level I previously assumed was impossible. Atlanta’s 45-24 humiliation of New Orleans on such a historic night is nothing short of astonishing, and requires a re-evaluation of what we all believed this Falcons team could be just a few weeks ago. After an 0-2 start where the team managed just 8 points per game (32nd) under third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, the Falcons have now averaged 40 points per game (1st) under starter Michael Penix Jr. Bijan Robinson is as dominant as ever, and his complement in Brian Robinson has also impressed. The Falcons offense looks balanced and unstoppable, and now enters a third-straight primetime matchup: Sunday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 5. The Falcons are 3.5-point home favorites per FanDuel —the first time Atlanta has been favored this season—implying a tight game, particularly if injuries impact the Ravens starting lineup. Falcons vs Ravens predictions The biggest thing to monitor heading into this game is the injury report. Baltimore seems likely to be without MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, as he missed practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. It’s not impossible for Lamar to suit up, but Atlanta will probably face veteran backup Tyler Huntley on Sunday night. This Ravens offense has been quite potent over the first four weeks of the 2026 season: 7th in scoring and 5th in total yards. But it’s unlikely that type of production will continue with Huntley in the lineup, as Jackson’s dynamic athleticism and playmaking ability raise the ceiling tremendously. Baltimore’s offensive line is also very banged up. The Ravens are down multiple centers are were forced to move rookie guard Vega Ioane into the middle. A trade for Cam Jurgens will provide long-term help, but Jurgens is not expected to play on Sunday. Left guard John Simpson has been limited with a groin injury, and reserve guard Andrew Vorhees (who is starting at right guard with Ioane at center) is dealing with a foot injury. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley is battling through toe and ankle injuries, but is expected to play. This is very bad news for the Ravens, with the Falcons boasting the league’s top run defense and the league’s top pass rush in pressures. Atlanta’s ability to dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball is part of what led to their lopsided victories over the past two weeks. Baltimore is a far better opponent than either Green Bay or New Orleans, even with Tyler Huntley, but that’s a tough matchup to deal with. On the other side of the ball, top edge rusher Trey Hendrickson and corner Marlon Humphrey both missed practice to start the week. This is the best defense the Falcons have faced yet, even with those two potentially out of the lineup, both those are major losses against a red-hot offense. Atlanta is the second-best rushing attack in the NFL (including the two Cooper Rush starts) and has allowed the lowest pressure rate in the league on offense. Those mounting injuries—along with the road trip to an Atlanta stadium that will likely be the most raucous it’s been in years after two straight blowout victories—could lead to a very difficult environment for the Ravens to have success. However, this is a well-coached team that’s still got talent all over the roster, and they’re not just going to roll over for the Falcons. All that being said, if Tyler Huntley plays, I’m not sure the Ravens will be able to get enough out of the passing game to keep pace with the Falcons offensively. Atlanta’s defense can be vulnerable to big plays in the passing game, but I don’t think Huntley is the type of quarterback who can take advantage. The Falcons will be loading up to stop Derrick Henry and crowding the short area of the field to take away quick play-action and YAC throws. This will be by far the best rushing attack Atlanta has had to defend, and we’re going to learn if the team’s elite run defense is capable of shutting down one of the best running backs in the NFL. The Ravens defense will put up more of a fight than either of their past two opponents, and I’d expect Atlanta’s offense to sputter a bit out of the gate. But the Falcons are simply too good on the ground to hold down for long, and the more Baltimore sells out to stop the run, the more downfield opportunities will present themselves for Michael Penix Jr. This could be a bigger test for Penix, as the Ravens will likely opt to “make Penix beat us”. Working out of play-action and finding the right times to attack downfield will be critical to keep the defense honest. An injury-marred Ravens team helmed by Tyler Huntley would’ve been a classic trap game for the Falcons under Raheem Morris. That’s a game this team would almost always find a way to lose, despite the matchups largely falling in their favor. I know Baltimore will put up a fight regardless of who is behind center, and Atlanta should be prepared for a brawl—particularly in the first half. Atlanta starts to wear down the Ravens in the second half, and ultimately comes away with the Sunday Night Football victory, 27-20. Rise up with Falcons fans on the SB Nation app! Follow every big play and talk through every game-day moment with fans who care just as much as you do. title: AFC North Preview, Week 5: Ravens and Browns look to break first-place tie
summary: Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: vs. Indianapolis Colts, 1:00pm EST The Steelers dropped to 2-2 last week with a three-point loss in Cleveland on Thursday. They’ve alternated wins and losses through four games, which is telling of some of their inconsistencies on both sides of the ball. They will look to bounce back with a […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Quarterback Tyler Huntley #5 of the Baltimore Ravens looks to pass the ball against the Tennessee Titans at M&T Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Updated Standings : Cleveland Browns 3-1 Baltimore Ravens 3-1 Pittsburgh Steelers 2-2 Cincinnati Bengals 2-2 Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: vs. Indianapolis Colts, 1:00pm EST The Steelers dropped to 2-2 last week with a three-point loss in Cleveland on Thursday. They’ve alternated wins and losses through four games, which is telling of some of their inconsistencies on both sides of the ball. They will look to bounce back with a home matchup against the Colts this Sunday, where they’re favored to win by just over one point. The Colts played in London last week and the Steelers have had a few extra days of rest, giving them a significant advantage. Pittsburgh’s offense has been more productive over the last two games, scoring a combined 54 points with over 40 first downs. Aaron Rodgers threw for a season-high 299 passing yards with three touchdowns against the Browns, but it was in a losing effort. Rodgers attempted 40 passes, which was more than double the amount of rushing attempts the Steelers had as a team (19). They likely want more run-pass balance moving forward, especially against a vulnerable Colts’ defense. The Colts rank in the back-third of defenses in both rushing and passing yards allowed, so the matchup sets up nicely for the Steelers to move the ball. Defensively, the biggest key for Pittsburgh will be slowing down Jonathan Taylor. The Steelers are ceding 112.8 rushing yards per game so far and rank better against the pass. Taylor is the engine of the Colts’ offense and in the midst of another strong season with 353 rushing yards and six touchdowns. Daniel Jones is prone to turnovers when pressured, so expect the Steelers’ defense to seek disruption in the backfield. Cleveland Browns Matchup: @ New York Jets, 1:00pm EST The Browns continue to be one of the league’s biggest surprises having won three straight games, all by five points or less. Their primetime victory over the Steelers last Thursday night was a convincing win in which they held a double-digit lead and then closed out the fourth quarter with a game-winning field goal. They’re 2-0 at home and 1-1 on the road, where they’ll be this Sunday taking on the New York Jets. Like the Browns, the Jets were projected to be an AFC bottom-dweller again this season, but have been surprisingly competitive through four games despite only being 1-3. Their defense ranks near Top 10 in points allowed and passing yards allowed. They are less stingy against the run, ceding over 123 rushing yards per game, so the Browns will likely look to attack them on the ground. That has been a struggle for their offense thus far. Quinshon Judkins is averaging only 3.0 yards per carry with 177 rushing yards through four games, so this could be a potential breakthrough spot for him. On defense, the Browns match up well with the Jets but will be missing stalwart defensive lineman Mason Graham and Mike Hall. That may challenge them along the front seven against a capable Jets’ offensive line. The Jets are without starting running back Breece Hall but Geno Smith is not afraid to air the ball out downfield. Denzel Ward versus star wideout Garrett Wilson will be a deciding matchup in this game. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: @ Miami Dolphins, 1:00pm EST The Bengals have lost two consecutive games after starting the season 2-0. Losing to the Jacksonville Jaguars as they did in Week 4, one of the better AFC teams, is nothing to scoff at. However, the Bengals had ample opportunities to win the game and came up short despite the Jaguars committing well over 10 penalties. The Bengals are still seeking to find more consistency on both sides of the ball. This week profiles as a good get-right spot for Cincinnati against a winless Miami Dolphins team. The Bengals will likely be without their starting wide receiver duo, as both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins suffered injuries last week. That will force backups Dohnte Meyers and Mitchell Tinsley into feature roles. Look for the Bengals to try to get Chase Brown going on the ground again and tight end Mike Gesicki will likely be a leading target for Joe Burrow through the air. Miami’s offense is limited, but they can unlock some explosive plays if quarterback Malik Willis is able to use his mobility or run the ball on designed plays. Keeping Willis in the pocket and contained in the ground game will be a defensive key for the Bengals. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: @ Atlanta Falcons, 8:20pm EST (Sunday Night Football) The Ravens are set to travel to Atlanta for their first primetime game of the season this Sunday night. They will be taking on a red-hot Falcons team without star quarterback Lamar Jackson, who is sidelined after suffering an ankle injury last week. Edge rusher Trey Hendrickson (finger) is also not playing for a second straight week. The Ravens improved to 3-1 with a win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, but it was a tale of two halves. They were outscored 11-0 in the second half after Jackson exited, but managed to hang on for a 24-18 win. With Tyler Huntley under center, there’s no question the Ravens’ offense becomes less potent. Huntley has proven he can win as a spot-starter in relief over the past several years and is dangerous as a runner. The Ravens will likely try to use Huntley’s legs in conjunction with featuring Derrick Henry on the ground. If Huntley can deliver the ball to Zay Flowers accurately, who has been almost uncoverable so far this season, the Ravens may be able to score enough points to win. Defensively, the Ravens will be tested tremendously against Bijan Robinson and Atlanta’s elite rushing attack. Since Michael Penix took over as the team’s starting quarterback two weeks ago, the Falcons have won two straight games in blowout fashion. The Ravens will need to disciplined against Robinson in open-field tackling, which has been an area of struggle for them at times so far this year.
