title: NFL predictions: Can the Bears keep it up against a beat up Packers team?
summary: For years, the Chicago Bears have looked to regain consistent footing against the Green Bay Packers, simply trying to steal a game here or there to maintain credibility. This year is different. The Bears have won three out of the last four games against the Packers, including a dramatic 31-27 victory in January’s playoff matchup. […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears reacts during the third quarter of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images For years, the Chicago Bears have looked to regain consistent footing against the Green Bay Packers, simply trying to steal a game here or there to maintain credibility. This year is different. The Bears have won three out of the last four games against the Packers, including a dramatic 31-27 victory in January’s playoff matchup. This year there are expectations . Despite the early shapes of each team’s season to this point, the Bears are still only a modest 1 game ahead of the Packers in the standings. In fact, if the Packers were to pull off a victory on Sunday, they would leapfrog the Bears in the standings. The Bears enter the game with the presumed starter at QB being Tyson Bagent, the backup QB who threw for 268 yards and an INT last week while leading the Bears to a steady victory. The Bears running back duo of Swift and Monangai pounded the rock against the Jets to a combined tune of 204 yards and 2 TDs (with Monangai doing most of the damage at 146 yards and both TDs). Even with Kyle Monangai’s health in question, expect the Bears to continue to run the ball effectively against a Packers defense missing their stud LB Edgerrin Cooper. Meanwhile, the Green Bay Packers have been signing seemingly every free agent OL in an effort to cobble together a unit that can go from “terrible” to “below average”. The additions of Kevin Zeitler and Laken Tomlinson helped last week during their victory against Tampa Bay, 17-14. They hit their high water mark of 86 rushing yards and managed to keep Jordan Love from taking a sack. While these are genuine improvements, the Bucs have the worst rated DL in the league and have only recorded 6 sacks through four games. Rivalry games are always tricky to predict, and this one might be even more difficult given Tyson Bagent’s start, Kyle Monangai’s injury status (dealing with a turf toe injury per Jeremy Fowler ), and the new OL acclimating to the Green Bay offense. Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have the Bears as a 1.5 road favorite, a slim number indicative of the factors above and the streak of close games between these two teams. Still, I think the biggest difference in this one is Ben Johnson over Matt LaFleur. Johnson has consistently shown the ability to adapt to the situation, and the Bears continue to find ways to win. The Packers, on the other hand, have had an almost comical run of finding ways to lose (and almost lose) since the middle of the 2025 season. I think the Bears win by ten, and I don’t think it feels that close in the end. The Bears are also second in the league at 7.8 points per game in the 1st quarter, and the Packers are 19th at 4.0 points per game in the 1st quarter. As such, I’ll take the 1st quarter spread of -1.5 on the Bears. Bear Down on game day with the SB Nation app! title: NFL Icon Mike Ditka passes away at 86
summary: The Chicago Bears and the NFL lost a true legend of the sport today, as Mike Ditka passed away at 86. Born Michael Keller Dyczko Jr. on October 18, 1939, in Carnegie, Pennsylvania, his family changed their name to Ditka because Dyczko was too difficult for people to pronounce. He went on to become one […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - CIRCA 1980's: Head Coach Mike Ditka of the Chicago Bears on the field before a mid circa 1980's NFL football game at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. Ditka was the head coach of the Bears from 1982-92. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears and the NFL lost a true legend of the sport today, as Mike Ditka passed away at 86. Born Michael Keller Dyczko Jr. on October 18, 1939, in Carnegie, Pennsylvania, his family changed their name to Ditka because Dyczko was too difficult for people to pronounce. He went on to become one of the most recognizable figures not only in sports but also in pop culture. Ditka won a championship as a player with the Bears in 1963, and he led them to the franchise’s only Super Bowl win in 1985. As a player, he revolutionized the tight end position by winning Rookie of the Year in 1961 and becoming the first tight end to surpass 1,000 yards in a season. He was also the first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the class of 1988. As a coach, he was the perfect hire for a franchise that needed a spark, and his fiery passion came through in everything he did. He led the Bears to the playoffs seven times over his 11 seasons in the Windy City and to three NFC Championship Games. Jarrett Payton, whose father, Walter Payton, was the centerpiece of Ditka’s offense during their run to Super Bowl XX, made the announcement live on air after receiving the news. Legendary Bears coach Mike Ditka has passed away, @paytonsun just learned. pic.twitter.com/2N821GERZS — 104.3 The Score (@thescorechicago) October 9, 2026 Jarrett also shared a statement from the family: It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka. While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever. With love and gratitude, The Ditka Family NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell issued a statement on the Passing of Mike Ditka. Mike Ditka epitomized football over so many years. He brought intensity, authenticity, and an unmistakable personality to everything he did. As a Hall of Fame player, Super Bowl-winning coach with his beloved and iconic Bears, and as a broadcaster, Mike served as an ambassador for the game and inspired generations of fans. Through his work with the Gridiron Greats Assistance Fund, Mike was a champion for taking care of those who helped build our game. We extend our deepest condolences to Diana and the Ditka family. Here’s the Chicago Bears statement. We are deeply saddened by the passing of legendary and treasured Chicago Bear and Pro Football Hall of Famer Mike Ditka. Mike’s impact on the Chicago Bears organization, over decades as a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organization, is immeasurable. His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations. We extend our love, prayers, and heartfelt condolences to the Ditka family, and join all Bears fans in deep sadness and reverence as we remember and honor Mike Ditka. “As far as I’m concerned, Coach Ditka is the gold standard,” head coach Ben Johnson said today. “He’s a legend around here, as a player, as a coach. His impact is still being felt to this day. As the head coach of the Bears, I feel humbled to be in that same chair that he was once in.” . . . There will never, ever, be another like Mike Ditka.
author: Lester A. Wiltfong Jr.

title: Chicago Bears Big Play Breakdowns from Week 4
summary: What, exactly, did I get myself into? Recap all the explosive plays each week, that won’t be that big of a deal. The Bears are starting a backup quarterback, it’ll probably be a light week. Wrong. Eleven explosive plays as the Bears offense was on the field for about three quarters of the game. Insane […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears runs the ball during the second quarter against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) | Getty Images What, exactly, did I get myself into? Recap all the explosive plays each week, that won’t be that big of a deal. The Bears are starting a backup quarterback, it’ll probably be a light week. Wrong. Eleven explosive plays as the Bears offense was on the field for about three quarters of the game. Insane numbers put up all around, explosives included. Let’s get to it. Explosive Play 4.1 – Q1 12:06, 3rd and 6 from the Chicago 26. Tyson Bagent passes short middle to Rome Odunze for 21 yards. Right off the bat, the Bears come out in shotgun in a 2×2 formation. Rome and Loveland work together on the left. Loveland’s route, for some reason, draws the attention of both Jets defenders, allowing Rome to run right by both into an empty pocket in the secondary. Bagent delivers a quick ball and just like that, the first explosive of the day. This sure seems like a blown coverage but excellent job of finding it quickly and delivering a good ball. Explosive Play 4.2 – Q1 11:38, 1st and 10 from the Chicago 47. Tyson Bagent passes complete deep middle to Luther Burden for 20 yards. On the very next play, Bagent goes back under center. Loveland motions right to left where Cole Kmet is attached next to Theo Benedet. Bagent gives a play action fake to Monangai before firing over the middle to Burden for back to back explosive passes. This is a bit more impressive here delivering a ball up and over the second level to Burden before the safety can make a play on it. Excellent opening sequence. pic.twitter.com/buMinEcIGO — Grim Cutty (モナンがい Szn) (@iamcogs) October 8, 2026 Explosive Play 4.3 – Q1 6:20, 2nd and 8 from the Chicago 45. Tyson Bagent completes pass deep right to Luther Burden for 22 yards. Back in shotgun here with 12 personnel on the field (Loveland and Kmet). Burden works from the left of the formation, Rome from the right. Burden and Rome run a deep crossing concept with the deep safety moving with Rome. Burden has a step on his defender and Bagent puts a decent ball on him as Luther tries to turn it up to an even bigger play. Great concept, read out well by Bagent, executed all around. pic.twitter.com/OgJZIoVXM7 — Grim Cutty (モナンがい Szn) (@iamcogs) October 8, 2026 Explosive Play 4.4 – Q1 2:57, 4th and 1 from the Jets 21. D’Andre Swift runs off right end for 13 yards. Rolling out the 13 personnel here with Roush and Kmet attached on the left side of the line and Loveland motioning left to right, Bagent pitches to Swift on the short side of the field on this fourth down call. The Jets flow to the pitch well – don’t get me wrong, Swift is going to pick this up 10/10 times as blocked – but the cut back here is beautiful to make this an explosive carry. While Ben Johnson would say all play calls are designed to go for an explosive, you need one here and Swift’s agility and vision makes it into a big play. Drive capper (finally) here by Monangai on 4th and goal. Jets defense was stout on the goal line early, but this was a nice breakthrough. Kyle Monangai and the Bears break through at the goal line ‼️ NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7HxOZN6OwK — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Explosive Play 4.5 – Q2 8:09, 1st and 10 from the Chicago 29. Kyle Monangai runs off right end for 19 yards. Bread and butter. The Bears come out in 12 personnel here with Kmet and Loveland attached to the right side of the formation next to Darnell Wright and Jonah Jackson. Burden motions right to left and Monangai takes the handoff and works behind the strength of the Bears offense. Wright and Kmet double the defensive end before Kmet quickly works to the second level. Jonah has no problem with the defensive tackle and Thuney executes a nice reach block on the back side of the play with help of a quick stab from Bradbury before he works to the second level. Monangai heads in the direction between Wright and Loveland’s blocks but as the safety commits to his run fit to the outside, Monangai cuts back up the middle and finds a patch of Bermuda grass. The backside linebacker makes the play well down the field. The Bears are so good at these run concepts and running to that side of the line. Explosive Play 4.6 – Q2 0:27, 3rd and 5 from the Chicago 47. Tyson Bagent completes pass deep middle to Rome Odunze for 37 yards. This drive was just about dead. Bears come out with three receivers bunched to the right side with Loveland attached on the left. Raymond draws the attention of two Jets defenders running to the boundary, allowing Rome to work one on one. This is just Rome winning beating the safety with some route running savvy at the top of the route and Bagent with the patience to find him. Excellent pocket from the offensive line allows the patience, which leads to three points at the end of the half. Rome Odunze picks up 37! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pupC7cnmpB — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 pic.twitter.com/m6E9gXaIaU — Grim Cutty (モナンがい Szn) (@iamcogs) October 8, 2026 Explosive Play 4.7 – Q3 9:51, 1st and 10 from the Chicago 4. Tyson Bagent completes pass deep left to Rome Odunze for 20 yards. This is a really good route by Rome and nice composure from Bagent delivering a good ball while standing in the end zone. The Bears use 12 personnel with Kmet and Loveland attached to the right. They’re at the four yard line. This is obviously a run to the right side to get a little breathing room, right? Wrong. Play action, trust your blocking, and Bagent delivers in rhythm. Rome does everything incredibly well here, including the one-handed grab to finish. This led a long drive that ended with a second Monangai score. Our friend Jacob Infante with the note on Rome’s route: Rome Odunze has no outside leverage pre-snap, so he attacks the inside on his stem and gets the DB to open his hips up, making him prone to the out route. Great route salesmanship by Rome, but the agility needed to cut like that at 6'3" is also insane. #Bears https://t.co/LTQAnogVq6 — Jacob Infante (@jacobinfante24) October 5, 2026 Two Kyle Monangai TDs! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Z2mrZUc1IP — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Explosive Play 4.8 – Q3 0:21, 1st and 1o from the Chicago 34. Luther Burden runs around left end for 11 yards. This is a very fun drive if you like the run game. The Bears use 11 personnel with Roush attached to Wright on the right side. Burden is motioned from right to left and gets the ball on a jet sweep while the line and fake to the back commits the blocking to the right. The Jets all bite on the run action except for one Jets defender who has no chance at the speedy Burden. The receivers do a nice job maintaining their blocks on the left side of the field and Burden has a first down before he’s touched. Explosive Play 4.9 – Q4 15:00, 1st and 10 from the Chicago 45. Bagent hands to Monangai on an outside zone play and the Bears simply have numbers. Hat on a hat gives Monangai a clear runway before first contact five yards down field. Three Jets defenders converge but he bursts through for an additional six yards after contact. He’s truly amazing with a head of steam. Scheme and blocking got him a positive gain of five and the explosive run style of Monangai earns the extra six. Explosive Play 4.10 – Q4 14:12, 2nd and 10 from the Jets 44. title: Bears at Packers Q&A: We asked ChatGPT since our sister site is running scared
summary: It’s Packers week, and in a big rivalry game like this, you know we will want to do our traditional 5 questions with the SB Nation Green Bay Packers site (Acme Packing Company). Unfortunately, multiple emails to our contact over at Acme went unanswered. Were they simply too busy? Or were they scared? Now, if […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: (L-R) Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers embraces Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears after the NFC Wild Card Playoff game at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Packers week, and in a big rivalry game like this, you know we will want to do our traditional 5 questions with the SB Nation Green Bay Packers site (Acme Packing Company). Unfortunately, multiple emails to our contact over at Acme went unanswered. Were they simply too busy? Or were they scared? Now, if this were a game against the New York Jets or Atlanta Falcons, it probably wouldn’t be the end of the world for our readers if we couldn’t get this Q&A. However, for Packers week, I feel like we needed to deliver. So, we asked ChatGPT to stand in for ACME Packing Company and answer our questions about the Packers. Here are the answers. 1. Are the 2026 Green Bay Packers a good football team? Short answer: not really. The 2026 Packers look more like a mediocre-to-below-average team with some upside than a true contender. They’re 2–2 after four games, including a 17–14 win at Tampa Bay last Sunday. The underlying numbers are concerning: 18.3 points per game (28th) and 26.3 points allowed (23rd), with a -32 point differential. Pro Football Reference’s SRS has them 29th in the league so far. The offense has been inconsistent. Jordan Love threw two TDs against Tampa, but Green Bay managed only 197 passing yards and 86 rushing yards. The defense has suffered a significant blow: linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season with an Achilles tear. Their division is also a problem: Minnesota is 4–0, and Chicago is 3–1, so Green Bay is already playing catch-up in the NFC North. That said, I wouldn’t write them off. Jordan Love gives them a legitimate quarterback, Matt LaFleur is a good coach, and a 2–2 record means they have plenty of time to turn things around. My current assessment: ~5.5/10 team. Possibly a wild-card contender, but nowhere near the NFL’s elite right now. And Sunday’s game against 3–1 Chicago is a pretty important early test. 2. Who is considered a better offensive mind in football: Ben Johnson or Matt LaFleur? If you mean pure offensive mind / schematic creativity, I’d take Ben Johnson over Matt LaFleur. My ranking 1. Ben Johnson — better offensive architect/play designer 2. Matt LaFleur — more proven overall offensive coach Why I lean Johnson: Johnson is more creative and unpredictable. His Detroit offenses were built around sequencing, formations, motion, personnel manipulation, and creating answers for whatever a defense presents. Detroit had three straight top-five offenses in points and yards during his OC tenure. He gets a lot out of the run game. Johnson doesn’t treat rushing as merely a way to stay balanced; he uses it to manipulate defensive structure and create passing opportunities. Chicago’s offense under him has retained that identity. His quarterback-friendly design is a major strength. The improvement from Caleb Williams’ rookie season to Year 2 was one of the strongest arguments for Johnson’s coaching ability. Defensive coaches clearly respect both. In The Athletic’s 2026 play-caller ranking, Johnson was No. 3 and LaFleur No. 4, so the league’s defensive personnel essentially had them in the same tier. Here are my distinctions. If you asked me, “Who would you rather have designing an offense for one game against a great defense?” Ben Johnson. If you asked, “Who has demonstrated over a longer period that he can consistently produce a good NFL offense?” Matt LaFleur. If you asked, “Who is the more naturally gifted offensive schemer?” Johnson, pretty clearly, IMO. And interestingly, the gap may be getting wider rather than narrower. Johnson is only in his second season as a head coach/play-caller, while LaFleur has been doing it for years. Yet Johnson is already being described by NFL analysts as potentially the defining offensive play-caller of the 2020s. My overall offensive-mind score: Johnson 9.5/10, LaFleur 8.0/10. The more interesting debate, though, is Johnson vs. Shanahan/McVay/Reid—that’s where I’d start separating “great play-caller” from “all-time offensive architect.” 3. Who would you rather have as your quarterback moving forward: Caleb Williams or Jordan Love? If I’m choosing one QB to have moving forward, I’m taking Caleb Williams. This season, though, Jordan Love is the better statistical quarterback today. Through four games in 2026, Love has 1,041 yards, 8 TDs, and 3 INTs with an 86.5 rating, while Williams has only played two games because of his hamstring injury. But for the next 5–7 years, I want Caleb: Age: Williams is 24; Love is 27. Ceiling: Caleb’s combination of arm talent, mobility, creativity, and off-platform throwing gives him a higher theoretical ceiling. Situation: I also really like what Ben Johnson could do with Caleb long-term. Risk: Love has already demonstrated that he can be a high-level NFL starter, whereas Caleb still has to prove he can consistently reach that level. The biggest argument for Love is that we already know Love can win from the pocket and play efficient, explosive football. His 2023–25 stretch was legitimately impressive, and even Ben Johnson recently called him one of the better QBs in the league. My ranking for dynasty/long-term: Caleb Williams — higher ceiling Jordan Love — higher floor 4. Many Packers fans are upset about the way Bears fans are talking about their team. Have Packers fans or players talked trash about the Bears in the past? Absolutely. Packers fans and players have talked plenty of trash about the Bears over the years. The Packers–Bears rivalry is one of the NFL’s oldest, and the trash talk has gone in both directions. A few especially good examples: Aaron Rodgers — “I own you.” In 2021 at Soldier Field, after running for a touchdown, Rodgers turned toward Bears fans and repeatedly yelled, “I own you! I still own you!” He later said he had reacted to fans giving him the middle finger, but also proudly connected the comment to Green Bay’s dominance of Chicago. Greg Jennings — “We hate them, too.” In 2012, after Bears receiver Brandon Marshall criticized the Packers’ defense, Jennings openly embraced the rivalry: “We don’t like them. They don’t like us.” He also mocked Chicago’s defense for playing Cover 2 and challenged Marshall’s complaints about Green Bay’s coverage. Charles Woodson — “Same-old Jay.” After the Packers beat Chicago in 2012 and Jay Cutler threw four interceptions, Woodson took a shot at him, saying essentially that Cutler was the same old Jay and would keep throwing the Packers the ball. Cutler had struggled badly against Green Bay throughout his career. Ryan Grant’s “little brother” line. Before the 2011 NFC Championship Game, Packers RB Ryan Grant described the rivalry as being like a family feud: “The Bears and the Packers are almost like big brother-little brother.” His point was essentially that you can respect your brother while still wanting to beat the hell out of him. And it goes way, way back. Accounts from early Packers–Bears games describe players and fans swearing at each other, shaking fists, and needing police protection around the field. This wasn’t some rivalry invented by Twitter in the last decade. The interesting part about today’s complaints Trash talk is baked into this rivalry. Packers players themselves have absolutely participated in it, sometimes very publicly and very aggressively. In fact, there have been periods when Green Bay’s dominance over Chicago gave Packers fans an enormous amount of ammunition. Rodgers’ “I own you” moment is probably the clearest modern example: it wasn’t just some random fanbase feud—an actual Packers superstar publicly taunted Bears fans in their own stadium. At the same time, there is a distinction worth making: not every Packers fan is hypocritical just because Packers players have trash-talked…

title: Bengals vs. Dolphins odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 5 matchup
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are traveling to Florida to play the Miami Dolphins. Even though Cincinnati has fallen to 2-2 after starting 2-0 — and could be without Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins — they are still being heavily favored against the Dolphins, who have yet to win a game or look impressive this season. Odds […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are traveling to Florida to play the Miami Dolphins . Even though Cincinnati has fallen to 2-2 after starting 2-0 — and could be without Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins — they are still being heavily favored against the Dolphins, who have yet to win a game or look impressive this season. Odds The Bengals open as 6.5-point road favorites against the Dolphins, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It is fairly rare for a team that has lost two straight to be almost a touchdown favorite on the road, but it goes to show how close those two games were — especially against the Jacksonville Jaguars, who appear to be a quality team in their own right — and just how bad the Dolphins have been. The over/under is set at 43.5 points. Miami has yet to get over 13 points in a game so far this season. That means there will be some real pressure on the Cincinnati offense, which could be without Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Certainly not impossible depending on which Bengals defense shows up, but pretty clear why it is one of the lower totals this week. Expert picks ESPN : All of their 11 experts are going with Cincinnati All of CBS Sports’ seven experts are taking Cincinnati All of NFL.com’s five experts are going with the Jaguars NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from experts around the web — has the Bengals being picked 98% of the time. Cincy Jungle Pick Going to be surprised, but I am going to go with the Bengals in this one over the Dolphins. Miami being without De’Von Achane makes a pretty significant difference, since he could have easily given the linebackers and safeties fits. Without him, there really isn’t anything to write home about with this offense. Meanwhile, Burrow has been playing pretty well as of late. Even without Chase and Higgins, this defense isn’t set up to slow his roll enough as the Jaguars did. This has all the makings of a game that should be an easygoing win, but we will see how this team comes out and plays going into their bye week. Final score prediction : Bengals 31, Dolphins 17

title: Bengals News: Should Cincinnati claim Kaytron Allen?
summary: One underrated area of need that the Cincinnati Bengals are getting a bit exposed on is depth at the running back position. Chase Brown and Samaje Perine or good at what they do, but what the team really needs is a running back who can go out there and get that tough yard or two […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Washington Commanders running back Kaytron Allen (31) runs the ball against the Detroit Lions in the first quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect One underrated area of need that the Cincinnati Bengals are getting a bit exposed on is depth at the running back position. Chase Brown and Samaje Perine or good at what they do, but what the team really needs is a running back who can go out there and get that tough yard or two when needed. It just so happens that one has been made available by the Washington Commanders : The Washington Commanders shockingly cut rookie running back Kaytron Allen, a sixth-round pick, while juggling the roster around to fit players returning from injury. That move exposes Allen to waivers, where the Bengals would be wise to have an interest. Right now defenses aren’t really respecting the running game in those short yardage situations, and Cincinnati hasn’t given them reason to need to. However, even just having the threat of being able to do that can open up more possibilities for Joe Burrow and the offense while also taking pressure off the passing game. It is a fairly low risk move that they should consider. Bengals News Quick Hits | Bengals Working Through Injuries; (Jordan) Battle Of Miami; The King And I It looks like Jordan Battle will get another opportunity to start by default against Miami as Kyle Dugger has yet to even practice since getting hurt in Week 3. Bryan Cook was at least limited Thursday, so maybe he can make a return. Bengals’ Jordan Battle reveals subtle Malik Willis tell ahead of Week 5 matchup against Dolphins There are people who are saying this isn’t a big deal and others talking about how dumb it is. At this point, I would just love to see him make a tackle on 3rd-&-very long to get off the field rather than whiffing in the most comedic way possible. Battle would be a totally acceptable safety if he could just make these tackles that he has unfortunately made a habit of missing. Ja’Marr Chase returns to practice for Bengals It is a fairly significant step in the concussion protocol to get back on the field. It certainly doesn’t mean Chase will be able to get through the protocol in time for Sunday’s game, but it makes it far more likely than it seemed on Monday. NFL News Jerry Jones ‘extraordinarily disappointed’ after Cowboys loss to Buccaneers This is exactly the result the Bengals need to avoid. Hopefully this prime time loss can serve as a warning to this team to not come out flat against a winless team on Sunday. Instead, come out and put it away early. NFL Week 5 bold predictions: Jahmyr Gibbs breaks Barry Sanders’ record; ‘Hawks punish Brock Purdy One is Marvin Harrison Jr. coming back to life against the Lions’ defense, which seems like an easy one to hammer home. The Lions are dealing with exactly what Cincinnati was last season. Every level of the defense is failing. Ravens preparing two game plans with Lamar Jackson’s status vs. Falcons up in the air It sounds like there is a very real possibility the Ravens are without Jackson, which would be a huge test for this new coaching staff. The team has traditionally struggled without him, which obviously is a huge hurdle for any team without their starting quarterback. It is an opportunity to show if things could be any different.
author: Patrick Judis

title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Dolphins
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will take on the Miami Dolphins this upcoming Sunday. While Miami hasn’t won a game to start the season, they played the Minnesota Vikings tough during Week 3 action. The offense has struggled mightily with Malik Willis throwing for just 85 yards against Minnesota. It is important to note that Minnesota is […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will take on the Miami Dolphins this upcoming Sunday. While Miami hasn’t won a game to start the season, they played the Minnesota Vikings tough during Week 3 action. The offense has struggled mightily with Malik Willis throwing for just 85 yards against Minnesota. It is important to note that Minnesota is one of the best defenses in the entire league. The Bengals cannot take this Dolphins team lightly. They had a ton of picks in this past draft, and a lot of those young rookies are playing key roles for Miami. New coach Jeff Hafley is still looking for his first win, but the Bengals cannot be the team that allows him to get it. Kadyn Proctor vs. Dexter Lawrence We all know that Dexter Lawrence will never be a one-on-one matchup for any offensive lineman during a game this year. However, I am intrigued to watch him going up against rookie offensive guard Kadyn Proctor. The Alabama offensive lineman is one guy who actually has similar/more size than Dexter. Proctor is listed at 6’7” and 366 pounds. He has only allowed two pressures over the last two games combined. Aaron Brewer is the Dolphins center who will be tasked with providing Proctor support in going up against Lawrence throughout the game. Those two, along with second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea, will have their hands full with Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence is playing dominant football on a weekly basis. It isn’t always what shows up in the stat sheet, but Lawrence commands double and triple teams to free up his teammates, is an absolute force pushing the pocket, and is finally starting to even get a holding call or two every now and then because of his pure dominance. Only 4 games in, but I don’t think it is hyperbolic to say that Dexter Lawrence is one of the most dominant defensive players I have ever seen put on the Bengals stripes. pic.twitter.com/Y8G96vn3NO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Chris Bell vs. DJ Turner Bell is a rookie receiver out of Louisville. While he has just 5 receptions for 92 yards on the season, he is still working his way back from a torn ACL in December of 2025. He also had a 67-yard touchdown reception called back against Minnesota after stepping out of bounds prior to the arrival of the football from Malik Willis. DJ Turner has had a bit of an up-and-down season for Cincinnati. He is allowing a 61.1% completion rate against him through the first four games. For comparison, Turner allowed just a 46.8% completion rate during the 2025 season. He also has 2 penalties already through 4 games, after having just 3 total penalties the entire season last year. The Bengals and Turner will not want to allow a young guy like Chris Bell with game-breaking ability to get going early on Sunday. Ollie Gordon vs. Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter Ollie Gordon is coming off his best game in the league. He rushed for 100 yards on just 9 carries against a very good Minnesota Vikings defense. That 11.1 yards per carry is elite-level stuff. Meanwhile, I would argue that Knight and Carter played their best combined games of the season at linebacker for Cincinnati. Most importantly for the two second-year linebackers is that they didn’t miss a tackle against Jacksonville. They will need that to be the case again during the game against Miami. Gordon is a powerful running back with great size at 6’2” and 225 pounds. Keeping that rushing attack in check and forcing the Dolphins to beat you through the air will be a top priority for the Bengals. Joe Burrow vs. Jordyn Brooks and Jacob Rodriguez Burrow is coming off a 428-yard passing game against Jacksonville. However, he is coming off a game with another two turnovers. One of those being an interception to a linebacker that he just didn’t see during the second half of the game. Burrow will have to take care of the football against a talented linebacker unit for the Dolphins. Jordyn Brooks recently signed a three-year, $51 million contract extension with Miami. He has been one of the best linebackers in football over the last few seasons. They also added Jacob Rodriguez in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Rodriguez was a first-team All-American selection at linebacker from Texas Tech last season. He has had no issues picking up right where he left off in college. He is currently leading the league in tackles and recorded 18 of them against Minnesota. This guy is everywhere, and he can make you turn the ball over too. It will be important for the Bengals to not allow that to happen this week in Miami.
author: Dale Altman

title: Bryan Cook doesn’t want to hurt the Bengals defense by playing injured
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-2, and while that record very much keeps them right in the thick of things at this point in the season, there are some reasons to worry. One of those reasons is the health of the team’s secondary. The Bengals were without starting safety Bryan Cook and backup safety Kyle Dugger […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-2, and while that record very much keeps them right in the thick of things at this point in the season, there are some reasons to worry. One of those reasons is the health of the team’s secondary. The Bengals were without starting safety Bryan Cook and backup safety Kyle Dugger last week, and Jordan Battle was limited throughout the week with a hamstring injury. With Battle’s struggles on the field and the lack of experience of the other safeties on the roster, it would be nice to know that Cook and Dugger will be good to go on Sunday. It’s still too early to tell, but Cook was very clear on Thursday that he wouldn’t play if he didn’t feel like he could pull his weight on the field. “You know how much I love my teammates, and I want to be playing, but I can’t be selfish in that aspect,” he said per Mike Petraglia. “But at the same time, I feel if I’m not being who they need me to be on the team, on the field, I’m hurting my teammates. So I never let that happen. “It’s always team first at the end of the day. So if I can be what I need to be for my team, I’ll be out there. And if I feel like I’m giving them less than myself, I’ll never let that happen. It’s always team first at the end of the day.” Cook injured his right ankle in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals are playing one of the winless teams remaining in the league, but winning on the road is tough, and the term “any given Sunday” exists for a reason. He did not practice on Wednesday, but he was a limited participant on Thursday, which is a step in the right direction. If Cook is able to play, he could help shore up a secondary in desperate need of a solid leader at the safety position. Going into the bye week with a losing record would be an absolute gut punch. After losing the last two games, largely due to their own mistakes, they’re in desperate need of a win. Then they can worry about health in their off week. summary: The Cleveland Browns have leaned on their defense this year with good results. full_text: The Cleveland Browns have leaned on their defense this year with good results. With three victories, all three wins were come-from-behind victories that required the defense to control the other club’s offense once the Browns got the late lead. Part of that success for the defense has been the play of their defensive tackles, who surprisingly have provided a very good pass rush. But for the upcoming game against the New York Jets, Mason Graham and Mike Hall, Jr. have been ruled out, and Kalia Davis will not be activated from injured reserve . RELATED: WEEK 5 INJURY REPORT Graham has been a constant spark plug in just his second season. He was injured in the Thursday Night Football game against division foe Pittsburgh Steelers. He was injured in a sea of bodies as he sprained his MCL and ankle, and then hobbled off the field on his own. After the game, he was seen on crutches and with a knee brace. MRIs showed there was nothing structurally wrong with Graham’s knee and that surgery would not be necessary. "Today, briefly saw him walk through the locker room. No crutches, no brace. So, that's a good sign." 🚨 @AshleyBastock42 w/ @NickWilsonSays and @JPeterlin with a positive update on #Browns DT Mason Graham pic.twitter.com/0KSJ67V4Gc — 92.3 The Fan (@923TheFan) October 7, 2026 All this past week, Graham did not practice, although he is no longer on crutches or wearing any type of brace. On Friday, the Browns officially ruled him out for the Jets contest. Hall, Jr. was injured right after Graham left the field. He sustained a lower-right ankle injury during the second quarter after his teammate, DE Jared Verse, was blocked into his leg. The cart was summoned, but Hall miraculously returned to the game in the second half and recorded a crucial sack against QB Aaron Rodgers. Like Graham, Hall did not practice all week. He was ruled out for the Jets game as well. Also ruled out is DT Kalia Davis (quad). New York will be without RB Breece Hall but have a chance to get their run game going without much of Cleveland’s interior linemen available. The Jets have only attempted 99 rushes this year and have the third-worst yards-per-carry average (3.4). The defensive tackle position has gotten pretty thin in Cleveland after being viewed as a team strength. DT Maliek Collins will start as usual, but the other DT spot will be manned by backup Adin Huntington, who is the last healthy defensive tackle remaining. On the practice squad are Zion Logue and Sam Kamara. Huntington had a sack in the game that was nullified by a penalty. Graham leads the Browns’ defense in sacks with four.

But the offense is intact, so perhaps this will be the week they put together a more complete game. The Jets are riding a three-game losing streak and are coming off an embarrassing performance against the Chicago Bears. But as the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers showed on Thursday night, you can’t take any team for granted in the NFL, and that is doubly true for the Browns. summary: Fans of the Cleveland Browns were very excited when GM Andrew Berry brought in two wide receivers early in the 2026 NFL Draft. full_text: Fans of the Cleveland Browns were very excited when GM Andrew Berry brought in two wide receivers early in the 2026 NFL Draft . Almost no one could have imagined, at that time, that the Browns would be 3-1 after a very rough start in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Cleveland’s offense has gone from terrible in 2025 to a passing grade in 2026. HC Todd Monken gets a lot of credit for that , but Berry’s additions have been huge. WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston are starting and making an impact, while OLmen Spencer Fano and Austin Barber are doing the same upfront. According to ESPN’s Bill Barnwell, Boston’s season has put him on track to be the NFL’s Offensive Rookie of the Year : Boston announced his presence in Week 1 with a 46-yard catch on a post route in garbage time, running past Jags cornerback Montaric Brown for his first pro touchdown. Boston has continued to make plays downfield, with catches of 28, 55 and 60 yards over his first four games. He and Zay Flowers are the only two NFL wide receivers with three catches of 45 yards or more through the first four weeks of the 2026 season. In a league where teams are desperate for deep threats, Boston ranks fourth in air yards per target (16.9) while bringing in nearly 60% of the passes thrown in his direction. He’s already enough of a downfield burner to give opposing defenses serious pause, and Boston has been one of the biggest reasons the Browns have been surprisingly effective on offense this season. The 6’4” Washington product has shown the ability to win on routes in multiple ways. His size allows him to box out defenders and break tackles, while his speed and quickness have helped him separate and run away from opponents. In four games, Boston has 13 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. To put that in perspective, only two receivers ( Jerry Jeudy, Isaiah Bond ) had more receiving yards all of last season. Boston is well on his way to eclipsing the team’s leading pass catcher, TE Harold Fannin Jr ., from last season as well (731 yards). Cleveland’s roster already includes the last two Defensive Rookies of the Year in DE Jared Verse and LB Carson Schwesinger ; Boston could keep that streak going with another award-winning season. title: Talking about the Browns’ 3-1 start: Team’s new identity setting the stage
summary: Every season, the NFL has a team that surprises everyone and comes out of nowhere in a positive way. It’s fair to say that the NFL has three of those teams this season, two in the AFC and one in the NFC. The Cleveland Browns and the Las Vegas Raiders are a combined 6-1 to […]
full_text: Every season, the NFL has a team that surprises everyone and comes out of nowhere in a positive way. It’s fair to say that the NFL has three of those teams this season, two in the AFC and one in the NFC. The Cleveland Browns and the Las Vegas Raiders are a combined 6-1 to start the season, while the New York Giants are 3-1 in an NFC East that contains the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles. Out of all the teams that are 3-1, the Browns being 3-1 are the biggest surprise. The question that everyone wants to know is whether the 3-1 start is a sign that things are changing or is it a mirage. It wasn’t long ago Cleveland had the same 3-1 record. Just a few years ago in 2021. However, that team didn’t make the playoffs. In the 2023 season, the Browns had a surprising start and that team found a way to make the playoffs despite injuries derailing them. Fast forward to now, Cleveland is back at 3-1. It’s fair to say after their Week 1 performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars, many people were writing the Browns off. Four weeks in, the narrative around the team has changed, but why (besides winning)? It’s not as cut and dry, but HC Todd Monken’s group has started to slowly find their identity as a team. Identity comes at different times for teams; the earlier the better, especially with a new head coach. It’s fair to say that the Browns have discovered their identity early, and it’s starting to materialize as a physical, gritty team that will turn every game into a phone booth type of battle. Thursday night’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers showcased that identity. The score isn’t indicative of how the game went. The Browns physically manhandled the Steelers for the majority of the time. Cleveland looked faster, more physical, and had more energy throughout the entire game. On the offensive side of the ball, the numbers don’t look appealing, but it’s a unit that is slowly starting to find cohesion. The offensive line appears to be much improved from a year ago, the skill position group has received a facelift, and the quarterback play has the stability game-to-game (not within each game) that the team has lacked. Defensively, the unit doesn’t have an alpha star anymore, but they have retained their identity and principles which made them great last season. With belief comes some doubt, and of course there are reasons to doubt if this 3-1 start by the Browns is actually legitimate, with many people waiting for the shoe to drop. It’s fair to believe no one is buying the Browns’ 3-1 start due to the opponents they played: Week 2: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (team is unraveling, then found a victory on Thursday Night Football) Week 3: Carolina Panthers (team might actually be good, but injuries have been overwhelming) Week 4: Pittsburgh Steelers (division rival) All three of the games that Cleveland won, they weren’t favored to win. As much as people question if the Browns are legitimate, the question can be asked for the Las Vegas Raiders as well: Week 1: Miami Dolphins (could be the worst team in the league) Week 2: Los Angeles Chargers (one of the biggest disappointments of the year) Week 3: New Orleans Saints (might be overrated) Week 4: Kansas City Chiefs (best team in division, but Raiders gave them run for their money) It’s hard to imagine this Cleveland team falling off completely. In fact, this team could be getting better. Peaking early in the season isn’t necessarily a good thing because you tend to burn out later as the season goes on, but the Browns have yet to play a complete game. The offense will continue to get better, the offensive line will continue to have cohesion, and the quarterback play will improve week to week. The same can be said for the defense in terms of their play. The team doesn’t have the high-end talent to make a deep playoff run, but Cleveland has the talent to give teams problems. The Browns haven’t arrived yet as a true contender, but teams shouldn’t take this team lightly. Legit or mirage? Is Monken’s team identity established already? How do you view the 3-1 start? full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cleveland Browns backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders is arguably one of the NFL’s most popular players. Sanders has a large fan base, including some who are also actually Browns fans, a famous last name, and, despite limited success on the field as a rookie, his jersey ranked No. 5 in sales among all NFL players heading into the season . Although Sanders has seen the field for only one play this season, thanks to quarterback Deshaun Watson’s mini-resurgence, Sanders’ appeal has not waned. Even though his career has gotten off to a slow start, Sanders has joined franchise legend and Hall of Famer Jim Brown in one category, as they may be the only Cleveland professional athletes to have a featured centerfold in Cosmopolitan magazine. Brown was featured in 1974, and now, 52 years later, Sanders is the focus of an article in the October issue titled Shedeur Sanders Thinks You’ve Got Him All Wrong . The opening paragraph of the story lays out part of what makes Sanders so appealing: Shedeur Sanders is football royalty. So it only makes sense that after this photo shoot in a sweltering Brooklyn house, he’s lying out on a brown antique couch in the basement in nothing but his boxers, posed like Adonis. He laughs with a full-faced smile when I ask if he’d like a second to get dressed before we start the interview. “Nah, it’s alright,” he says, flashing a pair of pearly whites that are almost blinding. In an hour, he’s headed to the 2026 ESPYs, and there’s no time to waste—not even for a shirt or pants. And I’m positive the women of TikTok who spend their time making fan edits of the rising 24-year-old NFL quarterback, calling him “’90s fine,” would be quite excited to be in my position. All kidding aside, the article is a good look at who Sanders is off the field: a likeable 24-year-old working to figure out who he is and who he wants to be in this world: “I wish people understood me more as a human being. I don’t think a lot of people really know me. I’m just now starting to understand that. You hear a lot of things online, but every encounter I have in person, people end up saying, ‘Oh, wow, he’s actually a great guy.’ Why would you think I’m a bad guy? So I’ve been looking at things a lot more lately, like, ‘Why would people think this?’ It’s not something I’m going to put [solely] on myself, but I do want to fix that. I want to connect with more people, so they can meet me and see the truth.” Basically, Sanders is like any other 20-something starting on the next chapter of their life; it’s just that he is doing it while playing for the city’s No. 1 team and in the spotlight of the country’s biggest sport. title: Cowboys news: Brian Schottenheimer vows that changes will be made after disappointing loss
summary: The Dallas Cowboys had an opportunity to continue their momentum when the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers came to town on Thursday night. Unfortunately, they were pretty much dominated for four quarters, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer says things will be different going forward as they seek changes. Team owner Jerry Jones made his disappointment about […]
full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys had an opportunity to continue their momentum when the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers came to town on Thursday night. Unfortunately, they were pretty much dominated for four quarters, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer says things will be different going forward as they seek changes. Team owner Jerry Jones made his disappointment about the game known while the battle was taking place with his reactions as well as afterwards during his postgame interview. On top of the loss, the Cowboys left the matchup with players banged up. Brian Schottenheimer: Cowboys will ‘absolutely’ make changes, adjustments – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys were embarrassed by the Buccaneers on Thursday night. As a result, head coach Brian Schottenheimer says the team will shake things up. “When you are a coach, there are going to be things you’re going to correct,” he said on Friday, in the immediate aftermath of the loss. “We are solution-makers. We’re not excuse-makers, we’re solution-makers. That’s what we’re working on really, really hard right now. “We’re having the hard conversations. We’re looking at the film. We’re studying the areas [of concern]. Those conversations are really important and we’re having them in all three phases, not just on defense.” Jerry Jones ‘extraordinarily disappointed’ after Cowboys loss to Buccaneers – Kevin Patra, NFL.com Cowboys’ owner Jerry Jones was visibly upset watching Dallas get beat by Tampa Bay. After the game, he was detailed as to why he was frustrated. “Extraordinarily, extraordinarily disappointed,” owner Jerry Jones said of the loss, via the team’s official website . “You really do need to get it done when it’s there to take. They basically were very physical. I thought both their fronts, was really surprised at how well they ran the ball, how they ran it between the tackles. That was surprising.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Cowboys get injury updates on Tyler Guyton, CeeDee Lamb and Joey Porter Jr. – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News The Cowboys left their defeat against the Buccaneers with several key players dealing with injury issues. Their statuses were updated on Friday. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said that X-rays on left tackle Tyler Guyton’s back were negative after the team’s 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday . Guyton missed the team’s final offensive series and was replaced by former first-round pick Broderick Jones. Guyton was seen holding his back and trying to move around during the timeout before the drive, but the team quickly decided to bring him to the locker room. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said after the game that Guyton was dealing with a strain. 5 takeaways from Cowboys’ catastrophe: The most inexcusable Schottenheimer loss – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Dallas was bad in all three phases of the game against Tampa Bay. With that said, there wasn’t anything good to say about their performance. As mentioned above, the cards were laid out for the Cowboys’ defense to get right against Tampa Bay on Thursday. The Buccaneers came into the game allowing the most sacks in the NFL, bottom three in giveaways and had failed to score more than 20 points in three out of four games. Let’s look at how the defense did with that: one sack, zero takeaways and 24 points allowed. The game plan for Tampa Bay was obvious, to shorten the game with long possessions and quick plays to make life easy for its rookie quarterback. It did exactly that with zero pushback from defensive coordinator Christian Parker’s unit. Cowboys TE position is a problem that just keeps getting worse – Reid D Hanson, Cowboys Wire Jake Ferguson had multiple drops against the Buccaneers, with the final one turning into an interception that sealed the game for the Buccaneers. His performance highlighted a huge issue at tight end with the Cowboys. With 1:22 on the clock, down by eight, and the Cowboys driving deep into Tampa Bay territory, Ferguson took a perfect Dak Prescott pass off the facemask for what would essentially be a game-ending interception. The play counted a staggering -4.4 EPA and marked the biggest shift in win probability of the day, dropping Dallas’ odds down to one percent. Ferguson’s tragic blunder was the latest of a long list of errors by the 27-year-old veteran. Ferguson has been guilty of dropped passes and costly fumbles for quite some time. His blocking has lacked in both execution and effort and ability to gain yards after the catch have dropped to late-career Jason Witten levels.
