title: Chargers-Broncos Game Preview: 3 things to watch for in AFC West showdown
summary: The Chargers are 0-4 and many believe the odds show a team that could be winless deep into the month of November. After this week’s game against the Broncos, the Chargers face the Chiefs, have a bye in Week Seven, then face the Rams, Texans, and Ravens in the subsequent weeks. Finally, on November 22nd, […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Omarion Hampton #8 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs the ball for a touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers are 0-4 and many believe the odds show a team that could be winless deep into the month of November. After this week’s game against the Broncos, the Chargers face the Chiefs, have a bye in Week Seven, then face the Rams, Texans, and Ravens in the subsequent weeks. Finally, on November 22nd, they play the Jets which looks like their best shot at a getting their first victory. But what if I told you that this week, against a Broncos team that does NOT look all that great on paper, could be their closest chance at getting in the win column well before then? The Broncos are in the bottom third of the league most offensive and defensive categories through the first month of the season. So are the Chargers, but that’s what makes this matchup close to a coin flip! Jim Harbaugh and Co., at home, could not only earn a much-needed win, but also get to .500 in the AFC West by beating Denver. I’m not going to sit here and give you much more than the little hope I can glean from the stat sheet, but when there’s next to nothing else to be optimistic about this year, we have to take what we can get. With that said, here are the three things I’ll be watching for when these two teams take the field in SoFi Stadium this weekend. 1.) Which bad offense will manage to come through for their team? The Chargers enter Week Five ranked 21st in total offense (306.8) but 29th in points per game (16.5). The Broncos are currently ranked 28th in total offense (280.3) while they’re averaging 18.5 points per game (27th). So while they are scoring more points per game, the Chargers are moving the ball at a better clip (that’s really weird to say but it’s true!). Sunday’s matchup may actually be a closer fight than the football world is giving it credit for. The numbers on both sides of the ball for Denver are really not that much better, if at all, than the Bolts. The biggest difference between the Chargers at 0-4 and the Broncos at 2-2 has been the lack of turnovers by quarterback Bo Nix. He’s thrown one more touchdown pass than Herbert and has half the interceptions (three) in the same span. That’s the margin it seems. So if the Chargers wish to steal a win at home, it looks like the main goal is to keep their stat sheet clean, but if I haven’t mentioned it yet, that’s going to be a hard ask given the state of the offensive line. 2.) What will Omarion Hampton’s workload look like? Since the beginning of the season, Hampton’s workload has seen a steady decline. This past Sunday, he received the smallest snap share between him, Keaton Mitchell, and Kimani Vidal. Despite that, he was the most-efficient player and arguably looked the best when running, as well. Mike McDaniel told reporters that Hampton’s workload decrease was not because of the two fumbles he lost against the Cardinals and Raiders. However, I think that’s just him saving some face for the former first-rounder. Otherwise, I truly don’t think it makes much sense given the efficiency numbers between the three. It also seems like McDaniel is forcing the ball too much to Mitchell, but that’s a whole other tangent to go on. After having a solid game against the Seahawks and scoring his third touchdown of the season, I’m intrigued to see if McDaniel rewards him for ball security and production in his smaller sample size. The Broncos are currently allowing 142.8 yards on the ground per game. That’s 29th in the NFL and should be a massive green light for the Bolts to lean upon him this week. But then, once again, comes the rough reality of the state of the offensive line. 3.) Can Chargers take advantage of ravaged Broncos secondary? The Chargers offense is catching a huge break this week as the Broncos are more than likely going into Sunday’s game without cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss. Those aren’t just their starting cornerbacks, but two of the best young corners in the entire league, including the 2024 Defensive Player of the Year in the NFL. In most weeks, this would be some of the greatest injury news you could hear coming out of the opposition’s camp. However, can the Chargers even take advantage of these injuries this week? Ladd McConkey has not practiced this week yet. Rookie Brenen Thompson took a step back and sat out Thursday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday. Quentin Johnston has logged two limited sessions and obviously isn’t 100 percent. That leaves Tre’ Harris as the current WR1 for the team, but let’s be honest, he was already that after Week Four due to leading the team in both yards and receptions on top of being the only one who can stay healthy week-to-week. Prior to losing Surtain and Moss this week, the Broncos were already allowing 232.3 passing yards per game this season which ranked 22nd in the league. Take out their top guys and the expectation is that this will be one of the easiest units to throw against in Week Five. But that leads me to another question: With the Chargers potentially starting multiple rookies, will Herbert even have the time to find his receivers? Will it even matter that Surtain and Moss are out? Seeing how bad things were when the likes of Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt were still healthy, I don’t know how much positivity I have for this week.

summary: And just like that, fans think the Rams are headed in the right direction. What a difference a close win over […]
full_text: And just like that, fans think the Rams are headed in the right direction. One week after fan confidence dipped to 40% of Rams supporters believing the team was headed in the right direction , the confidence polls are back up to 73% after a win over the Eagles. What a difference a close win over a bad team can make in one week. If the Rams beat the Bills on Monday, we should expect confidence to climb back over 90% again, as it was prior to Week 1. If you expect the Rams to keep stacking wins, you know you can check out FanDuel ’s odds to support the team in Las Vegas. L.A. is 3.5-point favorites over Buffalo this week. Do you agree with those odds? Who is the first coach fired? SB Nation did another round of surveys, and we’ll start with the expectation among voters that Todd Bowles is the most likely head coach to be fired before the end of the 2026 season with 47% of fans surveyed saying Bowles will be the first go. DeMeco Ryans, Jim Harbaugh, Aaron Glenn, Matt LaFleur and Nick Sirianni also received some votes, but not as many as Bowles. Frankly, Bowles may have been fired as early as October 9th, 2026, but sports is magical in the way that people get the chance to prove themselves right and others wrong. In Week 5 of the NFL season on Thursday Night Football, Bowles and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers proved themselves right, and everyone who bet on the Dallas Cowboys wrong. Bowles still has his job at the time of this writing. Even still, the expectation is that Bowles will not make it through the 2026 season, and that seems reasonable as the Buccaneers sit at 1-4. However, each week Bowles is still the coach is another week he can prove everyone wrong, prove the team right for sticking with him and keep his job. For the Bucs and Bowles, their situation will continued to be watched, and if you think you want to make a wager on which coach will go and or which coach can get their team right, check out FanDuel! The Cleveland Browns, despite a 3-1 start, are still expected to Browns “The Browns is the Browns” may be an insult to the franchise, or Todd Monken may be using it as a battle cry to inspire his team to win while making anyone who doubts them look foolish. Either way, fans surveyed expect the Browns to finish with a worse record than the New York Giants, the Minnesota Vikings, and the Las Vegas Raiders with 46% of fans voting for the Browns to falter. You can bet on the Browns however you want at FanDuel. They could win, they could lose. Will DeShaun Watson continue to lead them? They’re fascinating so far this season. The Browns have started 2026 stronger than expected when they traded Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. While the Rams have yet to truly benefit from adding Garrett to the team. Could the Browns end up with a better record than the Rams by the end of 2026? Going into Week 5, the Browns do have the better record.

title: Rams’ ‘draft regret’ isn’t giving them anything to fret about
summary: A strong start in his first training camp had some wondering if edge rusher Rueben Bain would make teams — including the Los Angeles Rams — regret letting him fall to the Buccaneers at pick 15. The answer through five weeks is a remarkably resounding ‘no’ because the Bucs have not been able to hide […]
full_text: A strong start in his first training camp had some wondering if edge rusher Rueben Bain would make teams — including the Los Angeles Rams — regret letting him fall to the Buccaneers at pick 15. The answer through five weeks is a remarkably resounding ‘no’ because the Bucs have not been able to hide Bain on the bench. Through the three games he’s been active for this season, Bain has played in 111 snaps and made three tackles, zero sacks or QB hits, and between zero to four pressures. Thursday night against the Cowboys, Bain made his first run tackle of his career. Several names have been thrown around as “better options” than Ty Simpson, the quarterback who L.A. selected at pick 13 and who has yet to be active for an NFL game, including Bain, Makai Lemon, and Kenyon Sadiq. Well, to date the only one of those players who has even had a single good game this season is Sadiq, and now the tight end is coming off of his worst game of 2026. Bain has a 7-10% pressure rate Going into Week 5, Next Gen Stats noted that Bain had a “9.8% pressure rate”, although pressures varies between site to site. After all these years, experts still can’t agree when a defender is “pressuring” a quarterback or not. Rueben Bain this season: 76 Snaps, 1 Tackle, 0 Sacks, 0 QB Hits, 2 Pressures, 38.7 PFF Grade (110th/110 EDGE). Nothing has gone right for the Bucs this season, and it just keeps getting worse. 💔 https://t.co/oVVM0A7oMF pic.twitter.com/PKJ9pLqIse — Football Stinkers (@NFLStinkers) October 8, 2026 Nobody has said how many pressures Bain had during his 35 snaps against Dallas on Thursday — a surprising win for the Bucs, their first of the season — but if he had zero then his rate would drop down to 7%. Next Gen Stats had him around 100th in pressure rate: “Rueben Bain Jr. has generated four pressures and a 9.8% pressure rate this season, tied for 80th-highest among 123 edge rushers with at least 25 pass rushes. Bain has generated one quick pressure, and his average time to pressure of 3.35 is the 29th-longest among the same group of players. Bain is also the only Buccaneers edge rusher who has yet to record a run stop (run tackle that results in a negative play for the offense).“ According to Pro-Football-Reference, they still have Bain down for zero pressures in 2026. Why this matters already Nobody was arguing that the Rams should draft a player for a long-term benefit, as the team was thinking when they selected Simpson. The entire point of the non-Simpson argument was simple: “Pick someone who can help you NOW!” Sean McVay argued after the draft that the Rams would have drafted someone else if they thought that player could help them win a Super Bowl in 2026. On Bussin’ with the Boys he said: “If drafting them would’ve ensured that we’re going to show at SoFi Stadium next year … I’d say sign me up. We’re taking that guy.” You can’t make a case right now that Bain or Lemon would do that. Through four games, Lemon is one of the least productive receivers in the NFL, catching 10 passes for 65 yards. Next Gen Stats says that Lemon has the third-lowest yards per route of any receiver in the NFL who has a minimum of 75 routes (Lemon has 65 yards on 108 routes). And Sadiq had seven catches for 105 yards with a touchdown against the Lions two weeks ago. That’s 75% of Sadiq’s season production in one game and it came against the Lions. Last week against the Bears, the Jets’ rookie had zero catches on four targets. Again, these are all players who could have bright futures. That’s not the point being argued. It’s whether or not they have a bright present . And you could make the argument that the Rams also could have drafted guard Vega Ione, safety Dillon Thieneman, defensive tackle Caleb Banks, or someone else who might have slightly more present day value. And you might even be right! But Bain? Lemon? Are they helping McVay “get to the show” this year? I think Ty Simpson is doing more for McVay’s health than any other rookies because at least he’s not the bane of his existence on the field like some of these other players would have been.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: The Rams have mismanaged this special teams role for longer than a year
summary: The Los Angeles Rams had a front row seat last weekend to watch one of the NFL’s best punt return men. Britain Covey playing well for the Philadelphia Eagles despite spending last training camp with the Rams. Covey serves as a reminder of how—after all this time—LA still does not prioritize special teams. The Rams […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Britain Covey #85 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Rams defeated the Eagles 24-20. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams had a front row seat last weekend to watch one of the NFL’s best punt return men. Britain Covey playing well for the Philadelphia Eagles despite spending last training camp with the Rams. Covey serves as a reminder of how—after all this time—LA still does not prioritize special teams. The Rams chose Xavier Smith over Covey out of training camp last year. That ended with Smith fumbling a punt return in the NFC Championship game. LA is struggling on special teams. It’s an issue that spans broader than a single bad decision surrounding which punt returner to keep. The Rams have made many poor special teams missteps. Covey is simply a symbol of the dysfunction. BRITAIN COVEY 41 YARD RETURN pic.twitter.com/lrckI0137D — Barstool Philly (@BarstoolPhilly) October 4, 2026 How did the Rams let Covey walk? Xavier Smith returned 16 punts over the 2024 season for 149 yards (9.3 average). He was kept out of the end zone and broke only a single return longer than 20 yards. Smith had the sixth-most fair catches that year with 20. Meanwhile Covey lost the punt return job in Philadelphia to then-rookie Cooper DeJean. He became expendable. The Rams brought him in to compete with Smith. But there truly was no preseason or camp competition. Smith was sidelined as LA’s returner in the preseason. Instead, Covey, Drake Stoops, and Brennan Presley were the only players to field punts in the 2025 exhibition games. Covey wasn’t going to make the roster as a pure receiver. He was released and found his way back to Philadelphia. Over the 2025 regular season Covey returned 11 punts for 124 yards (11.3 average) with one broken off for longer than 20 yards. Smith was consistent with his 2024 production on a per return basis. He averaged 9.3 yards despite a volume increase from 16 to 27 returns. Smith earned three returns longer than 20 yards with a long of 31. Unpopular opinion, but Britain Covey is one of the best punt returners in the NFL. #Eagles — Chase Senior (@Chase_Senior) October 4, 2026 The Rams still don’t have a returner Last Sunday in a head-to-head matchup, Covey returned three punts for 59 yards (19.7 average) with a long of 41. Smith was cut leading up to the game and replaced by Alex Bachman, who had three opportunities and managed a measly average of just 7.5 yards. On the season Covey ranks eighth in punt return average across the NFL. He already has two returns longer than 20 yards. The Rams are getting bottom of the league production from their specialists. And that matters. Poor starting field position increases the degree of difficulty for Matthew Stafford and the offense, which can help explain why one of the best units in the NFL from a year ago is suddenly buck average. Smith clearly wasn’t good enough. Bachman has somehow been worse. The decision to keep Smith over Covey in 2025 was egregiously bad. The Rams still have not course corrected. It’s one step in a long line of poor special teams management. Britain Covey reminded LA last weekend how far they have fallen in the third phase.
author: JB Scott

full_text: The Los Angeles Rams (2-2) host the Buffalo Bills (3-1) on Monday Night Football in a major matchup between two teams that are expected to be playing meaningful football all year, so who ya got? The Rams enter Week 5 coming off a gutsy win against the Philadelphia Eagles when they put up 14 unanswered points in the second half to rise to a .500 record. The Bills just lost to their divisional rival in the New England Patriots, and if that doesn’t fire up the Bills to play their best on Monday night, nothing will. The Bills want to avenge their latest loss and stay atop their division. The Rams want to build their first win-streak of the 2026 season, and perhaps set themselves up for a run. Two NFL MVPs are facing off , Aaron Donald and Jaylen Watson could be back , the Bills may be able to handle Kyren Williams and L.A.’s run game , will the Rams be able to handle Josh Allen and James Cook? If you want, you can check out some other picks here! You hear from us every day, and we want to hear from you too! Let us know what you think and let us know who ya got!

title: Rams vs. Bills will be decided by these 2 key factors
summary: Sometimes winning in the NFL is not sexy. For all the talk surrounding “super teams” and star players, there are plenty of games where the difference between winning and losing comes down to age-old adages. Take care of the football and force takeaways. Execute in the red zone. Score touchdowns instead of settling for field […]
full_text: Sometimes winning in the NFL is not sexy. For all the talk surrounding “super teams” and star players, there are plenty of games where the difference between winning and losing comes down to age-old adages. Take care of the football and force takeaways. Execute in the red zone. Score touchdowns instead of settling for field goals. Perform well in those areas and the rest should fall into place. It’s not about how many yards or fantasy points you accumulate. The troubling sign for the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5 is that the Buffalo Bills tend to be much better in the red zone. The odds currently favor LA by 2.5 points at home. Bills QB Josh Allen is a cheat code inside of the 20-yard line. He can win with his legs. He’s hard to tackle. He’ll find ways to get the ball into the end zone. That’s why Buffalo is the NFL’s ninth-best team in terms of scoring touchdowns inside the red zone with a 68.75% rate. It’s not a one-year blip either. On a percentage basis they are performing at nearly an identical rate as the 2025 season where they finished second-best in the league behind only the Eagles. Meanwhile you must scroll down the list a ways until you come across the Rams. They rank 21st in red zone touchdown rate at 53.33%. It’s a significant drop from last season where LA was scoring touchdowns at a 64.37% clip and ranked seventh. And then we get to taking care of the football, of which neither Allen nor Matthew Stafford are doing well right now. Allen puts the ball in harm’s way at the sixth-worst rate according to Pro Football Focus (PFF)‘s turnover-worthy play (TWP) rate. He has thrown three interceptions despite eight TWP’s. That’s a sign of good fortune. Stafford ranks 14th from the bottom and is middle of the pack in the same metric. He also has eight TWP’s but has thrown twice as many interceptions. That’s not a sign of good fortune. But While Stafford edges Allen out in terms of turnover-worthy plays, Allen does get the best of Stafford in terms of how often they are putting negatively graded plays on tape. Stafford earns a negative PFF grade on 10.3% of his plays, which ranks 10th-worst in the NFL. Allen is 14th at 9.0%. Monday night’s game will likely be decided by red zone performance and turnovers. Josh Allen and the Bills have the upper hand based on their track record so far this season. Neither Allen nor Stafford are taking care of the football. Whichever one plays within himself could give their team a better shot of leaving with a victory.

title: Can the Rams contain James Cook on Monday night?
summary: Everyone rightfully should be talking about how and if the Los Angeles Rams can handle Josh Allen, but another weapon on the Buffalo Bills is James Cook, can the Rams handle both Allen and Cook? Cook is capable of leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns and rushing scores, he has that type of talent. That […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 08: James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills hit by Keir Thomas #96 and Omar Speights #48 of the Los Angeles Rams during a 44-42 Rams win at SoFi Stadium on December 08, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Everyone rightfully should be talking about how and if the Los Angeles Rams can handle Josh Allen, but another weapon on the Buffalo Bills is James Cook, can the Rams handle both Allen and Cook? Cook is capable of leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns and rushing scores, he has that type of talent. That type of talent also can allow the running back to take over any game on any given Sunday, or for the Rams and Bills in Week 5, any given Monday. The Rams will have their work cut out of them. The Bills should too. One strength that the Bills have that Rams don’t is that Cook is about as explosive a back in the NFL as it comes. Of course, the Rams have their own strong back in Kyren Williams, and though he may not be quite as explosive as Cook or others, he’s very productive. So, Monday night’s matchup has the potential to be a lot of fun with a lot of star power. How each team can contain the other’s talent, could decide who comes out on top in Week 5. Three Areas Bills Must Exploit vs. Rams on Monday Night Football (si.com) “ 1. Bills must let their bell-cow RB ‘Cook’ In spite of all of the early publicity for quarterback Josh Allen and his impressive statistical start to the 2026 season, Bills’ veteran running back James Cook III— last year’s NFL rushing champion —is once again quietly near the top of the leader board for total rushing yards so far this fall. Trailing only Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker (87 carries/537 yards) and Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson (85 carries/494) at this point of October, Cook (70 carries/421 yards) could easily be atop the list if he would just be given more opportunity.“ Bills at Rams: Thursday injury reports for both teams (billswire) “ Did not practice LB Nate Landman (shoulder) LB Grant Stuard (hamstring) LB Josaiah Stewart (groin) S Quentin Lake (hip)“ Bills vs Rams Prediction & Tips: Week 5 (squawka.com) “ Buffalo has scored 127 points, more than any team in the NFL. Our Bills vs Rams prediction covers Monday night, and it is a 1.15am BST alarm call for anyone in Britain. The Buffalo Bills are 3-1 and average 5.05 yards a carry. The Los Angeles Rams are 2-2 and have conceded 582 passing yards, fewer than all but one team. They are without Myles Garrett.“ 49ers should brace for Xavier Smith experience Rams fans know all too well (xaviersmith) “Now San Francisco 49ers fans may be about to get a taste of the same. San Francisco signed Smith to the practice squad on Wednesday, desperate for any kind of punch on punt returns. It would be surprising if Smith remained off the active roster for long. He should be an upgrade on the Niners’ current output: six returns for 25 yards. In fact, despite his maddening inconsistency, he’d be the Rams’ best option were he still with the team. Waiving Smith when Alex Bachman as his designated replacement never made much sense. Still, San Fran fans beware. Smith is more tantalizing idea than a material needle-mover. Like a miniature Hot Wheels one of those build-a-ramp toy sets, Smith kept flying off the chute for the Rams, or else getting stuck somewhere in the spirals. “ 3 kickers the Rams could sign today to compete for the starting job (ramblinfan) “Well, here we go again: deja vu. Los Angeles Rams fans should already feel a premonition of imminent upheaval on special teams. We had a similar feeling of dread early last season. If you recall, that foreshadowed a complete midseason overhaul, including a change of special teams coordinators. New Rams coordinator Bubba Ventrone knows the history and is scrambling to avoid a similar fate. He’s already pulled return specialist Xavier Smith, outright releasing him after citing inconsistent decisions and performance. Unfortunately, that’s not the only area demanding attention.“ Injury Updates: ‘As long as they progress accordingly,’ Aaron Donald, Jaylen Watson and Colby Parkinson will be ‘ready to go’ for Week 5 against Bills, Sean McVay says (therams.com) “WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – All three of defensive end Aaron Donald (back), cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) and tight end Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) were inactive last Sunday against the Eagles. On Thursday, head coach Sean McVay said he expects them to all be ready to go for Week 5 against the Bills, barring any setbacks. “The expectation is as long as they progress accordingly, then they’ll be ready to go,” McVay said on Thursday of Donald, Watson and Parkinson. When asked if the plan is for the Rams to ramp up Donald, Watson and Parkinson in practice this week, McVay said “yep it is.” Donald did not practice all of last week with back soreness, and he was designated as limited in practice on Thursday. McVay said “everything has been progressing in the right direction” with Donald.“ Sean McVay explains why Rams signed Pro Bowl LB Eric Kendricks (ramwire) “During Thursday’s press conference, McVay explained the decision to sign Kendricks and talked about how he already displayed an impressive understanding of the defense in his first walkthrough. “Just the depth overall and really, you’re talking about a guy that’s played a lot of meaningful football,” McVay said. “He’s been a great player in this league. I remember even just watching him for all the years where he was such a stud at Minnesota. Then I remember watching the Philly-San Fran game where he comes in and he’s elevated off the practice squad and was a significant factor in a huge playoff win for the Niners. It’s good to be able to have him. You can see even in just the walkthrough, the ownership and understanding of all things defense. I’ve heard nothing but great things, know him a little bit and glad that he’s a part of the group.” Myles Garrett Injury Update Draws ‘Ron Burgundy’ Admission From Rams’ McVay (heavy.com) “I know that the rehab is progressing well,” McVay said, according to the Los Angeles Times ’ Gary Klein . “He’s looked good in the meetings. … I’ll find out so that I can have a little bit more of a specific answer for you guys. I feel like Ron Burgundy up here right now.” The latest assessment continues a string of positive updates surrounding Garrett, who is nearing the end of his mandatory four-game absence on injured reserve.“ Identity-defining wins, Matthew Stafford’s pivotal leadership, reigning MVPs on Monday Night Football & more | Between the Horns (therams.com) “On this episode of Between the Horns, J.B. Long, D’Marco Farr, and Maurice Jones-Drew reflect on the Los Angeles Rams’ comeback win in Philadelphia, break down quarterback Matthew Stafford’s performance, preview a talent-filled matchup in Week 5 vs. the Buffalo Bills, and more.” The Rams showed signs of life, but the real test lies on Monday Night Football (sports.yahoo) “The Rams provided a glimpse of their considerable potential Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, rallying for a victory that might ultimately be remembered as the moment their season turned around. The offense rediscovered its swagger. The defense delivered when it absolutely had to. And a team dangerously close to losing control of its season demonstrated the resilience and urgency that had been missing far too often.“ Comment of the Day: “We wouldn’t have this problem if we’d drafted for the future in 2025 and 2026 while realizing the “future is now.” I see we picked up a semblance of a LB and finally cut X-man. But, IF the Rams need to trade for OL, #3 WR, LB, CB and ST help, now’s the time. If any other team wanted them we could trade Fiske, Mump, Whit, Klare, McClendon, Stetson and some others without skipping a beat. Might get 1-2 decent players for these guys and some of our late round picks. Just sayin’.“ -SlowTightEnd Feed Post of the Day:

title: Las Vegas Raiders-New England Patriots FEED topic: Will wide receivers be more involved in offense?
summary: Wide receiver Tre Tucker is the Las Vegas Raiders’ leading receiver with 15 catches for 233 yards and a touchdown heading into the Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots. However, tight ends Brock Bowers (16/202/2) and Michael Mayer (20/169/1) and running back Ashton Jeanty (19/165/2) occupy the second through fourth spots, and no […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wide receiver Tre Tucker is the Las Vegas Raiders’ leading receiver with 15 catches for 233 yards and a touchdown heading into the Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots. However, tight ends Brock Bowers (16/202/2) and Michael Mayer (20/169/1) and running back Ashton Jeanty (19/165/2) occupy the second through fourth spots, and no other receiver has more than 65 yards on the campaign. On top of that, the majority of Tucker’s production came in one game, recording five receptions, 119 yards and his lone score in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Granted, this shouldn’t be too surprising. The position is viewed as one of, if not the, weakest spots on the Raiders’ roster . Also, Las Vegas was expected to have a tight end-heavy offense after hiring Klint Kubiak as head coach in the offseason, especially since Bowers is such a unique offensive weapon. However, Kubiak may have to lean on his receivers more in New England. According to StatMuse , the Patriots have only allowed 19 catches for 104 yards and have yet to surrender a touchdown to a tight end during their first four games of the season. Last week was especially impressive since Dalton Kincaid of the Buffalo Bills came into the game leading the position in receiving yards (263) but was limited to just seven yards against the Pats. Of course, Bowers is more than capable of bucking that trend. But regardless, the Raiders need to get more production out of their wideouts moving forward. After Tucker, Cody White has been the team’s next most productive receiver with five catches, 64 yards and a team-leading three touchdowns. As the latter number suggests, White has been a valuable red zone target with his contested-catch ability. However, he needs to be more productive between the 20s to have a bigger role in the offense moving forward. Then, there’s the guy many are pointing the finger at: Jalen Nailor. Despite signing a three-year, $35 million contract in free agency this offseason, Nailor has just five catches for 52 yards and hasn’t found the end zone yet in four games with the Silver and Black. Obviously, that’s not what the organization bargained for during the spring. This being said, Nailor suffered a concussion last week and has not cleared the league’s protocol at the time of writing, meaning he may not play Sunday. [Editor’s note: Kubiak said that Nailor is out for the Patriots game after this was written, shifting the focus to Malik Benson and Dareke Young.] It’s still early in the season, so there’s time for a wide receiver to step up and to get more production out of the position. However, the clock is ticking, and it feels like the timeline is speeding up since the surprising 3-1 Raiders are in the playoff conversation after the first quarter of the season . That’s led to some trade rumors circulating in Sin City with the NFL’s deadline about a month away. Many have started to speculate that receivers like Marvin Harrison Jr., Brian Thomas Jr., Jerry Jeudy and Chris Godwin could be on general manager John Spytek’s radar. So, Tucker, White and Nailor should feel some pressure heading into Sunday, especially given the Patriots’ success against tight ends. To be fair, Marcus Johnson showed on the latest Tape Don’t Lie that there have been situations where wideouts have gotten open, but quarterback Kirk Cousins opted to throw elsewhere. That isn’t something new for Cousins, who has built a reputation for using his check-down options in the passing game. And who could blame him, given the difference in talent between the Raiders’ tight ends and wide receivers? But that might not be the case in New England, meaning Cousins will have to rely on his receivers more than he has in the first month of the season. That creates an opportunity for Tucker, White, Nailor or any other wideout on the roster to have a big day. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be keeping tabs on Las Vegas’ wide receivers. The game kicks off at 10:00 a.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!
author: Matt Holder

title: Raiders Week 5: Eyeing the Patriots that present problems for Las Vegas
summary: You have to give Klint Kubiak kudos for the confidence he not only has in his Las Vegas Raiders, but also the way he prepares his football team. The head coach is set to take his 3-1 Silver & Black on the road to face the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough this […]
full_text: (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images You have to give Klint Kubiak kudos for the confidence he not only has in his Las Vegas Raiders, but also the way he prepares his football team. The head coach is set to take his 3-1 Silver & Black on the road to face the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough this Sunday. The Week 5 tilt between the two AFC teams is set for an earlier kickoff time than what the Pacific Standard Time desert marauders are accustomed to, despite the team playing on the road twice already this season — but with afternoon start times. Thus, during his media availability this week, Kubiak was asked what challenges an earlier kickoff — the game is at 1 p.m. Eastern Standard Time but 10 a.m. PST — presents to his team. “We practiced at 7:30 in the morning all training camp, so it’ll be different. But I’m not worried about it,” the head coach responded. Indeed. Timing shouldn’t be a major concern for the Raiders. It’s the of attacking and defending the Patriots that’s of utmost importance this Sunday. So far on the young season, New England has seemingly covered the full gamut of the good, bad, and the ugly an NFL team can present through four games. At 2-2 though, and coming off a stunner of a victory over AFC East favorite Buffalo Bills (29-26 win last Sunday), the Patriots are not to be taken lightly. Grounded Approach With 120 rushing attempts and 471 yards total, the New England offense helmed by former Las Vegas head coach Josh McDaniels ranks fourth and 10th in the league, respectively, in those two categories through four games. In the upset win over Buffalo, New England churned out 143 yards on 35 attempts and a touchdown so expect McDaniels to test a Las Vegas run defense that’s allowed 538 yards on 104 attempts, which ranks 27th in the league in total yardage yielded. Here's why Patriots coaches seem to trust Rhamondre Stevenson more than TreVeyon Henderson. Stevenson's success rate of 43% ranks 13th of 51 running backs with at least 20 carries. Henderson ranks 51st out of 51 running backs in success rate. pic.twitter.com/mtdKWEwTEK — Chad Graff (@ChadGraff) October 6, 2026 The Patriots ground game is a three-headed dragon of sorts with veteran running back Rhamondre Stevenson leading the group with 163 yards on 44 carries (3.7 yards per carry average) and a touchdown. He’s followed by second-year tailback TreVeyon Henderson (38 carries for 141 yards and a touchdown, 3.7 yards per carry) and third-year quarterback Drake Maye (23 rushes for 136 yards, 5.9 yards per carry). Stevenson has been limited in practices due to a knee injury suffered last Sunday but the speedy Henderson alongside Maye can do damage against a Raiders defense that’s allowed an increasing amount of rushing yards since Week 1: 74 to the Miami Dolphins in the opener; 127 against the Los Angeles Chargers; 148 against the New Orleans Saints; and 189 against the Kansas City Chiefs last Sunday. While Maye leaves plenty to be desired as a passer — 73 of 117 for 854 yards with four touchdowns and a league-leading seven interceptions — he’s got the wheels and willingness to run to move the chains. His favorite targets so far are veteran wide receivers Mack Hollins (a former Raider) and Romeo Doubs. That duo leads New England with 20 targets apiece with Hollins snaring 15 for 209 yards and Doubs catching 12 for 203 yards and two touchdowns. Hollins got hurt last Sunday and was declared out for Sunday’s game by the Patriots on Friday. That noted, veteran tight end Hunter Henry remains a capable pass catcher with 12 receptions for 133 yards on the year. What About Bob? Yet another former Raider in this matchup is Patriots middle linebacker Robert Spillane. The 31-year-old leads the team in total tackles (29) and has one forced fumble thus far. Expect the hard-charging linebacker to drop the hammer against both the Las Vegas’ ground game and aerial attack in the middle. While Spillane doesn’t have an interception or pass deflection yet, he’s no slouch in pass coverage as he had five in his two season with the Raiders (2024-25) and two in his first year with the Patriots last season. Raiders RB Dylan Laube on Patriots LB Robert Spillane: “He’s a big guy, he’s super physical, and he’s pretty fast, too.” 🎥: @MikeDixon_VST #RaiderNation | #LVvsNE pic.twitter.com/QWLIcdj2te — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) October 8, 2026 Fellow linebacker Christian Ellis — limited in practices with a chest injury — is right behind Spillane with 25 total tackles and has a sack and forced fumble so far this season. The duo are active second-level defenders who love to come downhill to stymie the oppositions ground game. Off the edge, youngers Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas are hoping to replicate the pressures the Kansas City Chiefs generated against Las Vegas last Sunday, in this upcoming Week 5 matchup. Ponder (24 years old) leads the team with 2.5 sacks (also team-leading four tackles for loss), while Jacas (22) has 1.5 sacks (and two tackles for loss). In the trenches, defensive tackles Christian Barmore’s and Milton Williams’ stat lines are paltry (nine and four total tackles with no stops for loss), but both have the size and power to anchor and make running the ball difficult — especially for a Raiders team struggling to get consistent production from the run game. Head-to-Head Sunday’s matchup marks the 40th meeting between the two storied franchises and it’s the Patriots that lead the overall series 20-18-1 (18-17-1 in regular season action, 2-1 in postseason play). The Raiders, however, have won the last three meetings with the most recent outcome a 20-13 win in the two teams’ regular season opener in 2025 in New England. The Patriots were victorious in six-straight meetings from 2005 to 2020, however, marking the longest win streak of the all-time series. Quotes of Note “I just worry about us. Not thinking as much about them, other than the game, the team we’re playing this week schematically and player-wise. But as far as what we’re trying to build is, we’re just trying to win, trying to win every game, just like every team the NFL is. That is our mindset, just to win. Not to build or rebuild or anything. Just looking at the next game and competing and winning that game.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak when asked if he sees parallels from his team to what the New England Patriots accomplished in 2025 “Well, I think it’s been a resilient group. I think our defense has played very well. I think guys are making plays. I think it’s probably less learning and more confirming what I learned about them back in the spring or even in training camp. These guys, they want to do it the right way. Football means something to them. They’re hardworking, listen well, and it makes it a joy to be the quarterback for a group of guys like that. But you got to go prove it again every week.” —Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins on what he’s learned about the team after the first four games

title: Ashton Jeanty is questionable to play Sunday
summary: Las Vegas Raiders’ starting running back Ashton Jeanty apparently injured his foot in practice Thursday and he did not practice Friday as the team prepares to play at the New England Patriots on Sunday. Jeanty, who was practicing fully with an ankle issue, was added to the injury report Thursday and he was limited by […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders’ starting running back Ashton Jeanty apparently injured his foot in practice Thursday and he did not practice Friday as the team prepares to play at the New England Patriots on Sunday. Jeanty, who was practicing fully with an ankle issue, was added to the injury report Thursday and he was limited by a foot injury. Raiders’ coach Klint Kubiak said Jeanty is questionable to play Sunday. If Jeanty doesn’t play Sunday, rookie Mike Washington will start for the Raiders, who are looking to ignite the game game. They are ranked last in the NFL on the ground. Meanwhile, starting wide receiver Jalen Nailor will be out with a concussion. He didn’t practice all week. Rookie offensive lineman Trey Zuhn is also out with a knee injury that kept him out of practice Friday. He has been playing a handful of offensive snaps in Jumbo packages. Starting right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson is expected tp play Sunday after he missed last week with a groin injury. The team could activate wide receiver Dont’e Thornton from the injured reserve this week. He practiced fully all week after dealing with a hamstring injury, but Kubiak said he will not be activated this week. He must be by Oct. 28. Meanwhile, New England is battered, especially at cornerback. Four of their five cornerbacks has been ruled out including star Christian Gonzalez and fellow starter Carlton Davis and backups Karon Prunty and Channing Canada. That’s a huge opportunity for the Raiders. Receiver Mack Hollins, a former Raider, is also out as if fullback Reggie Gilliam.

title: Following the Raiders scouting department after five weeks of college football
summary: While the Las Vegas Raiders are 3-1 heading into their game against the Patriots, it is always draft season for the college scouting department. They have been on the road trying to find the next players that can improve this roster for the future. For most fans, the biggest need is wide receiver. Based on […]
full_text: (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Las Vegas Raiders are 3-1 heading into their game against the Patriots, it is always draft season for the college scouting department. They have been on the road trying to find the next players that can improve this roster for the future. For most fans, the biggest need is wide receiver. Based on where Raiders scouts have traveled early this season, they seem to agree on the types of prospects they’re looking for. Last week, they traveled to the Iowa vs. Ohio State matchup, where big-time prospect Jeremiah Smith is the apple of most Raiders fans’ eye. The other top prospects were Iowa Hawkeyes offensive linemen. Raiders fans might not know IOL Kade Pieper, but he is going first-round in early mock drafts. Tackle Trevor Lauck is 6’4, 318 pounds, and could sneak into the first round as well. The only team the Raiders have visited twice so far is Oregon. The Raiders watched them in Weeks 1 and 4. Defensive tackle Amauri Washington would be the highest-rated prospect at a position of need. He is a great run defender with high pass-rush upside that could help the Raiders beef up inside. Safety is also highlighted, with plenty of visits. It is early in the process, but we get a glimpse of where the Raiders want to upgrade at certain positions.
author: Marcus Johnson

full_text: (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders fell to 3-1 a 30-27 Week 4 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Let’s look at their wide-receiver production in the game: Tre Tucker Tucker also played 56 snaps, the most all of all Raiders’ wide receivers. He had four catches on eight targets for 44 yards. Tucker has had 49 yards or less in 14 of his past 15 games.. Cody White: The player, in his first game as a member of the 53-man roster, played a career-high 52 snaps. He played in 33 snaps total in the previous three games when he was elevated from the practice squad. White had two catches on four targets for 36 yards, including a spectacular 27-yard grab. Jalen Nailor The free-agent addition played 19 snaps before leaving with a concussion. He didn’t have a catch before leaving the game. Dareke Young: He played 12 offensive snaps for the third straight game. He had one catch for nine yards on two targets. Malik Benson The rookie sixth-round pick played seven offensive snaps. He was not targeted. He has one catch for six yards on four targets this season Conclusion: The Raiders threw 34 passes to tight ends and running backs in Week 4. That was the most by an NFL team in nearly six years. That may continue with this group being banged up and not overly productive as it has 439 receiving yards, the third fewest by any wide-receiver group.

title: Who’s to blame for the Las Vegas Raiders’ woeful rushing attack?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders didn’t run the ball efficiently against the Kansas City Chiefs. Before we dive into what they did wrong, credit must be given where credit is due. Peter Woods, Felix Anudike-Uzomah, Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga did a helluva job giving the Raiders’ offensive line absolute fits in their run defense. Throughout […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders didn’t run the ball efficiently against the Kansas City Chiefs. Before we dive into what they did wrong, credit must be given where credit is due. Peter Woods, Felix Anudike-Uzomah, Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga did a helluva job giving the Raiders’ offensive line absolute fits in their run defense. Throughout the entire game, the Chiefs defensive line initiated contact and brought the fight to the Raiders’ run blockers. Woods is a large man who plays angry; moving him continuously was a problem, even with duos (double teams). In fact, the Chiefs’ defensive line did well at defeating double teams and combo blocks. When they weren’t outright defeating those blocks, they disrupted pathways for Raiders linemen to climb to the second level and block linebackers. On one particular play, Chris Jones maintained 2-gap integrity by keeping outside leverage, temporarily opening the inside gap before defeating Caleb Rogers’ blocking attempt and forcing Mike Washington Jr. back toward his help. What looked like a play where the designed hole was open and a cutback lane formed ended up being a run stuff for the defense. Spencer Burford has been a factor in the run game; when he succeeds, the run game is a beautiful thing to watch. However, when he is getting pancaked by a defensive tackle on the line of scrimmage, there is no hope. Burford got sat on his butt so fast by the man he was trying to block that it took a great reaction by Washington to avoid him and bounce the run outside to gain positive yards. Klint Kubiak’s scheme could use some tweaks When Kubiak told reporters he needs to scheme the run game better, he was spot on. Despite utilizing 12/13 personnel the most in the league, he’s not receiving the results he seeks. Part of it is actually the lack of creativity, surprising considering Kubiak’s chalkboard mastery of the passing attack. More often than not, the offensive player going in motion is leading the defense directly to the ball. Lacking any consistent type of misdirection may work when you have a numbers advantage on the play side, or superior size and push upfront from the offensive line. But when enough weeks of film are available, tendencies begin to display themselves as they are formed. Like running inside zone on first downs, or running to the edges on second downs when not passing. There haven’t been many, if any, endarounds, fly sweeps, or counter plays. Not a lot of draws, nor many running back screens. It was definitely something Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo picked up on when studying film. How do we know this? The Chiefs defense made a concentrated effort to sell out against the run game. Whenever a receiver or tight end went in motion, the linebackers shifted over as soon as the offensive player crossed behind the center. A safety rolled into the box to overload a side of the line of scrimmage by creating a numbers advantage. Figuring out a way to be less obvious with the run game is vital to getting it going again. The Raiders offensive line isn’t bad, and according to nearly every analytics site out there, they are a top-ten unit. But two things can be equally true: the run-block win rate can be ranked high, but when the defense brings extra heat, the unblocked defender is killing the effectiveness of the run game. Not getting a push Without being privileged to sit inside the offensive line room, it’s hard to speak on what exactly the blocking scheme is. Breaking down film, we have to slow it down to about 1/2 speed or lower to watch the line go through their assignments. Free agent Center, Tyler Linderbaum is the best at engaging in a duo block and then climbing to the second level. From time to time, Burford will pull and lead the running back through the hole. No push is most noticeable in short-yardage-to-go situations. The tush push run by Connor Heyward has been executed flawlessly; however, counting on the run from longer than three yards will make you hang your head. The Raiders run into the highest percentage of stacked boxes and consequently running back Ashton Jeanty has been hit in the backfield at an alarming rate. Offensive linemen getting pushed into the backfield disrupts the scheme as a whole, not just the running back. In the Chiefs game alone, there were quite a few times when pulling and motioning blockers were not able to get to their assignments because they were disrupted by a fellow lineman getting blown up and pushed into their path. Lacking vision, no trust and not enough burst Any NFL running back worth a salt would admonish being compared to “T-rich,” Trent Richardson, who was ‘T-rash” when it came to field vision. Speed in the NFL is at a completely different level; players simply move faster than most can anticipate. Holes open and close in a fraction of a second, but that is on the running back to be able to see them, make quick decisions to change course and burst through them. Which brings us to a lack of trust in the blocking. Either the running backs don’t see the hole or don’t think they can make it through in time. Whatever the case, some holes aren’t being run through. This is frustrating to watch and a shame. Raiders’ outside runs are being negatively impacted by runners looking for cutbacks instead of focusing on hitting holes. Not being able to burst through open gaps and creases is exactly why the running game has been struggling.

title: Raiders-Patriots Week 5: 5 things to wacth
summary: The 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders play at the 2-2 New England Patriots on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 10 a.m. PT. Here are five keys to victory for the Raiders: Get turnovers: The Raiders ran out to a 3-0 start to the season fueled by takeaways. They had a league-high nine in that stretch. They […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders play at the 2-2 New England Patriots on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 10 a.m. PT. Here are five keys to victory for the Raiders: Get turnovers: The Raiders ran out to a 3-0 start to the season fueled by takeaways. They had a league-high nine in that stretch. They lost the turnover battle 2-0 in their loss to the Chiefs in Week 4. Thus, they need to get back on the plus side of the turnover game. This is a good matchup for them. The Patriots are tied for a league high 10 turnovers and quarterback Drake Maye has thrown seven interceptions. The Raiders have to capitalize. Win the fourth quarter: Fourth-quarter play was another difference in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss. In the first three games, the Raiders didn’t allow any points in the fourth quarter. They allowed 20 against the Chiefs. The Raiders must get back to finishing games. Stop the run: Kansas City running back Kenneth Walker had 177 yards rushing and averaged eight yards a carry last week. That has to change, but expect the Patriots to try to get Rhanondre Stevenson (has been out of practice some but has a chance to play) and TreyVeyon Henderson going early in this game. Run the ball: The Raiders’ running game has been lacking since Week 1. It’s an issue and they must estbalish the ground game soon. Tight end dominance: The Raiders’ wide-receiving group was thin to start with and now they have injuries, so the emphasis on the tight ends. Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas combined for 16 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns last week. They will need another high-production day from the group this week.

title: Miami Dolphins claim former Washington Commanders RB off waivers
summary: The Miami Dolphins will host the Cincinnati Bengals this Sunday at Hard Rock stadium, but despite the impending clash against Joe Burrow and company, general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan is not done tweaking the team’s roster. On Friday, the Miami Dolphins announced that they had claimed running back Kaytron Allen off waivers. Allen — a 6th […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Kaytron Allen #31 of the Washington Commanders celebrates after scoring a rushing touchdown against the Miami Dolphins during the first half of a preseason game at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins will host the Cincinnati Bengals this Sunday at Hard Rock stadium, but despite the impending clash against Joe Burrow and company, general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan is not done tweaking the team’s roster. On Friday, the Miami Dolphins announced that they had claimed running back Kaytron Allen off waivers. Allen — a 6th round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft by the Washington Commanders — was waived this week when Washington added veteran tailback, Austin Ekeler to their squad. He was not jobless for long, as Sullivan made Allen the newest Miami roster addition this afternoon. Allen played in all four Commanders games this season — totaling 41 yards on 12 carries. He added 29 snaps on special teams. During his four seasons at Penn State, Allen amassed 4,180 yards rushing on 769 attempts (5.4 yards per carry) and 39 rushing scores. The 5’11”, 216 lb back added 70 receptions for 490 receiving yards and four touchdowns through the air. During the preseason, Allen rushed for 85 yards and a touchdown against the Dolphins when the two teams faced off in the exhibition contest — likely a performance that impressed his new general manager, Sullivan. Allen will look for playing time behind Miami’s new backfield starter, Ollie Gordon II, and the banged up Jaylen Wright.

title: Miami Dolphins vs. Cincinnati Bengals: Three Reasons The Dolphins Can Win, Lose Week 5
summary: The Dolphins had their moments in week 4 to secure their first victory of the season, despite the ugliness of the game.  Alas, they were unable to get it done.  They have one more contest before their week 6 bye and it happens to be the Cincinnati Bengals.  For the first time this season, the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 04: Ollie Gordon II #2 and Willie Gay Jr. #40 of the Miami Dolphins interact prior to the start of the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dolphins had their moments in week 4 to secure their first victory of the season, despite the ugliness of the game. Alas, they were unable to get it done. They have one more contest before their week 6 bye and it happens to be the Cincinnati Bengals. For the first time this season, the Dolphins face a team that has lost a game. The Bengals are coming off a 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Unlike in weeks past, this game has a feel like Miami could steal an early victory from a daunting schedule. It won’t be easy, but for the first time in forever, there is legitimate hope. 3 REASONS FOR HOPE HOME COOKIN’ ONCE AGAIN Being from the south and the Appalachian (apple-AT-chan, not apple-A-chan) Mountains, a home cooked meal is something we all look forward to ’round these parts. The Dolphins finally get to have some home cookin’ with 3 of their next 4 contests in the confines of Joe Robbie Hard Rock Stadium. The Vikings’ offense is pretty bad from a stats perspective, but the first 3 opponents Miami faced are top 8 in scoring. The Chiefs are 6th at 29.5 and have scored 30 or more points in 3 of their first 4 games. The lone exception? The game in Miami. Miami held the Chiefs to 24 points, with 7 of those coming in the final few minutes. We all know how bad the Dolphins are, but they held a 4-0 contender with a top QB in check for the better part of a game. Not coincidentally, that was the only game played in Miami this season. The weather and scorching Miami sun should have the Bengals hotter than a Mercedes-Benz with the windows up when the temp goes up to the mid-80s. The predicted temp for the game in the high 80s so you know that opposing sideline will be blistering hot. Like with the Chiefs, if the Dolphins can get the ground game going and lean on big Ollie Gordon, they can wear down the Bengals. Plus, this will be the Bengals 3rd road game in 5 weeks, just like the Dolphins and right before their bye week, just like the Dolphins. THE OFFENSE HAS AN OPPORTUNITY Last week was expected to be a problem for the Miami offense. The Vikings are the top scoring defense, produce the most pressures and sacks, and blitz more than anyone else. This week, the Dolphins get a team in the Bengals that are up there in terms of pressures, but overall, have allowed the 7th most passing yards in the NFL. They are 20th in passer rating allowed. The Bengals are 8th in rushing yards allowed but are 23rd in YPC allowed at 4.5 YPC. The Dolphins had a breakout game from Ollie Gordon last week. According to Next Gen Stats, OG2 is 5th in efficiency at 3.16 (Bijan Robinson is 4th at 3.14 – the lower the number, the more north-south a runner is). The Bengals are near the bottom of the league in missed tackles with 29. A bruising, angry runner against a team that missed tackles and has a high YPC rate in the hot Miami sun could be formula for sustained drives and offensive success. The Dolphins are averaging 4.3 YPA, so this matchup may favor the Dolphins. The Bengals have a low CP allowed at just 63.8% but are 21st in YPA allowed at 7.7 and are tied for 31st in INT% at 0.7%; they have 1 INT on the season. They are also last in YAC allowed with 603 yards after catch. There should be opportunities for the offense to get something going in the passing game. THE DEFENSE HAS AN OPPORTUNITY The Bengals have the 5th best passing offense and that’s bad news for a struggling Dolphins pass defense. However, the secondary has started coming together with rookie Chris Johnson starting to stand out in a good way. The Chiefs and Vikings both stayed away from him for the most part. The Bengals don’t have to worry about weapons as they have a dynamic WR duo in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. But those two may miss the game this week. Chase in in concussion protocol and Higgins is hindered by a hip adductor injury. If they play, they may not be 100%. If they DON’T play, then the Bengals’ next group of WRs are rookie Dohnte Meyers (16 targets), Mitchell Tinsley (7 targets), Andre Iosivas (4 targets), and rookie Colbie Young (2 targets). This isn’t to underestimate these players, but you’d rather face them than the Chase/Higgins duo. Their passing game will rely on RB Chase Brown, who is 3rd on the team in targets at 24 and former Dolphins TE Mike Gesicki (15 targets). Last week, the Dolphins struggled with Hockenson, but one could assume they’d learn from that. Plus, Gesicki has never been a shifty player in the open field, nor has he been a big YAC guy. The Bengals are mid-pack in terms of sack percentage, but Miami is starting to turn up the heat with Chop getting 10 pressures against the Vikings and the Dolphins getting 4 sacks last week. Burrow has been pressured about 1 every 4 dropbacks this season. They have improved their OL, so this will be a good test for the emerging Dolphins pass rush. However, with the 2 biggest playmakers ailing, the Bengals may opt for short, quick passes to underneath targets. The Dolphins are tied for 5th in missed tackles with 14, so they are at least good at getting players to the ground. On the ground, the Bengals are near the bottom in both total yards and YPA. The Bengals are 31st in yards with 297 and only 4 teams in the league have a lower YPC than the 3.6 the Bengals are averaging. The Dolphins struggled last week against Aaron Jones but did well against the 49ers rushing attack and held league leader in both yards and YPA Kenneth Walker III to 70 yards and under 4.0 YPC (he’s averaging 6.2 YPC and 134.3 YPG). The Bengals’ RBs only have 71 attempts on the season for 249 yards (3.5 YPA). Meanwhile, Burrow is averaging over 39 pass attempts per game. Needless to say, unless the Bengals flip the script in this game, they are going to pass a lot more than they will run. The Dolphins may also get a boost from the return of Kenneth Grant to help boost the middle of the defense. In any case, there could be favorable matchups for the defense to get some stops and get off the field. REASONS FOR CONCERN MALIK WILLIS I am loathe to start a QB discussion because, well, I’ve been in WAY too many of them over the course of 16 years on The Phinsider. I covered and argued for them all from Chad Henne to #BlameTannehill to Tua. QBs and OL are the hottest of hot topics amongst this fanbase. I covered in the Tuesday article that Willis is struggling but doesn’t have great help. Those things are not mutually exclusive; both can be and are true. Based on the stats I look at, he is below the standard . His completion percentage is at the bottom, ironically right there with his previous teammate Jordan Love. His YPA is below the Mendoza line at 6.9 – tied with Justin Tannehill Herbert (and above Jordan Love). His INT% is at least decent at 1.9%, but he has only thrown 1 TD, so his TD% is abysmal. These numbers MUST improve significantly. I think it’s premature to write Willis off after 4 games with this team. Perhaps some see the following reasons, but they are legitimate issues. It’s a new offense with a new OC (see the LA Chargers) and that can take time with even good QBs (see the LA Chargers). He is playing with limited pass catchers who have been struggling to create separation on a consistent basis. Three of them are rookies. One of the rookies has missed time. Another is working back from a major injury just last November. He has faced 4 teams that are a combined 15-1 and have the 7th, 8th, 11th, and 18th best passing defenses, two of those without his best offensive weapons in Achane and Douglas. All four of those teams are top half in pressure percentage, but 2 of them are 1st and 2nd (more on that in a moment). None of these issues/reasons/excuses are conducive to a…

title: Former Bears Coach, Vikings Nemesis Mike Ditka Passes Away
summary: On Friday, the National Football League lost one of the legendary figures of the sport, and someone who fans of the Minnesota Vikings are very familiar with, even though he never wore the purple and gold. Mike Ditka, who was the first tight end to ever be enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - CIRCA 1980's: Head Coach Mike Ditka of the Chicago Bears on the field before a mid circa 1980's NFL football game at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. Ditka was the head coach of the Bears from 1982-92. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Friday, the National Football League lost one of the legendary figures of the sport, and someone who fans of the Minnesota Vikings are very familiar with, even though he never wore the purple and gold. Mike Ditka, who was the first tight end to ever be enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame and later went on to become a Super Bowl-winning head coach for the Chicago Bears, passed away on Friday. He was 86 years old. Ditka, ironically enough, came into the NFL the same year that the Vikings did, as the Bears selected him with the fifth pick of the 1961 NFL Draft. He was also selected #8 overall in the AFL Draft that year by the Houston Oilers, but opted to play for Chicago instead. Over the course of his playing career, he played for Chicago, the Philadelphia Eagles, and the Dallas Cowboys. Upon retiring in 1973, he joined Tom Landry’s staff in Dallas, where he was an assistant until the Bears hired him as their head coach in 1982. Ditka led the Bears for 11 seasons, from 1982 to 1992. That meant he got to lead the Bears into the Metrodome once a year, and he didn’t have much of an affinity for the place. In 1987, he referred to it as the “Rollerdome,” stating that it would be better suited for roller skating than for football. Then-Vikings GM Mike Lynn responded by sending a pair of roller skates to Halas Hall. The nickname actually stuck to the point where a skating club was founded that used the Dome until it was torn down following the Vikings’ 2013 season. The game Vikings fans may remember most, however, is likely Ditka’s final game at the Metrodome as the Bears’ head coach in 1992. In that game, the Bears led the Vikings 20-0 early in the fourth quarter, and Chicago quarterback Jim Harbaugh called an audible that he thought was going to be a short pass to running back Neal Anderson. Anderson missed the audible, and instead the pass went to Vikings’ defensive back Todd Scott, who took the ball into the end zone for a 35-yard touchdown. That was the first of three unanswered touchdowns for the Vikings, who turned that 20-0 deficit into an improbable 21-20 victory. Ditka was. . .shall we say. . .less than impressed with Harbaugh’s decision. After leaving Chicago, Ditka took a break from coaching for several seasons before being hired by the New Orleans Saints in 1997. He coached the Saints for three seasons before leaving the coaching ranks for good after the 1999 season and moving into the world of broadcasting. Ditka is one of just two people, along with former Raiders head coach Tom Flores, to win a Super Bowl as a player, an assistant coach, and a head coach. We want to send our condolences to the family, friends, and loved ones of Mike Ditka on his passing, as well as to our NFC North brethren in Chicago, who are no doubt taking this one pretty hard.

LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. For the Saints, Alvin Kamara is questionable but my guess is he’ll play on Sunday. Safety Julian Blackmon is also questionable but probably will play as well. Those are the two key players on the Saints list this week. Everyone else is either listed as out or do not have a deisignation and/or are a backup. Suit Williams joins The Real Forno Show to preview Vikings-Saints Week 5 at the Superdome , where Minnesota has been haunted for decades. Host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano welcome Saints expert Suit Williams of SuitWilliams.com to break down every angle of this Week 5 clash — from Brian Flores’ league-best defense to the Kyler Murray experience under center and whether New Orleans can rebound from a humiliating Monday night loss to the Atlanta Falcons. The conversation centered on two storylines: can the Saints offense survive Flores’ blitz-heavy scheme, and is Kyler Murray the answer for Minnesota? Williams offered high praise for Saints quarterback Tyler Shough: “Shough, everybody believes in. People think Shough is the truth. I think he’s already a top 10 quarterback in the league.” But he questioned head coach Kellen Moore’s slow starts: “Why does the team start slow every week? Why can’t we score touchdowns in the first quarter? That just feels like a feature of the system and not a bug.” The Saints’ offensive line is decimated — Kelvin Banks Jr. is sidelined, leaving backup Asim Richards to face Dallas Turner, who leads the NFL in pressures. “The league leader in pressures against our backup tackle, that’s terrifying,” Williams admitted. Forness didn’t hold back on Flores’ defense, which boasts a staggering -0.18 EPA per play: “He is waterboarding you every single play. And it is relentless.” Williams also questioned the Vikings’ quarterback swap: “I’d have given it another year with McCarthy,” while calling Murray “a guy who lives off of like highlights and playing him on Madden.” Despite it all, Williams predicted a gritty Saints win: “14 to 12 over the fighting Reichards.” Key points: Saints injuries derail offseason plans: Jordyn Tyson (8th overall pick), Kaden Elliss, Travis Etienne, and Kelvin Banks Jr. all sidelined Devaughn Vele (acquired from Denver) emerging as a reliable target — “Third and Vele is a real thing” Chris Olave earning his contract extension despite concussion history, now “balling out” with a guardian cap Vikings offense dead last in passing yards (177 per game); Justin Jefferson limited to just 18 snaps with Murray Will Reichard looming as a difference-maker — “Reichard can win this game.
