title: Commanders GM Adam Peters talks Kaytron Allen, Austin Ekeler, Nick Cross
summary: General manager Adam Peters held his weekly Friday interview with The Junkies on 106.7-FM The Fan and clearly wasn’t ready to break news during it, as he did with Jayden Daniels a few weeks back.   He did offer some insight on several decisions over the last week, including the Kaytron Allen cut, receivers Terry […]
full_text: General manager Adam Peters held his weekly Friday interview with The Junkies on 106.7-FM The Fan and clearly wasn’t ready to break news during it, as he did with Jayden Daniels a few weeks back. He did offer some insight on several decisions over the last week, including the Kaytron Allen cut , receivers Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, and safety Nick Cross. Let’s get right to some highlights from the interview: The Kaytron Allen cut “We’re not down on Kaytron at all. We really like Kaytron. You never want to release a guy at any point in time, but certainly not someone you like and who has shown promise. This may sound like GM speak, but every move you make, you’re trying to everything you can for the best of the team and win the next game and have the best season possible. For this week and moving forward, we have a lot of moves to make in the next few days to get up and play this weekend, and so that was the case of that. … With Kaytron, he has shown a lot of promise and done a nice job. We expose him waivers, and if he doesn’t get claimed, we’d like him back on the practice squad.” Terry McLaurin/Stefon Diggs playing status “With both of those guys, they’re really pushing to play. They’re big-time competitors. They’ll play and they’ll play hurt if they can. Neither of them have practiced yet this week. We have (Friday), usually how it works is that, if a guy practices on a Friday, he has at least a chance to play. If not, there’s less likely of a chance. Both of those guys will push to practice and we’ll reassess after the practice to see where they’re at. It’s touch and go for both of them. It’s tough not to have those guys, but we’ve got a deep room, too.” On Austin Ekeler’s involvement “We knew what type of worker and what type of pro he was and would come back and be strong from that. But that first day of practice in London, he was at a different speed. We were like, ‘we’ve got to get this guy in the game’. He made some big plays and we could see that juice. You talk about fresh legs, but he’s fast anyway. He helped us a lot. …He’ll have more of an expanded role this week. … He’s going to be more embedded in what we’re doing.” On Nick Cross “Nick has been practicing all week and his injury has got to be a doctor’s clearance. If he doesn’t get cleared by the doctor, he won’t be able to play. If he does, he’ll be able to play. He’s another guy who is itching to play and he can help us a lot when he’s out there. We’ll have final clearance on that, and that’s the deciding factor because he’s out there and he wants to play.” View Link

title: Stats and Snaps – 2026 Week 4, Commanders vs Colts in London
summary: A week after the Commanders pulled off the upset of the season, under leadership of backup QB Marcus Mariota, they were dealt another setback, when Mariota exited the London game with an injury in the first quarter. Mariota’s trip to the medical tent left 2026 seventh-round draft pick, Athan Kaliakmanis atop the QB depth chart. […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 4: Athan Kaliakmanis of Washington Commanders Brandon Coleman of Washington Commanders Chris Paul of Washington Commanders and Jerry Tillery of Indianapolis Colts battle for the ball during the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders match between Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 4, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images A week after the Commanders pulled off the upset of the season, under leadership of backup QB Marcus Mariota, they were dealt another setback, when Mariota exited the London game with an injury in the first quarter. Mariota’s trip to the medical tent left 2026 seventh-round draft pick, Athan Kaliakmanis atop the QB depth chart. In his first NFL appearance, the rookie from Rutgers flashed some impressive ability to stretch the field, but also made the mistakes one expects when a late-round rookie QB is thrust into action. The defense came out on fire, setting up the offense with good field position on the first two drives. But unlike the previous week, against the Colts, the offense was unable to convert the short fields to touchdowns, settling instead for field goals. After Mariota left the game, the Commanders’ next five drives ended as follows: punt, punt, punt, turnover on downs, punt, interception. Compounding the absence of the franchise QB and his backup was the failure of the running game outside of the QB position. For the past two games, the Commanders have been held to 100 or fewer rushing yards, with significant contributions from the QBs. Without QB runs, the rushing totals are 71 yds and 49 yds. Against the Colts, the running backs averaged just 2.7 yards per attempt on 18 carries. Overall, the Commanders’ rushing attack averaged a disturbingly low -0.267 EPA/att (you want the number to be positive), ranking 25 th in the NFL. If that were not bad enough, the run defense, which held the Seahawks to 32 nd place in Week 3 at -0.564 EPA/attempt, cratered under the relentless assault from RBs Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan, allowing the Colts to rush for 0.281 EPA/att, the second highest figure in Week 4. With the rookie backup QB playing most of the game, and little to no help from the running backs, the Commanders ranked 30 th in offensive efficiency in Week 4, while ranking closer to average than worst in the league in defensive efficiency: As disappointing as the loss may have been to fans expecting the team to ride the momentum boost from the previous week’s upset win, it was not all bad. OLB Odafe Oweh made the play of the game, with an unconventional strip sack on the opening drive. Center Lucas Patrick was a bright spot on an otherwise underperforming OL, Dyami Brown stepped up as WR1, with others absent or underperforming, Rasul Douglas led the CBs in a bounce back performance, with Amik Robertson continuing to prove that he is the toughest player on defense on a per pound basis, and Daron Payne made some noise on the defensive interior. With Jayden Daniels, Sam Cosmi and Nick Cross possibly returning to the roster, those performances might be something to build on against the Giants. But before we get ahead of ourselves, let’s see who played where, who stood out and who sat down in the Commanders’ 13-30 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in Hotspur Stadium, London. Technicalities: Stats were sourced from the official NFL gamebook via NFLGSIS, Pro Football Reference (PFR), Pro Football Focus (PFF) and ESPN’s total QBR. In cases where advanced stats are scored differently, I have chosen preferred providers (eg. QB pressures – PFF, yards before contact – PFR). Where differences in advanced stats result from judgment calls (eg. Coverage yards allowed, broken tackles) I have gone with a modified consensus approach. When there is fundamental disagreement between sources, the stats won’t be reported. Minor differences between sources that support the same conclusion are reported. If advanced stats are reported without attribution of source, it means there was consensus. As always, official NFL stats override conflicting data from other sources. BIGGEST PLAYS OF THE GAME These plays had the biggest impact on teams’ scoring potential within the respective drives, as quantified by Expected Points Added. EPA threshold = +/- 2.3 Biggest Plays for Commanders Q3, 10:47, 1 st and 10 at IND 47: Athan Kaliakmanis pass complete deep left to Treylon Burks for 47 yards, touchdown. EPA 4.54 Q1, 8:29, 3 rd and 6 at IND 42: Marcus Mariota pass complete short left to Jacory Croskey-Merritt for 35 yards. EPA 3.78 Q3, 6:56, 1 st and 10 at WAS 16: Athan Kaliakmanis pass complete deep right to Dyami Brown for 48 yards. EPA 3.32 Q4, 3:25, 4 th and 2 at IND 40: Athan Kaliakmanis pass complete short right to Dyami Brown for 8 yards. EPA 2.86 Q4, 9:48, 4 th and 3 at WAS 32: Athan Kaliakmanis pass incomplete short left intended for Austin Ekeler (defended by Akeem Davis-Gaither). Penalty on Sauce Gardner: Defensive Holding, 5 yards. EPA 2.64 Q1, 10:39, 1 st and 10 at WAS 19: Marcus Mariota left end for 35 yards. EPA 2.37 Q2, 9:59, 3 rd and 10 at WAS 44: Daniel Jones pass short right intended for Ashton Dulin is intercepted by Rasul Douglas at WAS-34 and returned for 3 yards. EPA -2.82 Q1, 14:50, 2 nd and 10 at IND 32: Daniel Jones sacked by Odafe Oweh for 8 yards. Daniel Jones fumble forced by Odafe Oweh, recovered by Oweh at IND 21. EPA: -4.70 Biggest Plays for Colts Q2, 10:35, 4 th and 1 at IND 48: Seth McGowan left guard for 8 yards. EPA 2.84 Q2, 5:12, 3 rd and 14 at WAS 30: Daniel Jones pass complete short right to Josh Downs for 5 yards. Penalty on Amik Robertson: Personal Foul / Defense, 12 yards (accepted). EPA 2.63 Q3, 13:28, 3 rd and 6 at WAS 16: Daniel Jones pass complete short left to Laquon Treadwell for 11 yards. EPA 2.54 Q3, 14:17, 3 rd and 17 at WAS 24: Athan Kaliakmanis pass short right intended for Antonio Williams is intercepted by Jaylon Carlies at WAS-27 and returned for 7 yards. EPA -3.09 OFFENSE Marcus Mariota went down with an MCL injury on a sack during the Commanders’ second offensive drive. Prior to the injury, he completed 3/4 passes for 46 yds, and ran once for 35 yds. That long run made him the Commanders’ leading rusher in the game. Mariota recorded a 20% passing success rate, a 112.5 passer rating, and a 88.3 total QBR. With the two QBs ahead of him on the depth chart out with injury, Athan Kaliakmanis got his first game experience. It went about as well as expected for a seventh-round rookie QB who didn’t practice with the first team through the week. Athan completed 15/33 attempts (45.5%, ADOT 14.1 yds) for 186 yds, with a long of 48 yds to Treylon Burks, 1 TD, 1 INT and 1 sack for 9 yds. On the ground, Athan ran 3 times for 16 yds (5.3 Y/A, long 9), making him the team’s third leading rusher. Athan’s first NFL penalty was a 5 yd delay of game flag in the 4 th quarter. Athan finished the game with a 29.4% passing success rate, a 20.7 total QBR, which placed him ahead of Sam Darnold (20.4) and Daniel Jones (19.6) in Week 4. It can only go up from there. Jacory Croskey-Merritt had 9 carries for 15 yds (1.7 Y/A) and 1 first down (22.2% success rate). According to PFF, 7 of Bill’s 9 carries were through the A-gaps, where there was little room to run, as indicated by his paltry average of 0.4 yards before contact/attempt. Bill also caught 2/4 targets for 35 yds, with a long of 35 yds. That made him the team’s second most productive receiver at an impressive 2.69 Y/RR. title: Washington Commanders vs New York Giants Week 5: Five Questions with Big Blue View
summary: It’s week 5 of the NFL season, and the 1-3 Washington Commanders will be facing the 3-1 New York Giants at Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD this Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. The Giants lost starting QB Jaxson Dart in week 2 to a season-ending knee injury, yet have managed to persevere with backup Jameis […]
full_text: New York Giants wide receiver Wan’Dale Robinson (17) is tackled during the first quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. | Amber Searls-Imagn Images It’s week 5 of the NFL season, and the 1-3 Washington Commanders will be facing the 3-1 New York Giants at Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD this Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. The Giants lost starting QB Jaxson Dart in week 2 to a season-ending knee injury, yet have managed to persevere with backup Jameis Winston to lead the NFC East. Of course the biggest offseason changes to the Giants were on the coaching side, with the removal of Brian Daboll and his coaching staff and the arrival of John Harbaugh, one of the most coveted head coaching candidates in the 2026 offseason. The Giants offense is designed by a combination of OC Matt Nagy and “Senior Offensive Assistant” Greg Roman, though the plays are called by Nagy from the booth . It seems that the Giants have found a way to marry the run game of Greg Roman (featuring downhill gap power schemes and heavy use of QB mobility) with the passing game of Matt Nagy (featuring a West Coast Offense with spread elements and a heavy use of RPO to get the ball out quickly). The result has been an offense that grinds yards out slowly, but consistently, maintaining control of the ball, yet also gets the occasional deep pass to WR Malik Nabers, who caught 6-of-7 targets for 112 yards and a TD in week 4. The offense is helmed by backup QB Jameis Winston after starting QB Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury in week 2. Winston’s stats haven’t been great so far, with a 70.4 passer rating (29th in the NFL), a 10.34% sack percentage (29th in the NFL), and a 3.8% interception percentage (26th in the NFL). Overall, the Giants have the 26th-ranked offense in terms of yards gained (27th in passing yards, 12th in rushing yards). However, due to the grinding nature of their offense, the Giants have the 2nd-highest time of possession in the NFL. On defense, the Giants are led by Dennard Wilson, former DC of the Tennessee Titans the past two years. You may also remember him as DB coach and passing game coordinator of the Eagles in 2021-2022 under Jonathon Gannon. Wilson runs a 3-4 defensive front with frequent use of simulated pressures, where more than 4 players line up close to the line of scrimmage to simulate rushing the QB, but several drop back into coverage at the snap so that only 4 actually rush, but from unexpected positions. In coverage, the Giants have a man-coverage rate of 26.3% (7th-highest in the NFL) and zone-coverage rate of 69.0% (7th-lowest in the NFL), with an emphasis on pressing at the line to disrupt WR routes. Overall, this is a defense that ranks 9th-best in yards allowed (with the 10th-fewest passing yards allowed and 16th-fewest rushing yards allowed). I asked Ed Valentine of Big Blue View five questions to better understand the state of the Giants and what to look for in this game. 1) A lot of the Giants’ season is going to revolve around QB Jameis Winston and his ability to fill in for Jaxson Dart. What have you seen out of Jameis so far, and what do you think about what he brings to the table vs JJ McCarthy? Jameis is Jameis. He was fantastic at times against the Cardinals, mystifyingly bad at other times. That’s how you throw for 250 yards with 3 TDs and 2 INTs. I’m going to discount Week 3 against Tennessee because that game was played in rain and high winds with gusts nearing 40 mph. He did not turn the ball over and the Giants won, despite not scoring a touchdown. So, you live with it. Jameis brings experience and leadership. He was named to the team’s Leadership Council and voted as a team captain long before Dart was injured. How many backup quarterbacks are voted as a captain by teammates? If the Giants win enough games, it is going to be hard for John Harbaugh to justify replacing Winston with McCarthy. That said, if Winston’s turnovers hold the Giants back Harbaugh won’t hesitate to go to McCarthy. Nobody really knows what the Giants will get out of McCarthy if and when he plays, but Harbaugh won’t sit around and watch the season go down the drain because Winston can’t, or won’t, protect the football. 2) The Giants are currently 3-1 and sitting atop the NFC East as division leaders. What are you most confident about with respect to the Giants and what are you most worried about heading into Sunday’s game? Well, I know what the Giants are. They are a flawed team, but they play with physicality, resilience, a belief that they are good enough and have worked hard enough to deserve to win games. I worry about a lot of things because the Giants don’t have a massive margin for error. Mostly, I guess, you wonder how long the ride is going to last. 3) What is your overall opinion of John Harbaugh as a head coach so far and how has he changed the team? Harbaugh’s time with the Baltimore Ravens ran its course. I get that. He has been the perfect coach at the perfect time for the Giants, though. They haven’t had a coach with this kind of credibility since Tom Coughlin. He is the first coach with a Super Bowl title elsewhere that they have ever hired. He brought a proven track record that created immediate credibility. He has brought expectations and standards the entire franchise needed, and has demanded the best work players could give every day. I don’t know what the ceiling is for this team. I do know that Harbaugh isn’t going to accept anything less than the best everyone can do, and the franchise desperately needed that. 4) Who is one Giants player on offense and one player on defense that Washington fans probably don’t know much about, but should? I don’t honestly know how many “unfamiliar” players the Giants use regularly. I will, though, give you a couple of players new to the Giants to be aware of. Offense — Isaiah Likely. The Giants signed Likely to be their primary tight end, and second option as a receiver behind Malik Nabers. He formed a tremendous connection with Dart, and looked primed for a massive season because of that. He leads the Giants with 22 receptions, but the timing and communication between Likely and Winston has not been what it was with Dart and Likely. That is a work in progress. Defense — Watch the veteran DT duo of D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris. The Giants are using a village to replace Dexter Lawrence, and those two were really good in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals. 5) How should Washington go about gameplanning this matchup on both sides of the ball? Offensively, you test the Giants run defense. Particularly to the edges. See if this will be a good or bad week for the run defense. Teams have used a lot of quick-game in the passing attack. Even though he doesn’t have a sack, you want to know where Abdul Carter is. The secondary has been better than anticipated, but you make them prove it. Defensively, the Giants want to run the ball but they don’t have any home-run hitting backs. I think you crowd the line of scrimmage, try to make Winston win with his arm. He is capable of doing it but he is also capable of gifting you the ball — and points — at any moment. Bonus Q) What do you think about Lucas Patrick? The Commanders signed him after Giants cutdowns and it looks like he’ll be our starting Center. I think Patrick is an adequate veteran fill-in offensive lineman. He didn’t make the Giants roster for a couple of reasons. There were concerns about a knee issue that caused him to miss time in camp. John Harbaugh called it “old man” stuff. Also, Bryan Hudson is a younger player the Giants really like. He won the backup job, and may now actually be the starting center. A companion article to this with my answers to Ed’s questions is linked here . Thanks again to Ed Valentine for taking time out of his day to answer our questions about the Giants.
author: eboracum

title: NFL Week 5 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: Big performances for Brock Bowers, Travon Walker and Luther Burden III? The Giants pulling an upset? And an under-the-radar RB emerging this week in fantasy?
full_text:
Week 5 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Buccaneers defeated the Cowboys on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 14 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Could the Giants pull off an upset? How many yards will Steelers running back Jaylen Warren record against the Colts? Is Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett a safe starter in fantasy? And which Bears receiver will find the end zone? Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Las Vegas Raiders +3.5 (+164 moneyline) at New England Patriots 

 Patriots QB Drake Maye 's breakout against the Bills last week didn't solve New England's protection problems. He was still heavily pressured, while his receivers didn't create much yardage after the catch.

 Meanwhile, Raiders QB Kirk Cousins has a useful answer against this defense: play-action. New England is much tougher when quarterbacks simply drop back, but it has allowed the fifth-highest QBR against play-action this season. That fits what Cousins does best, giving Las Vegas a way to manufacture enough offense to create tension.

 
 

 

 New York Giants +3.5 (+150 moneyline) at Washington Commanders 

 Giants QB Jameis Winston showed against the Cardinals last week that he can find WR  Malik Nabers and produce touchdowns. That ability, combined with the Commanders' poor pass defense, is what makes this a live play  Sunday . Washington's blitz-happy approach only helps if it disrupts Winston before he finds those openings.

 Offensively, the Commanders will return QB  Jayden Daniels , but they've struggled to stay out of third-and-long. The Giants' secondary has limited passing yardage while creating interceptions this season (six, tied for the most in the NFL).

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Jaylen Warren , RB, Pittsburgh Steelers : 16 carries, 104 yards, 1 touchdown, 1 reception, 19 receiving yards 

 Warren has been getting a heavy workload this season, and there's no reason that shouldn't continue Sunday against the Colts . Indy ranks 30th in run stop win rate and 25th in opponent EPA per designed carry. It has surrendered 4.8 yards per carry (tied for fifth most), and that number holds steady against duo runs, which the Steelers run frequently (33% of the time).

 I do expect Warren's production will be more on the ground in this game than usual, however, because the Colts play a lot of man coverage, which usually discourages RB targets and receptions.

 
 

 Travon Walker , Edge, Jacksonville Jaguars : 1.5 sacks, 6 pressures, 23% pass rush win rate 

 Since Walker typically lines up opposite the opponent's right tackle, he will be the immediate beneficiary of Lane Johnson's retirement . In Johnson's stead last week against the Rams , rookie Markel Bell recorded a pass block win rate in the 19th percentile among tackles for the week. Quarterback  Jalen Hurts has taken sacks at an 8.8% clip this season, the fourth worst among qualified quarterbacks. And the Jaguars are strong favorites over the Eagles, which only increases the probability of a sack for Walker when Philly is in must-pass situations.

 
 

 Greg Dulcich , TE, Miami Dolphins : 5 receptions, 64 yards, 1 touchdown 

 Picking a tight end to have a big day against the Bengals is almost too easy, as they've allowed a league high in yards to opposing tight ends and a massive 2.7 yards per route run. The combination of Cincinnati's linebackers struggling in coverage and its cornerbacks playing well has funneled opponent production to tight ends.

 And this would qualify as a big day for Dulcich, who was shut out of the box score last week against the Vikings .

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Will Shipley , RB, Philadelphia Eagles (32.3% rostered) 

 Shipley is on the flex radar with  Saquon Barkley unlikely to play due to a hamstring injury and Tank Bigsby  on injured reserve after core muscle surgery. That should put Shipley in line to lead the Eagles' backfield. He had six carries for 23 yards after Bigsby exited last week, and Shipley was already being used on passing downs.

 The Jaguars have been tough against the run, so this is more about opportunity than matchup. Shipley should see enough volume to be deployed in lineups.

 

 
 

 Malik Washington , WR, Miami Dolphins (32.0%) 

 Washington has seen at least five targets in each game this season, including two with eight or more. His receiving yards have increased in each of the past three games, with 67 yards and 12.5 fantasy points against the Vikings last week.

 Washington has become the favorite target for new Dolphins QB Malik Willis , especially since rookie WR Caleb Douglas has missed the past two games with an ankle injury. Washington is on the flex radar against the Bengals this week .

 
 

 Jacoby Brissett , QB, Arizona Cardinals (31.5%) 

 Brissett has one of the best QB matchups of the week against the Lions , putting him firmly on the streaming radar. Detroit has allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks (32.7), including at least 21 fantasy points to every quarterback it has faced.

 Brissett threw three interceptions against the Giants last week , but he had only one through his first three games. He has also produced 818 passing yards, six passing touchdowns and a rushing score this season.

 

 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Amon-Ra St. Brown , WR, Detroit Lions 

 Take the matchup and the steady volume for Brown versus Arizona's defense. St. Brown has seen double-digit targets -- with at least one touchdown grab -- in three of four games. The Cardinals have given up 11 touchdown passes this season, which is tied for the most in the league.

 
 

 Quinshon Judkins , RB, Cleveland Browns 

 Judkins has seen at least 20 touches in each of his past two games, and he caught a season-high six passes in the Week 4 win over Pittsburgh . With that level of volume, in a Todd Monken offense that will lean on the downhill run game, I like Judkins to score against the Jets on Sunday . New York gave up three rushing scores to the Bears last week.

 
 

 Luther Burden III , WR, Chicago Bears 

 Burden has one touchdown on the season, but he has at least six targets in three straight games. He also had a rushing attempt in each of the past two games.  Against Green Bay , look for coach Ben Johnson to get Burden the ball on a schemed concept in the low red zone. What could that concept be? Most likely a screen or jet sweep.

 

 

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 The Broncos' offense will have its worst game of the season 

 Denver coach Sean Payton might be taking back the playcalling from Davis Webb this week , but the Chargers' defense has stiffened up over the past couple of weeks. They largely limited big plays and created takeaways against two of the league's most explosive offenses (Buffalo, Seattle). Now they get a Denver offense that's struggling less for playcalling and more for timid quarterback play. I wouldn't be surprised if some frustration boils over amid a nine-point outing.

 
 

 Raiders TE  Brock Bowers ' Offensive Player of the Year hype will begin 

 The Patriots might be down both starting cornerbacks against the Raiders, as neither Carlton Davis III nor Christian Gonzalez practiced Wednesday or Thursday. Against Bowers, who lines up primarily at receiver, a depleted cornerback room is a nightmare. He has been active for only two games but is already on pace…

title: Inside the NFL's wild endings and why coaches need to adapt
summary: Scoring too early and kicking the ball into the end zone can be costly, as the Cowboys learned.
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts appeared positioned for exactly the kind of finish that keeps NFL stadiums packed.

 Fourth quarter. Their ball. Down one point against the Houston Texans with 1:48 remaining. On the second play of what would be their final drive in Week 3, Colts quarterback Daniel Jones ripped a pass down the middle to receiver Laquon Treadwell for a 20-yard gain. Just like that, the Colts were cooking at the Houston 45-yard line.

 What happened next left some perplexed: The Colts began to display a sudden lack of urgency.

 They ran the ball on their next play. Next, they casually allowed the clock to tick down from 40 to 29 seconds before the following play -- that's when Houston, interestingly, called a timeout. Then, another run.

 Not until the Colts faced a third-and-6 did they make a more concerted effort to achieve a first down. Receiver Keenan Allen came up inches short after a 6-yard reception, so kicker Spencer Shrader came on and booted a 53-yard game-winning field goal with 21 seconds remaining.

 Why weren't the Colts more aggressive? And when did a 53-yard field goal become a slam dunk? The situation offered a prime example of how the traditional approach to late-game situations in the NFL has necessarily evolved at a time when more and more games are being decided late.

 In some instances, the "hurry-up" offense becomes more like "hurry up ... kinda."

 

 "That is real," Colts coach Shane Steichen said. "There's no doubt. When you have an opportunity to finish the game, you want it to be the last drive."

 Just ask the Dallas Cowboys , who can attest to it after losing a Week 3 game to the Baltimore Ravens on an inexplicable seven-second scoring drive.

 If it feels like there has been more last-minute scoring in the NFL lately, it's because there has been.

 Since the latest change to the NFL kickoff process last year, with the ball positioned at the 35-yard line after touchbacks, madness has ensued in the final moments of games. The number of drives starting in the final minute of halves culminating in a touchdown or field goal attempt skyrocketed by more than 50% relative to the 10 seasons before the changes.

 Meanwhile, the increasing strength and skill level of kickers, combined with underappreciated changes to rules governing how kicking balls -- known as K-balls -- may be manipulated by teams, has spurred a 60% increase in field goal attempts of 50 yards or longer in just five seasons. Many of those attempts are coming late in games and proving decisive.

 There were an NFL-record 12 field goal conversions of 60 yards or longer last season, including Jacksonville Jaguars kicker  Cam Little 's 68-yarder, the longest in NFL history.

 Subtle changes are translating into massive impacts on the game, and the trends seem unlikely to slow anytime soon.

 "Now you're seeing, I mean, chaos out there from some teams," Jaguars coach Liam Coen said. "And it's cool to watch."

 When a touchback can cost you the game 

 Of course, it's less cool if you're on the wrong side of the outcome.

 That brings us back to the Cowboys. There are a host of reasons they lost 34-31 to the Ravens on Sept. 27 in Rio de Janeiro, among them some curious coaching decisions and poor execution by players.

 

 But not to be overlooked was the role that today's kickoff rules played in the defeat. Had the Cowboys made the exact same miscues and been subject to the same circumstances just a few years ago, they likely would have held off Baltimore and pushed the game into overtime.

 One of the biggest variables in the loss was Dallas' decision to kick into the end zone after their tying field goal. With just seven seconds remaining, kicker Brandon Aubrey was instructed to aim for a touchback. But in the past three seasons, field position after touchbacks has been overhauled. After a 2024 change, teams were awarded the ball at the 30-yard line after touchbacks. (It was previously the 25-yard line.) A year later, in 2025, the rule was amended again, placing the ball at the 35.

 Ten yards of additional field position is priceless in an environment where kickers are capable of making field goals from near midfield.

 "There are so many yards at stake,"  Los Angeles Rams  coach Sean McVay said. "That's led to just so many more action plays in the kicking game in general. It's a big deal."

 Said Steichen: "You get the ball at the 35, and, shoot, someone hits an in-cut [route]. Next thing you know, they're at the plus-45 [yard line] and they kick a game-winning field goal."

 It's precisely what happened to Dallas, when quarterback Lamar Jackson hit receiver Zay Flowers for a 27-yard gain immediately after Dallas' kickoff. Baltimore called a timeout with one second remaining, allowing kicker Tyler Loop to convert a 56-yard field goal as time expired.

 Two-minute situations have been turned upside down by all of this.

 According to the Elias Sports Bureau, there were 49 game-winning drives that ended in the final two minutes of regulation in 2025, the most since 2000. Through four weeks of the 2026 season, there have already been 11 such drives. That puts this season on pace to match or exceed last year's total.

 "It used to be easy," said New York Giants coach John Harbaugh, who began coaching in the NFL when touchbacks translated to drive starts at the 20-yard line. "You kick a touchback and it's a gift. Good field position for your defense. They eliminated that because they want more returns, which I'm always for more."

 

 Adding to the issues is the complexity of today's dynamic kickoff process. Because the ball must land within the specified landing zone -- between the receiving team's goal line and the 20-yard line -- the possibility of a miss exists. When kickers are attempting to kick into the corners or hit kicks at specific angles to disadvantage kick returners, the odds of a miscue increase. The potential consequences are dire: The receiving team takes possession at its 40-yard line if a kick misses the landing zone or the ball goes out of bounds.

 The whole exercise is harder than it looks.

 "People don't get how hard it is for it to land just in the landing spot," San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Not a touchback, not short and not out of bounds. It's not as easy as people think.

 "You want to kick it high in there, but you're a little amped up and [could be] a touchback and that's a big miss because it's already at the 35 now."

 Why manipulating K-balls for the kicker could be huge 

 It's a part of the game few fans concern themselves with: the origins of the footballs used on game day.

 But it's actually a huge aspect of game prep for teams, both in terms of the balls used by quarterbacks and those set aside for kicks and punts. That's why a little-discussed rule change in 2025 has seemingly played an important role in today's frenzied final minutes of games.

 The NFL years ago standardized kicking balls, putting a stop to the over-manipulation of balls by teams looking to achieve better ball flight. The balls were presented to teams by the officiating crew, fresh out of the box, 60 minutes before kickoff. Equipment managers could address the balls using water, towels and brushes, but time was limited.

 But that rule was rescinded last year. Now, teams have the freedom to address the balls to their liking throughout the week, just as they have been doing on behalf of quarterbacks for years.

 Whether it has made a tangible difference is difficult to prove. But it's hard to imagine the explosion in long field goals since last season's rule change is coincidental. Three of the seven longest field goals in NFL history have come since the start of last season.

 

 And while the accuracy rates of kickers hasn't increased substantively, the increased willingness of teams to attempt long kicks is undeniable. According to ESPN Research, in 2020, there were 168 field goal attempts of 50 yards or longer. In 2025, there were…

title: NFL Week 5 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, betting odds, fantasy tips
summary: Bears vs. Packers? 49ers vs. Seahawks? There are 14 more games in Week 5, and we have picks, predictions and more for all of them.
full_text:
Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season is here. Can the Raiders get back on track against the Patriots after losing their first game of the season? Will the undefeated Vikings keep rolling against the Saints? Who has the edge in Bears-Packers? How will Eagles-Jaguars play out in another edition of London football? And what can we expect from the 49ers' visit to Seattle?

 We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, NFL analyst Ben Solak gives one reason to tune in to each game, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel, and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder all give us final score picks for every game.

 Let's get into the full Week 5 slate, which culminates with a "Monday Night Football" matchup between the Bills and Rams on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless otherwise noted, and all odds are via DraftKings.)

 
 Jump to a matchup: 
 PHI-JAX | CHI-GB | LV-NE 
 MIN-NO | CIN-MIA | IND-PIT 
 HOU-TEN | NYG-WSH | CLE-NYJ 
 DEN-LAC | SF-SEA | DET-ARI 
 BAL-ATL | BUF-LAR 

 Thursday: TB-DAL 
 Bye: KC , CAR 

 
 

 What ESPN Analytics says ... 
 

 

 
 

 Eagles (2-2) at Jaguars (3-1)  in London 
 9:30 a.m. ET | NFL Network | JAX -7.5 (41.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Eagles: Philadelphia entered the week with significant offensive problems. The Eagles have gone three-and-out on a league-high 15 possessions and rank 25th in points per game (18.8), 29th in total yards per game (269.8) and are tied for fourth in most sacks allowed (12). Things went from bad to worse with right tackle  Lane Johnson retiring and starting offensive lineman  Cam Jurgens being traded to Baltimore . "I think it's ironic because my thing when I came in as a rookie was, 'Don't dip your toe in the water, drown in it and learn how to swim.' We're drowning right now, and we're learning how to swim," left tackle  Jordan Mailata  said. -- Tim McManus 

 What we're hearing on the Jaguars: An under-the-radar reason for the Jaguars' offensive success over the first month is how good they've been on third down. They're converting 51.1% (ranked third), and they've been especially good in third-and-short (3 yards or less), converting 10 of 13 chances (76.9%, ranked third). "The biggest reason is staying ahead of the chains and being more consistent first and second down, less penalties, less negative runs, sacks, all those things play a part in it," QB Trevor Lawrence said. -- Michael DiRocco 

 Stat to know: The Eagles have allowed the second-lowest QBR on deep passes (20-plus air yards) this season. Opponents have completed 27% of deep passes for zero touchdowns and two interceptions against Philly. -- ESPN Research 

 Bold prediction: The Jaguars will win by two touchdowns. Philadelphia is 2-2 and ranks 27th in EPA per play on offense and 25th on defense. That is rough. And in three of those games, the Eagles had the now-retired Johnson, too. We can and should think about these teams dramatically differently now than when the season began (for the Jaguars, this is a good thing!). -- Walder 

 Why you should watch this game: You can play a game called "how many Eagles players do I recognize?" as they take the field without Johnson (retired), TE Dallas Goedert  ( knee ), WR DeVonta Smith  ( hamstring ) and RB Saquon Barkley  ( hamstring ) -- and now Jurgens is a Raven! If Willie Lampkin gets the start on the now sparse offensive line, as expected, he'll be the shortest Eagles offensive lineman (5-foot-11) to start in over 60 years. -- Solak 

 

 Injuries: Eagles | Jaguars 

 Fantasy nugget: Jaguars WR Parker Washington has scored at least 13 fantasy points in three of four games this season, so I wouldn't be too concerned about his 2.0-point Week 4 performance. He also had a 39-yard reception overturned. Washington is in a good spot to bounce back against a defense that has allowed the 10th-most fantasy points per game to WRs and has struggled against slot receivers. See Week 5 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: The Eagles are 7-0 ATS (against the spread) as underdogs since 2024. Jacksonville gives up plenty of passing yards, so QB Jalen Hurts can keep drives alive with quick throws and his legs. The Jaguars can win by leaning on the run, but Philadelphia still makes passing touchdowns tough to come by. That should help the Eagles hang around and cover the spread. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Jaguars 24, Eagles 19 
 Moody's pick: Jaguars 30, Eagles 23 
 Walder's pick: Jaguars 31, Eagles 14 
 FPI prediction: JAX, 73.4% (by an average of 6.5 points)

 

 Matchup must-reads: How will the Eagles move forward without Johnson? ... Why Jags play 26 of next 30 regular-season games away  ... Tracking Hunter's 2026 season 

 
 

 Bears (3-1) at Packers (2-2) 
 1 p.m. ET | Fox | CHI -1.5 (45.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Bears: Coach Ben Johnson announced Tyson Bagent as the starting QB early in the week. Getting reacquainted with the silent cadence is paramount for what is expected to be a hostile environment at Lambeau Field. Bagent is no stranger to rivalry games, having gone head-to-head with Shippensburg during his years at Division II Shepherd, but being the starter for Bears-Packers carries a different weight. "This is one of the greatest rivalries in all of sports," Bagent said. "It's easy for the fans to get up for, easy for us to get up for, so it will certainly be a different feel out there." -- Courtney Cronin 

 What we're hearing on the Packers: During TE Tucker Kraft 's rehab from last season's torn ACL, he said he saw no reason he couldn't return as the same player -- or even better. Through four games, he's tied for 15th among TEs in catches (15) and tied for 17th in receiving yards (148) with only one touchdown and has also battled the drops. "Statistically, it might not look like I'm playing better," Kraft said. "Some could even say that I might've lost my stinger. ... This week, try to get back to my roots, the kind of s--- I was on my first and second year when I was playing to the echo of the whistle and being hard on the defense." -- Rob Demovsky 

 Stat to know: The Packers' 22% pass block win rate is the worst by any team through the first four games of a season since ESPN began tracking in 2017. -- ESPN Research 

 

 Bold prediction: Bears edge Dayo Odeyingbo will stay hot and record a sack for a fourth straight game. Odeyingbo looks improved, with a 22% pass rush win rate at edge that's above average for the position. And we all know the Packers' offensive line is struggling mightily. -- Walder 

 Why you should watch this game: Do you remember the past two times the Bears and Packers played? Johnson and Packers coach Matt LaFleur had handshake drama . There's a rivalry reigniting ... and you're going to miss this game? -- Solak 

 Injuries: Bears | Packers 

 Fantasy nugget: Bears RBs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai could have big games. Green Bay ranks 25th in run stop win rate and has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to RBs. title: How wild-card game sent Bears, Packers in opposite directions
summary: Ever since Chicago sent Green Bay home, the Bears have taken flight and the Packers can't find their footing.
full_text:
Nearly nine months later, two things remain true about the Jan. 10, 2026, wild-card playoff game between the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field: It was an epic event on its own, but it also deeply affected the course of each franchise and the vibe around each team.

 While the Bears were eliminated from the playoffs a week later in an overtime loss to the Los Angeles Rams , confidence has gushed from Chicago ever since quarterback Caleb Williams capped an improbable comeback and a 25-point fourth-quarter barrage with the game-winning touchdown to DJ Moore to eliminate the Packers from the playoffs 31-27, thus ending their season on a five-game losing streak.

 That game, combined with another improbable comeback against the Packers less than a month earlier, validated everything that coach Ben Johnson preached when he got the job about his team's approach to their rivals from up North.

 From Johnson's comment during his introductory news conference -- when he said how much he enjoyed beating LaFleur twice a year when he was the Detroit Lions ' offensive coordinator -- to his "F--- the Packers" exclamation in the locker room after the playoff game, the Bears coach hasn't been shy about injecting himself into the rivalry.

 Everyone in the Bears' locker room after Sunday's 23-12 win over the New York Jets had to know what was coming from Johnson at some point during his postgame speech. He saved it for the end.

 "You guys know what next week is?" Johnson exclaimed.

 "You guys know what next week is?" he repeated for emphasis. "Enough said."

 

 Meanwhile in Green Bay, the blown 21-3 lead in the playoff game hung over coach Matt LaFleur -- and all the high-ranking decision-makers in the Packers organization for that matter -- like the sword of Damocles. Just like in ancient Greek story, the sword has seemingly followed them ever since, just waiting to drop.

 As much as Johnson has enjoyed poking the Packers since he got the job, LaFleur has taken a different approach, which he reiterated this week.

 "This game is about players, and so we'll keep it about the players," LaFleur said. "I'm not the one out there playing, so I think that's always been my mentality, and we're going to keep it about those guys.

  "And don't get me wrong, I love the rivalry. It's awesome. It's great. It's intense. You can feel it on game day. You can feel it throughout the course of the week, and also the significance. I mean, they're the defending North champions. So, what a great opportunity, great challenge for us in our home stadium to play against the defending champs."

 The two teams meet again Sunday at Lambeau Field ( 1:00 p.m. ET, Fox ) for the 214th time, playoffs included, in their storied histories. While only one game separates the Bears (3-1) and the Packers (2-2) in the NFC North standings, they look like organizations that have headed in opposite directions since the last meeting.

 At one point, LaFleur was 11-0 against the Bears. Now, Chicago has won three of the past four.

 This week, the Bears are road favorites against the Packers (-1.5, per DraftKings) for the first time since the 2006 season opener, and the Packers are home underdogs against anyone for the first time since Week 9 of the 2024 season against the Lions.

 

 Bears taking flight 

 Beating the Packers twice in three weeks at the end of the 2025 season did a lot to change the emotional DNA of the Bears' locker room.

 Flanked by his toddler son donning a cheese grater hat following Chicago's wild-card win, Moore tried to make sense of the shift that was taking place in this rivalry after catching his second winning touchdown in as many games against Green Bay 

 "To beat the Packers how we did and then just move on in the playoffs is amazing," Moore said on Jan. 10.

 And then just move on. 

 Moore's delivery was given in such a matter-of-fact way that the words seemed to describe an expectation of victory in a rivalry that had been so one-sided for years.

 That expectation created a carry-over effect for a team leaving its rebuild phase in the past as it transitioned into an aggressive contender expecting to repeat for the NFC North title in 2026.

 "Winning helps," Bears special teams ace Josh Blackwell said. "I think us winning and knowing what that feels like and carrying that momentum into the season helps. Whereas I feel like they ended on the loss and haven't found their footing this season."

 The makeup of the Bears is different now with Moore on the Buffalo Bills , but the edge Chicago gained by leveling the playing field with its heated rival remains within the walls of the locker room.

 It has been that way since the offseason began. Even those who weren't a part of last season's series understood what those wins did to catapult Chicago into a new class of the NFL.

 "I didn't really tune in too much about it because we were still in season ourselves," said defensive back Cam Lewis , who was with Buffalo during 2025. "Since I've been here in the spring, getting here it was just like, 'f--- the Packers.' This week now, we've been focused. Now let's tighten our focus even a little bit more. But it's just cool to be a part of something so historic. We just trying to go out there and get a win on Sunday, beat they ass and come back here."

 

 The Bears are seeking their first 4-1 start since the 2020 season and fourth win over the Packers since 2024. That would match their win total over the previous 15 seasons combined (2009-23), a 4-27 record against Green Bay which was the worst mark by any team against a division opponent during that span.

 As the Bears' trajectory has gone upward, so has the outside belief in this organization as evidenced by the Bears being favored at Lambeau Field for the first time in 20 years.

 And that's with a backup quarterback at the helm. Even after Williams went down with a hamstring injury in Week 2, Chicago hasn't lost its footing. The Bears lead the NFL with 1,716 yards of total offense, their most through four games in a season in franchise history, powered by the league's best run game and wins by both of their backup quarterbacks, Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent . 

 But the offense hasn't had to pull out wins on its own. The Bears have held opponents to fewer than 14 points in three straight games after allowing 37 during their opener at Carolina. Their 39 takeaways since the start of last season are the most in the NFL, including one in each of their past two meetings with Green Bay.

 That backs the belief internally for a team that enters Week 5 with the upper hand. 

 "We just want to beat them real bad and make them quit," wide receiver Luther Burden III .

 

 Packers can't get on track 

 The Packers have 15 players on their roster who weren't with the organization in any capacity for that playoff loss to the Bears.

 Shortly after one of those players arrived, he seemed confused when the subject of last season's collapse was brought up.

 "How did it end, again?" the player asked clearly oblivious to the weight the Packers had been carrying around for months.

 When reminded of the collapse against the Bears, the player's response was: "Oh yeah, that's right."

 If only the Packers had an entire roster of players who weren't affected by it. If only Lambeau Field was full of coaches and executives who didn't have the scars from the living through it.

 "When you end a season on a note like that, you spend a little more time looking at it," Packers quarterback Jordan Love said this week.

 As LaFleur put it in the immediate aftermath of the collapse, "A lot of bad things happened."

 Even in the wake of it all, LaFleur and general manager Brian Gutekunst both received contract extensions shortly after. But neither could shake questions about the way last season ended in collapse -- losing twice to the Bears and ending the season on a five-game losing streak. Just about every time LaFleur or Gutekunst took…

title: Can Burrow, Bengals establish identity vs. Dolphins?
summary: The Bengals put Burrow under center but ultimately went back to what the QB knows best. What's next?
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- When the Cincinnati Bengals needed to make something happen, quarterback Joe Burrow and the offense relied on what they knew best.

 Over the past several months, Cincinnati took a slew of reps with Burrow lined up under center, an indication that Cincinnati wanted to expand the menu of options available to the former MVP finalist.

 But ultimately, Burrow and Cincinnati went into shotgun.

 Through four games, the Bengals are still trying to figure out the best way to operate offensively. And it puts the mission for this Sunday's road game against the Miami Dolphins (0-4) squarely into focus as the Bengals try to find what parts of the offense fit.

 "We have to improve at them -- we can't just abandon them -- and find what our identity is going to be these last three quarters of the season," offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said Monday.

 What the Bengals are doing under center falls squarely into that category. Entering Sunday, Cincinnati is last in the NFL in yards per play while under center (3.3). And after an offseason of trying to put Burrow beneath center Ted Karras , the Bengals lead the NFL in shotgun usage (72.3%).

 

 Those numbers are heavily skewed because of what happened in the team's recent outing. The Bengals had 15 carries for just 23 yards. According to ESPN Research, that was Cincinnati's lowest total since the 2012 season.

 And with that not working, Cincinnati leaned on throwing the ball. Burrow had the fourth-most dropbacks in his career (58) and the Bengals were in shotgun formation on 85.5% of the team's snaps.

 After the 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday after 2-0 start, Burrow talked about throwing the ball even more when the run game is struggling.

 A few days later -- and after he had some time to cool off -- a more sensible approach prevailed.

 "We have to be more balanced going forward, and a big part of that is the run game," Burrow said.

 And Cincinnati's ever-confident and contact-embracing quarterback also espoused his belief that the team shouldn't abandon its vision of an offense that can operate effectively from under center.

 "We obviously have to be better at it," Burrow said. "We're still going to stick with it and keep getting reps invested in that. I think it's very valuable, so we have to be able to do it. But we need to be better."

 Getting better in one specific area is crucial. As Burrow explained, being able to use play-action passes from under center requires having a run game that defenses actually respect. Otherwise, a team's offensive linemen will be subjected to edge rushers who didn't buy the fake and are screaming toward the quarterback.

 

 "That's not a recipe for success," Burrow said.

 The Bengals have worked at trying to build a more explosive rushing attack. In the weeks leading up to the Jacksonville loss, Cincinnati coach Zac Taylor talked about the team being close to finding big runs that can make things easier on the offense.

 Against the Jaguars, one of the best run defenses in the league, that felt distant. This weekend should provide a better opportunity to find that offensive identity. The Dolphins are ranked 29th in the league in points allowed per drive.

 As for what defines a success under center attack, Taylor kept his answer simple.

 "Scoring points," he said.

 Added Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher: "It's our job as coaches to evaluate where we're at in any given moment -- in a season, in a game -- and make the decisions that we think are going to best lead us in the right direction."

title: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Stroud, Washington among top options
summary: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
full_text:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues. 

 Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in fewer than 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions. 

 The Week 5 NFL schedule features some really tough matchups for fantasy football, starting with the quarterback position. However, I still have four options -- in the QB2 range -- who have some upside. There are also a handful of wide receivers below, including deeper-league fliers you can take a chance on. As always, we'll hit on the running back and tight ends, and I have two available defenses to stream this week.

 

 Quarterbacks 

   Kirk Cousins , Las Vegas Raiders (33.3% rostered; at Patriots) 

 Cousins has scored 20 or more points in three straight games, and he has thrown two or more touchdown passes in all four games. Now, Cousins isn't going to provide any upside as a runner. We know that. But in Klint Kubiak 's offense, one that leans on tight end usage, Cousins can play on rhythm. And the Raiders are going to throw the ball in scoring position, as Cousins' eight red zone touchdown passes are tied for second most in the league. He's a superflex starter in the road matchup versus the Patriots.

   C.J. Stroud , Houston Texans (41.1% rostered; at Titans) 

 

 Stroud benefited from the return of wide receiver Nico Collins in Week 4, producing a season-high 23.08 points in a prime matchup versus Dallas. Collins had 118 yards receiving, plus he scored two touchdowns on end zone throws. It's a much tougher matchup this week versus the Titans, but Stroud is scoring 17.1 PPG, and Collins is the difference-maker in the Houston route tree. Stroud has value here as a QB2 in superflex formats.

   Jordan Love , Green Bay Packers (48.9% rostered; vs. Bears) 

 Love averages 16.2 fantasy PPG and has thrown two touchdown passes in all four games played. And due to a subpar rushing attack in Green Bay, Love is attempting 38.5 passes per game. Yes, the Bears defense ranks in the top 12 versus quarterbacks, but I do see positive perimeter matchups here for Packers wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . If you need a QB2 this week, Love does have some value.

   Deshaun Watson , Cleveland Browns (15.7% rostered; at Jets) 

 Watson (16.7 fantasy PPG) has scored 19 or more points in two of four games played, and he's averaging 31.8 rushing yards per game. The Jets defense ranks in the top five versus quarterbacks, so I don't love the matchup. However, if you need a QB2 with dual-threat upside Watson fits. We've seen the Browns take vertical shots in the pass game, so there is big-play potential for Watson.

 Wide receivers 

 

   Dohnte Meyers , Cincinnati Bengals (12.2% rostered; at Dolphins) 

 With Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) and Ja'Marr Chase (concussion protocol) both questionable for Sunday's game vs. Miami, managers can pivot to Meyers if either is unable to go. In the Week 4 loss to Jacksonville, Meyers scored 15.2 fantasy points, catching seven of nine targets for 82 yards. We saw the quicks and screens underneath, plus Meyers got loose on a deep over route for a 29-yard reception. He would be a WR3/flex option if one of the above stars is out, and he would have even more upside if both are inactive.

   Malik Washington , Miami Dolphins (33.4% rostered; vs. Bengals) 

 I really like the tape on Washington, along with his versatility in the Miami offense. Very similar to what we see with Deebo Samuel Sr . in San Francisco. Washington has scored 11 or more points in back-to-back games, and he's averaging seven targets per game (27% team target share). Plus, he's had at least two carries in two straight. I'd have him in the lineup as a WR3.

 

   Keenan Allen , Indianapolis Colts (38.5% rostered; at Steelers) 

 Allen (groin) missed the Week 4 win over the Commanders, but he is expected back for Sunday's game in Pittsburgh. In Week 3, Allen scored 18.3 points versus the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and a score. He can still uncover and work the dirty areas of the field, which is a fit for a Colts pass game lacking a vertical element with Alec Pierce (heel) on IR. You can play Allen as a WR3.

   Darius Cooper (6.0% rostered) and  Dontayvion Wicks , Philadelphia Eagles (47.6% rostered; at Jaguars) 

 It's a tough matchup here versus the Jags defense, but with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still out, both Cooper and Wicks are deeper-league fliers this week. Cooper saw seven targets in the Week 4 loss to the Rams, catching three passes for 33 yards and two touchdowns for 18.3 fantasy points, and Wicks has produced two games this season with 12 or more points.

   Malachi Fields , New York Giants (7.3% rostered; at Commanders) 

 Fields is a matchup play versus a Commanders defense ranking in the bottom five versus wide receivers. Fields, who scored a season-high 13.1 points in Week 4, is averaging only 3.8 targets per game, but he did catch a touchdown pass in the win over the Cardinals on a red zone throw. Fields also has the physical tools to win one-on-ones as a boundary option. He's a deeper-league flier.

   DeMario Douglas , New England Patriots (2.2% rostered; vs. Raiders) 

 With Mack Hollins (calf) expected to miss Sunday's game versus the Raiders, Douglas should see an expanded role in the Patriots' offense. Douglas' usage has been down this season (nine receptions on 17 targets for 82 yards), but he could be in a position to operate as the outlet out of the slot for Drake Maye  on Sunday.

 Running backs 

   Brian Robinson Jr ., Atlanta Falcons (44.2% rostered; vs. Ravens) 

 Robinson scored a season-high 25.7 points in the Falcons' blowout win over the Saints in Week 4, rushing for 62 yards and three touchdowns. As the No. 2 behind Bijan Robinson , Brian has seen 10 or more carries in three straight games, posting at least one rushing touchdown in two of them. Steady volume here in an offense averaging 181 rushing yards per game (second most). Brian is a deeper-league flex this week versus the Ravens.

 

   Keaton Mitchell , Los Angeles Chargers (23.5% rostered; vs. Broncos) 

 The winless Chargers moved to a three-man backfield committee in the Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, and it was Mitchell who paced the position with 15 touches, compared to Omarion Hampton 's 11 and Kimani Vidal 's seven. Mitchell rushed for only 39 yards on 10 carries, but he did catch five passes for 24 yards. Mitchell has scored 11 or more points in two straight, and he brings more receiving upside to the lineup.

   Will Shipley , Eagles (37.8% rostered; at Jaguars) 

 With both Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (IR) down this week, Shipley is in line to see a bump in volume. However, the Eagles' No. 3 running back hasn't had more than nine touches in a game this season, and Philly is also going through major transitions on the offensive line. Plus, Dameon Pierce could also factor into the run game. Shipley should be viewed as a deeper-league option only in this matchup with Jacksonville.

   MarShawn Lloyd , RB, Packers (46.9% rostered; vs. Bears) 

 Lloyd should split touches with Kaleb Johnson this week, as Chris Brooks is dealing with an ankle injury. Lloyd's lack of rushing efficiency (2.7 YPC) remains an issue, but he does provide some value as a pass catcher. He caught five balls for 36 yards in the Week 4 win over Tampa Bay, and he has at least two receptions in three straight games, adding a touchdown grab back in Week 2.

title: Do the Broncos have a reliable No. 1 running back? Sorting Denver's backfield
summary: The Broncos' running game has been stuck in neutral, as J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie have struggled in the early going.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Through four games, the Denver Broncos ' search for Mr. Right in the run game is still in progress. Or the quest for the right combination of Mr. Rights. Or the journey to discover any run game. But this isn't a new problem.

 Let's go back to Jan. 27, two days after the Broncos lost the AFC Championship Game to the New England Patriots . In his season-ending news conference, Broncos coach Sean Payton said: "When we want to run it under center and control a game, we've been able to do it a few times, but not as much as I'd like."

 Fast forward almost nine months later. After a 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers dropped the Broncos to 2-2, a visibly frustrated Payton said: "I think at half we were at 30-some (rushing) yards, that's something that has to get better."

 The Broncos will enter their Week 5 matchup against the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday in SoFi Stadium ( 4:05 p.m. ET, CBS ) with a murky at best rotation in the backfield. That has resulted in Denver having the 29th-ranked rushing attack in the league at 81.3 rushing yards per game. At 40.3 rushing yards per game, J.K. Dobbins is the only Broncos back among the league's top 65 rushers and is below 12 quarterbacks. So, Denver hasn't been able to find that reliable back it can depend on.

 

 "Overall, just the consistency and our approach -- whether it's in the shotgun or under center -- that will continue to be a focal point for us," Payton said earlier this week. "It's always in these details."

 The struggles boiled over against San Francisco, as a frustrated Dobbins exchanged words with running backs coach Lou Ayeni on the sideline during a game in which he finished with 11 carries for 40 rushing yards. Denver running backs ended up with 20 carries for 72 rushing yards (3.6 yards per carry).

 The Broncos' backfield was set back early when fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman suffered an ankle injury in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars and placed on injured reserve . He'll be eligible to return as soon as the Broncos' Week 7 game against the Arizona Cardinals but showed flashes of being a complement to Dobbins prior to the injury. His decisive running nature stood out, and he led the team with 39 yards on 10 carries and a second-half touchdown in the comeback victory over the Jaguars.

 That leaves Dobbins, who leads the team in carries (46) and rushing yards (161) in a current rotation with second-year man RJ Harvey (12 carries, 49 yards) and Tyler Badie (four carries, 10 yards). That group hasn't meshed smoothly. Only once has a Broncos running back had more than 11 carries in a game -- Dobbins had 17 carries for 49 yards in a Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Rams .

 Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb has cited a lack of assertiveness on carries -- especially from running backs not named Coleman -- as a reason why the backfield hasn't gotten on track.

 "I think we have to run with a little more conviction, for sure," Webb said. "When they can see a hole, run through it, full speed ahead. And I think our runners do that, I just think there's been some times where that can be a little bit better and I anticipate that getting better."

 Leaving yards on the field has been a problem. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, all three running backs currently on the active roster have a negative average rushing yards over expected, a metric which measures how many yards a ballcarrier gains in comparison to how well a play is blocked.

 Dobbins ranks 52nd in the NFL with minus-0.6 yards over expected per carry, and his 3.5 yards per carry is well below the 5.0 he averaged last season (153 carries for 772 yards) before getting hurt in Week 10. Harvey averages minus-0.8 yards over expected per carry, with Badie at minus-1.8 in a very small sample size. Even Coleman, at 0.1 yards over expected per carry, has essentially gotten the yardage that is blocked.

 

 By comparison, the Kansas City Chiefs ' Kenneth Walker III leads the league at 2.5 yards over expected (minimum 10 carries), with the Atlanta Falcons ' Bijan Robinson in second at 1.95 yards over expected.

 The Broncos' inability to run the ball has bled into the passing game, too. With the running backs not providing oomph on the ground, defenses have been content to sit back with two safeties deep in coverage to prevent downfield strikes in the passing game, relying on their front seven to contain the run.

 That's been successful at both levels, as the Broncos' passing game is 29th in air yards per attempt (5.9) and 20th in pass plays of 20 or more yards. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix knows how important it is to get the running backs going to make his job easier.

 "I think overall when you get 2-high zone you just want to run the football," Nix said. "And so we just got to find ways to continue to do that."

 But who will take the reins and be that consistent backfield running threat? Is it as simple as waiting for Coleman to return from injury? Payton has promised to "look at everything" to get the run game going, and facing the Chargers' 22nd-ranked run defense might help a bit.

 It's a mixed bag between Sunday and Denver's Week 10 bye, as the Broncos will face the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (No. 11 in rushing defense), the Cardinals (No. 20), Chiefs (No. 5) and Carolina Panthers (No. 32) in Weeks 6-9.

 "It's not one thing," Payton said. " ... It's still that work in progress, with the runners, all of it, the coaches, what we're doing. We'll get there."

title: Texans, Titans face off desperately seeking first win after 0-4 starts
summary: Tennessee coach Robert Saleh and Houston coach DeMeco Ryans put friendship aside in battle of winless teams.
full_text:
For the second consecutive year, the Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans will face off in desperate need of their first win of the season.

 Last season was a matchup between two 0-3 teams, only for this year to be even more dire with both sitting at 0-4 for their meeting in Nashville, Tennessee, on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ).

 Houston won last year's matchup 23-0 en route to a 12-5 record and a trip to the divisional round of the playoffs. Meanwhile, the Titans finished 3-14 for the second straight season and earned the No. 4 pick in the draft.

 The Titans currently have a 10-game losing streak to AFC South opponents and are tied for the current longest regular-season losing streak at six games, and Houston, a team that came in with Super Bowl aspirations and were considered favorites to win the AFC South, needs to defy the odds (only one team -- the 1992 Chargers -- have made the playoffs after starting 0-4) to make the postseason for a fourth straight season.

 

 "Anything's achievable." Titans coach Robert Saleh said Wednesday, "You get on a run and you start getting -- like momentum and confidence is such a big deal and a very, very underrated thing in the NFL. I just feel like if we can just get one, it'll snowball and who knows what will happen. But it's never over until that little 'E' shows up on the standings ... or whatever signifies that you've been eliminated. You just keep on fighting and even when you are eliminated, it still doesn't matter. You still got to show up and do your best."

 For now, both are looking up at the Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) and Indianapolis Colts (2-2) in the division through four weeks.

 "One of the things we talk about is owning the South," Saleh said. "Owning it is not just a one-time thing. We want to own it for as long as we're here and this is our first crack at a division opponent."

 The Texans already fell to the Colts in Week 3 in the only interdivisional game amongst AFC South teams in the first four weeks, so they already sit at the bottom of the division in that regard as well.

 But if Houston were to get its first win of the season, Ryans would not only be denying one of his closest friends from getting his first win this season, he'd also be denying him from getting his first win as the head coach of the Titans.

 "Saleh means a lot to me and when it comes to coaching and why I'm coaching," Ryans said. "He's going to have his guys fired up, ready to play. We're in the same position. I know he's bringing his best, we have to bring our best. It's always going to be a great matchup. He knows what we do. We have to know what he does defensively. May the best man win."

 

 Titans looking to change directions 

 At this point, it looks like desperation is peaking for the Titans. Saleh said the team has to learn how not to lose before it can learn how to win. He pointed to turnovers, penalties and missed assignments as weekly examples of how the team puts itself behind the 8-ball.

 The Titans have lost the past three games by a combined total of 17 points. Late mistakes have contributed to the Titans losing their past two games -- like a blown coverage that allowed the Philadelphia Eagles to score a last-minute game-winning touchdown in Week 2 and a backbreaking interception thrown by Cam Ward in the end zone on what would have been the go-ahead drive with seconds left against the New York Giants .

 The first win would mean a lot to Saleh, but Houston is where he broke into the NFL as a defensive intern in 2005. He's not the only Titan that has a connection, as Titans controlling owner Amy Adams-Strunk, whose father Bud Adams founded the Houston Oilers in 1960 and moved the team to Tennessee, proudly sported an Oilers belt buckle as she gave a tearful speech after then-coach Brian Callahan's 32-27 Week 12 win over the Texans in 2024.

 That's the last time the Titans beat Houston after losing three straight, but Saleh said he doesn't feel pressure from Adams-Strunk to win just because it's the Texans.

 "I don't remember if she even talked about this one," Saleh said. "Like all of us, she's looking forward to finding a win, but I don't think anyone in this organization puts one game over the other. I recognize and acknowledge the history, but that was a lot of generations ago. If you're talking to the players that are on the football field, it's a rivalry because it's a division opponent, and we're trying to get a win."

 Having grown up in the Houston area, Ward knows the significance of the rivalry. But like everyone else, he's simply seeking his first win regardless of the opponent.

 "Every division game is a rivalry," Ward said. "We're both 0-4 teams. We're both searching for a win this year. It could really ... get us going in the right direction."

 

 Texans look to spark change 

 Houston is searching for a way to heat things up after a cold start, and the next step toward that was coach DeMeco Ryans taking over the defensive playcalling duties .

 After boasting one of the top defenses last season, the unit is one of the biggest reasons Houston is winless. The defense ranks 26th in points allowed per game (27.3), 20th in yards allowed per game (343.8) and has given up game-winning drives late in the fourth quarter in three of the first four games.

 "Right now, we haven't done great the first four games defensively when it's been on guys to close the game out," Ryans said Wednesday. "It's just, 'Can we spark a little change?' [Defensive coordinator] Matt Burke has done a good job. We're not overhauling the defense, just trying to spark some change."

 

 In contrast, Stroud, who's betting on himself after opting to  not sign a contract extension prior to the start of the season, has done his part. He's sixth in passing yards (1,141) and sixth in explosive rate (20%) on his dropbacks, per Next Gen Stats. He has also led three potential game-winning drives in the fourth quarter.

 Stroud came into the season under heavy criticism following his recent playoff run highlighted by a four-interception performance in the divisional round. But even after his promising start, he's focused on helping the team.

 "It's all about winning," Stroud said. "So, looking at myself in the mirror, what else can I do to be better, to make us better on third down, keep us on the field, to control the game maybe a little."

 Despite being 5-1 against the Titans since Stroud and defensive end Will Anderson Jr . were drafted with back-to-back picks in the first round of the 2023 draft, they aren't looking past their opponent.

 "This is going to be a battle," Anderson said. "There are two teams facing each other that haven't won a game yet this year. For us, we're going to have to go in this game with the intensity that we have to get a win."
